   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020 Made 11th November 2020 Coming into force in accordance with article 2 At the Court at Windsor Castle, the 11th day of November 2020 Present, The Queen's Most Excellent Majesty in Council», the United Kingdom's emissions trading scheme order, as it stands with later amendments, including the 2026 extension to ships. Its jurisdiction is the United Kingdom: «This Order extends to the whole of the United Kingdom.» What the Order requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Order sets a cap-and-trade system for greenhouse gas: «This Order establishes a trading scheme, known as the “UK Emissions Trading Scheme” or “UK ETS”.» Its purpose: «The purpose of the UK ETS is to limit, or encourage the limitation of, the emission of greenhouse gases». The explanatory note says what it covers: «This Order establishes a new emissions trading scheme covering greenhouse gas emissions from power and heat generation, energy intensive industries and aviation.» It replaces the EU system in the UK: «It is the successor, in the UK, to the EU Emissions Trading System (established by Directive 2003/87/EC )» The unit traded: «An allowance is an allowance to emit 1 tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent.» The first scheme year: «scheme year ” means the calendar year beginning on 1st January 2021 or any of the 9 subsequent calendar years» The Order enters into force as the text states: «Except as provided by paragraph (2), this Order comes into force on the day after the day on which it is made.»

The scheme now reaches ships. The revised text records: «Sch. 2A inserted (1.7.2026) by The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) (Extension to Maritime Activities) Order 2026 (S.I. 2026/392)». Its first line reads: «The UK ETS applies to maritime activities as set out in this Schedule.»

*Analytical inference:* aviation and, from the 2026 extension, maritime activities are the parts of the scheme closest to freight. The duty to hold and hand back allowances falls on the aircraft operator or maritime operator, not on a forwarder, and the Order states no pass-through of that cost to a customer.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COST ALERT: from 1.7.2026 the Order puts the cost of handing back allowances for maritime emissions on maritime operators, as it already does for aircraft operators, and that cost is in force. The Order states no pass-through of it to customers, so whether carriers add it to rates is a gap. No step falls on a freight operator that is not an aircraft operator or maritime operator within the next 30 days. The first maritime allowance handback has a later date: «on or before 30th April 2028 in relation to maritime emissions in the 2026 scheme year», and for later years «(b) in relation to maritime emissions in any other scheme year, on or before 30th April in the following year.»

- A carrier-relations lead asks each aircraft operator and each maritime operator in the business's rate agreements, at the next rate review, whether an allowance cost under the scheme is added to the rate and how it is calculated.
- A pricing lead records, per quote that includes a United Kingdom sea leg or a flight from a United Kingdom aerodrome, which operator is the maritime operator or aircraft operator and whether the rate includes an allowance charge.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the operator duties above; the Order requires neither of a forwarder. A missed handback carries a penalty: «The excess emissions penalty is £100 multiplied by the inflation factor for each allowance that the operator [ F237 , the aircraft operator, or the maritime operator ] fails to surrender.» *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any scheme cost can be charged by a maritime operator or aircraft operator to a forwarder or its client under the business's contracts.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Order names the operator of an installation, the aircraft operator, the maritime operator, the regulator and the UK ETS authority. The maritime operator is defined as «a person is a maritime operator in relation to a scheme year, where in respect of that year that person— (a) performs a maritime activity in a ship; and (b) in respect of that ship is— (i) unless sub-paragraph (2) applies, its registered owner; or (ii) where sub-paragraph (2) applies, its ISM company.». For aircraft: «A person who is an aircraft operator in relation to a scheme year must surrender, on or before 30th April in the following year, an amount of allowances equal to its aviation emissions in that scheme year (expressed in tonnes).». An ISM company's duties are set out: «An ISM company that has assumed responsibility for obligations imposed by or under this Order in accordance with paragraph 3(2)(b), must notify the regulator in writing where there is a change to its written agreement with the registered owner of a ship that affects its responsibility for compliance with those obligations.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. They meet the scheme through the registered owner, ISM company or aircraft operator that carries their cargo. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party is the maritime operator for a ship a client books, and whether the contract allows a charge.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Order.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets dated steps, some already passed. The scheme is reviewed: «The review dates are 31st December 2023 and 31st December 2028.» The 2023 review date has passed and 2028 is ahead. Offshore ships are outside the maritime Schedule only for a time: «(l) up to and including 31st December 2026, an offshore ship.» The regulator moves installation permits at set dates, for example «The regulator must convert the greenhouse gas emissions permit into a hospital or small emitter permit with effect from 1st January 2026» (that date has passed), and «the operator must apply for a greenhouse gas emissions permit and comply with the conditions of the permit from 1st January 2027». Allocation tables: «(a) the allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(a) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2027; and (b) the updated allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(b) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* the review at the end of 2028 is the point where the scheme's reach and rules may change, and offshore ships fall into the maritime Schedule after the stated date. The installation steps concern industrial sites, not carriers. The text states no content for the review beyond its report.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a ship is inside the maritime part is its size: «This Schedule applies to a ship of a gross tonnage of 5000 or more calculated in accordance with the tonnage determination regulations contained in Annex I to the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, adopted by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) in London on 23rd June 1969, except— (a) a ship in the armed services of the United Kingdom or another country (including a naval auxiliary ship);». The scheme counts only United Kingdom voyages: «A “ voyage ” means any movement of a ship that— (a) commences at the last berth at a port of call within the United Kingdom’s jurisdiction; (b) ends at the first berth at that port of call or another port of call within the United Kingdom’s jurisdiction; (c) does not arrive at a port of call outside the United Kingdom’s jurisdiction; and (d) is not an excluded activity.». Time in port is covered too: «An “in-port activity” consists of the following but does not include an excluded activity— (a) movements of a ship within a port of call within the United Kingdom’s jurisdiction that do not form part of a voyage; and (b) a ship being at berth at a port of call within the United Kingdom’s jurisdiction.». A port of call is defined by cargo or passengers: «the expression “ port of call ” means any port that a ship arrives or is present at and at which— (a) passengers or crew embark, or disembark, that ship; or (b) cargo is loaded onto, or unloaded from, that ship.». For aviation: «An aviation activity consists of any of the following activities other than excluded flights— (a) a flight departing from an aerodrome situated in the United Kingdom and arriving in an aerodrome situated— (i) in the United Kingdom; (ii) in an EEA State; (iii) in Gibraltar;».

*Analytical inference:* the scheme covers movements between United Kingdom ports and flights from United Kingdom aerodromes to the places listed, not an ocean voyage that leaves United Kingdom jurisdiction; movements within a United Kingdom port and time at berth there are also covered. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular sea leg or flight on a client's route is inside these definitions.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Maritime scope. «This Schedule applies to a ship of a gross tonnage of 5000 or more».

Maritime reporting and handback. «Each maritime operator must monitor its maritime emissions in accordance with— (a) the requirements of Part 4; (b) the emissions monitoring plan issued to the person under paragraph 10.» «The annual emissions report and the verification report must be submitted to the regulator by the maritime operator on or before 31st March in the year following the scheme year to which it relates.» «A person who is a maritime operator in relation to a scheme year must surrender an amount of allowances equal to— (a) 50% of its maritime emissions arising in that scheme year (expressed in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent) from voyages— (i) starting at a port of call in Northern Ireland and ending at a port of call in Great Britain; (ii) starting at a port of call in Great Britain and ending at a port of call in Northern Ireland; (b) 100% of maritime emissions arising in that scheme year (expressed in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent) from any other maritime activity.»

Aircraft operators. «must be submitted to the regulator on or before 31st March in the year following the scheme year to which it relates». «A person who is an aircraft operator in relation to a scheme year must surrender, on or before 30th April in the following year, an amount of allowances equal to its aviation emissions in that scheme year (expressed in tonnes).» «An aircraft operator must comply with the requirement in paragraph (1) before the end of the period of 42 days commencing with the day it becomes an aircraft operator.»

Allowances. «An allowance is an allowance to emit 1 tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent.»

Penalty. «the operator of an installation [ F235 , an aircraft operator, or a maritime operator ] is liable to the civil penalty (the “excess emissions penalty”)». «The excess emissions penalty is £100 multiplied by the inflation factor for each allowance that the operator [ F237 , the aircraft operator, or the maritime operator ] fails to surrender.» Article 51, which concerns installation permit conditions only and not aircraft or maritime operators, sets a separate penalty: «The civil penalty is— (a) £20,000; and (b) a daily penalty at a daily rate of £500 for each day that the operator fails to comply with the condition or requirement».

*Analytical inference:* each duty above falls on the operator that holds the allowance; the Order states no cost to a customer of that operator. No phase-in is stated in Articles 33, 34 and 52.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these operator duties creates a charge or liability for a forwarder or its client.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 11.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Order sets scheme rules for operators, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Accounts are held in the registry: «(iv) aircraft operator holding accounts (see paragraph 13); [ F370 (iva) maritime operator holding accounts (see paragraph 13A);». An aircraft operator submits its monitoring plan quickly: «An aircraft operator must comply with the requirement in paragraph (1) before the end of the period of 42 days commencing with the day it becomes an aircraft operator.». Maritime operators have their report checked: «The annual emissions report must be verified as satisfactory in accordance with the requirements of Part 8.»

*Analytical inference:* these registration and report duties fall on the operators; the text states none on a forwarder.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COST ALERT: the Order puts the system work on operators. For ships: «A maritime operator must carry out their obligations relating to monitoring and reporting of maritime emissions under this Order in accordance with the following principles— (a) a maritime operator must determine emissions using the appropriate monitoring methodology set out in Part 4;»; «monitoring and reporting must be complete and cover all maritime emissions». Small aircraft operators are excused from verification of the report, not from reporting: «does not apply, and the aviation emissions stated in the report are considered to be verified, where the person required to prepare the report in relation to a scheme year»; the excuse needs that the person «determined its emissions using the small emitters tool approved under Commission Regulation (EU) No 606/2010, the tool having been populated with data by Eurocontrol». The size limits: «less than 25,000 tonnes from full-scope flights; or (ii) less than 3,000 tonnes from aviation activity».

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder that moves cargo on a ship or aircraft within these definitions sees the effect as an operator's allowance cost and reporting, not as a system to build; the text states no data request to forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client or operator may ask a forwarder for voyage or flight data.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some flights and ships are outside the scheme. Flights: «(f) humanitarian flights; (g) emergency medical service flights;» and «(m) flights performed by aircraft with a certified maximum take-off mass of less than 5,700 kilograms.» The Order defines humanitarian flights as «“ humanitarian flights ” means flights operated exclusively for humanitarian purposes which carry relief personnel and relief supplies such as food, clothing, shelter, medical and other items during or after an emergency or disaster». Ships: «(k) a ship that operates a Scottish ferry service;».

*Analytical inference:* a flight carrying relief supplies for an emergency may fall in the humanitarian exclusion only if it is operated exclusively for that purpose. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular relief flight meets that definition.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no adjacent industry research or alternative is held for this Order.*

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 11th November 2020: Order made
- 1st January 2021: first scheme year, the calendar year beginning on 1st January 2021 (in force)
- 1st January 2026: regulator changes for some aircraft operators and some permit conversions (date passed)
- 1.7.2026: maritime Schedule 2A inserted into the Order (in force)
- 31st December 2026: offshore ships stay outside the maritime Schedule up to and including this date
- 1st January 2027: allocation table for the later allocation period published before this date; ultra-small emitter status exit permit duty starts
- 1st January 2028: updated allocation table published before this date
- 30th April 2028: first maritime allowance handback, for 2026 emissions
- 31st December 2028: review date of the scheme

## 15. Sources

- The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Order 2020, UK Statutory Instruments 2020 No. 1265, legislation.gov.uk: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/1265

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2904, an act of the European Commission that changes the rules for the Union Registry, the register in which emission allowances for the EU emissions trading systems are held. Its jurisdiction is the European Union. Title: «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2023/2904 of 25 October 2023 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/1122 supplementing Directive 2003/87/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the functioning of the Union Registry» Dated: «Done at Brussels, 25 October 2023.»

The Regulation addresses account holders, national administrators and the central administrator and does not name freight forwarders, shippers or customs brokers. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. The captured text states no review date.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation updates how allowances are held and tracked so that shipping companies, aircraft operators and the road and buildings fuel system fit into the same register. Base rule: «lays down general, operational and maintenance requirements concerning the Union Registry provided for in Directive 2003/87/EC and applies to allowances created for the purposes of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)» Shipping: «Directive 2003/87/EC has been amended to include as of 2024 emissions from maritime transport in the EU ETS. Shipping companies will thus be subject to a requirement to surrender emission allowances corresponding to a certain share of its greenhouse gas emissions, which will gradually increase until 2026» Road and buildings fuel: «Directive 2003/87/EC has also been amended to include as of 2027 a separate but parallel emissions trading system to be applied to fuels used for combustion in the buildings and road transport sectors as well as in additional sectors of industrial activities not covered by Annex I to that Directive»

Start dates: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» «Article 1, points (21), (22), (25) and (28)(c), shall apply from 1 January 2025» «Article 1, point (30)(b), shall apply from 1 January 2027.» Reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Who it touches: shipping companies, aircraft operators, stationary installations and regulated entities, and the national administrators who open their accounts. The text names no freight service.

*Analytical inference:* because shipping companies and aircraft operators are the account holders, a freight operator meets this Regulation through the carriers it books and the carbon costs they carry, not through a duty of its own.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Regulation falls to a freight operator within thirty days of the date of this document; the dates ahead are 1 January 2027 and the first June of 2028. Three steps a freight desk can start now:

- A carrier-relations lead adds the Union Registry public compliance symbol and statement for each ocean carrier and airline to the carrier review file, and checks it after the date on which it is updated each year.
- A pricing lead asks each ocean carrier before the next rate round whether its emissions charge covers methane and nitrous oxide, which count in verified emissions of shipping companies from 2026, and asks for the charge basis in writing.
- A contracts lead adds 1 January 2027 to road fuel surcharge clauses as the date from which regulated entity allowances are transferred from the EU Regulated Entity Auction Account for auctioning, and the first June of 2028 as the first date for regulated entity compliance status.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: shipping companies, aircraft operators, stationary installations, regulated entities, national administrators, the central administrator, Member States and the Commission. «“operators” means stationary installations, aircraft operators, shipping companies and regulated entities» «“surrender” means the accounting of an allowance by an stationary installation, an aircraft operator, a shipping company or a regulated entity against the verified emissions of its installation, aircraft, or ship or against fuel released for consumption»

The Regulation names no forwarder, shipper or customs broker, and does not say whether a freight business is a shipping company, aircraft operator or regulated entity.

*Analytical inference:* the surrender duty runs to the account holders named above, so a freight business is affected where a carrier or fuel supplier that holds an account carries its allowance cost into a charge, which the text does not say.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that owns, charters or operates a ship or an aircraft, or that releases fuel for consumption, is a shipping company, aircraft operator or regulated entity under Directive 2003/87/EC, which this text does not decide.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Regulation changes registry rules and binds account holders and administrators. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Scope: «applies to allowances created for the purposes of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)» Shipping compliance status: «For the period from 2024 to 2030, derogations pursuant to Article 12(3-e) to 12(3-b) of Directive 2003/87/EC shall be taken into account in the calculation of the compliance status for shipping companies» «From 2026, the verified emissions of shipping companies shall also include methane and nitrous oxide.» Aviation: «The central administrator shall ensure that the Union Registry transfers aviation allowances, and from 1 January 2025 general allowances, automatically from the EU Aviation Allocation Account to the relevant open aircraft operator holding account with compliance status A» «Each aircraft operator shall have no more than one aircraft operator holding account.» Member State accounts: «Where a Member State notifies the Commission of the application of the exemption in accordance with Article 30e(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC and the Commission does not raise an objection to the application of that derogation, the Member State concerned shall, by an official letter, request the central administrator to open a tax derogation deletion account in the Union Registry»

What this changes: the register calculates and shows compliance status for shipping companies, aircraft operators and, later, regulated entities. Effect by cargo vertical: not stated.

The Regulation states no pass-through of allowance costs to carrier surcharges or freight charges.

*Analytical inference:* the shipping and aviation rules set what counts as verified emissions and how allowances reach accounts, which determines the allowance cost a carrier faces; the text states no link from that cost to a freight rate.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which account holders and which emissions a given carrier's compliance status covers, since the status is calculated per account and not per freight service.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Document date:** 2026-11-01

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2023/2631 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 November 2023 on European Green Bonds and on optional disclosures for bonds marketed as environmentally sustainable and for sustainability-linked bonds. It is a European Union regulation, so it applies in the Union.

How to read it: statements of what the regulation says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation creates a voluntary EU label for green bonds and a supervision system for the reviewers who check them. In its own words it «lays down uniform requirements for issuers of bonds who wish to use the designation ‘European Green Bond’ or ‘EuGB’ for their bonds that are made available to investors in the Union». It also sets up a register of external reviewers and provides optional disclosure templates for other sustainability bonds. The label is protected: «The designation ‘European Green Bond’ or ‘EuGB’ shall be used only for bonds that comply with the requirements set out in this Title.» «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Why it reaches freight: the Union's stated reason for the label includes transport. «Environmentally sustainable bonds are one of the main instruments for financing investment related to environmentally sustainable technologies, energy and resource efficiency as well as environmentally sustainable transport infrastructure and research infrastructure.» For a freight operator the practical link is financing and customers. A transport business that issues a bond under the label has to show where the money goes; an operator whose own bond or whose client's bond uses the label may be asked for evidence about the assets the proceeds paid for. The regulation sets no rate, charge or surcharge on freight.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted recital names environmentally sustainable transport infrastructure as one use of such bonds, and the quoted article limits the label to bonds that comply, so a freight business is touched when it issues such a bond, when it supplies evidence to an issuer, or when it invests in one; the regulation does not say that any freight service is rated.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this regulation falls due for a freight operator within 30 days. The Commission's report on sustainability-linked bonds is due by 21 December 2026 and creates no duty for an operator; the two steps below follow from the label and from that report.

- A finance lead, before deciding to issue a bond that will carry the designation 'European Green Bond', lists the planned use of proceeds against the allocation categories in section 8 and asks an external reviewer registered with ESMA to confirm the factsheet, because the factsheet needs a positive pre-issuance review before issue.
- A finance lead who holds or plans a sustainability-linked bond reads the Commission's report due by 21 December 2026 when it is published and checks whether the legislative proposal it may carry changes the terms of that bond.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation names these parties. The issuer: «‘issuer’ means an entity that issues bonds» The external reviewer, which is registered with the European Securities and Markets Authority: «External reviewers for European Green Bonds shall, before taking up their activities, be registered with ESMA.» It also names national competent authorities, ESMA, the Commission, sovereign issuers and the investors to whom bonds are made available.

The regulation names no freight forwarder, carrier, shipper or customs broker. A freight operator therefore sits in the chain only as an issuer, as a business that supplies asset evidence to an issuer, or as an investor. *Analytical inference:* the quoted definition covers any entity that issues bonds, so a transport company that issues a green bond is an issuer under it; the text does not say what a supplier owes an issuer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the freight operator, or a client of the operator, is an issuer under the quoted definition for a given bond, and which of the issuer duties in section 8 then apply.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The regulation sets reviews and publications that will change the analysis. Dates are quoted from the text; the first three below fall before the date of this document and are stated as past because the captured text does not say whether each was delivered.

- Optional disclosure templates (date passed): «By 21 December 2024, the Commission shall publish guidelines establishing templates for voluntary pre-issuance disclosures for issuers of bonds marketed as environmentally sustainable and of sustainability-linked bonds.» The templates are for bonds marketed as environmentally sustainable and for sustainability-linked bonds.
- Technical standards for external reviewers (date passed): «ESMA shall submit those draft regulatory technical standards to the Commission by 21 December 2025.» ESMA's draft standards set what the reviewer rules in the regulation mean in practice.
- Taxonomy review report (first date passed, then every three years): «The Commission shall, by 31 December 2024 and every three years thereafter, publish a report to inform issuers of European Green Bonds about the review conducted pursuant to Article 19(5), third subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) 2020/852»
- Full review (next date ahead): «By 21 December 2028 and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall, after consulting ESMA and the Platform on Sustainable Finance established by Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2020/852, submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the application of this Regulation.»
- Possible further report: «By 21 December 2029, the Commission may, based on the report referred to in paragraph 5, submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council.»

What changes when these arrive: the template guidelines set what an issuer of a bond marketed as environmentally sustainable can disclose; the review report from the Commission feeds any change to the rules in section 8, including the seven-year window for amended criteria; the 2028 review looks at uptake of the label and the supervision of external reviewers. *Analytical inference:* a freight operator that issues or buys such bonds would see terms change only if a review leads to a legislative proposal, which the quoted articles allow but do not promise.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Duties fall on issuers that use the label and on external reviewers. The ones that matter to an issuer in transport are below. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether and how each duty applies to a given bond and issuer is a question for counsel and is not settled here.

**Use of proceeds.** «Before the maturity of a European Green Bond, the proceeds of such a bond shall be allocated in full, in accordance with the taxonomy requirements, to one or more of the following categories (the ‘gradual approach’): (a) fixed assets that are not financial assets;» The text lists further categories of assets and expenditure after that one. A limited flexibility exists: «issuers may allocate up to 15 % of the proceeds of a European Green Bond to economic activities that comply with the taxonomy requirements, with the exception of the technical screening criteria» The recital says why it is limited: «Such flexibility should be appropriately limited in size and scope in order to maintain a very high level of ambition for European Green Bonds.»

**Moving criteria.** «where technical screening criteria are amended after the issuance of the bond, the following proceeds be allocated in alignment with the amended technical screening criteria no later than seven years after the date of application of the amended criteria» *Analytical inference:* the quoted rule rests on criteria that change after issue, so an issuer's allocation can need to be re-checked against the amended criteria within the quoted period.

**Factsheet and review before issue.** «Prior to issuing a European Green Bond, issuers shall: (a) complete the European Green Bond factsheet set out in Annex I; (b) ensure that the completed European Green Bond factsheet has been subject to a pre-issuance review with a positive opinion by an external reviewer.»

**Annual allocation report.** «For every 12-month period until the date of full allocation of the proceeds of their European Green Bond and, where applicable, until the completion of the CapEx plan, issuers of European Green Bonds shall draw up a European Green Bond allocation report using the template set out in Annex II» «Issuers of European Green Bonds shall ensure that the annual allocation reports and, where applicable, any post-issuance review required by this Article are made public within 270 days of the end of every 12-month period referred to in paragraph 1. Within that period of 270 days, issuers shall ensure that the external reviewer has at least 90 days to review an allocation report.» A review is not required in one case: «no change in allocation was made to the portfolio of assets and no asset in the portfolio was changed or was itself subject to a change in allocation»

**Impact report.** «Issuers of European Green Bonds shall, after the full allocation of the proceeds and at least once during the lifetime of those bonds, draw up and make public a European Green Bond impact report on the environmental impact of the use of the bond proceeds, using the template set out in Annex III.»

**Penalties on issuers and reviewers.** National authorities hold the power to fine issuers; the text sets a floor for the maximum fine: «(e) in the case of a legal person, maximum administrative fines of at least EUR 500 000, or, in the Member States whose currency is not the euro, the corresponding value in the national currency on 20 December 2023, or 0,5 % of the total annual turnover of that legal person according to the most recent available financial statements approved by the management body» The authorities can also bar issuance: «an order prohibiting the natural or legal person responsible from issuing European Green Bonds for a period not exceeding one year» ESMA fines external reviewers: «the minimum amount of the fine referred to in paragraph 1 shall be EUR 20 000. The maximum amount shall be EUR 200 000.»

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Issuers publish their documents: «Issuers of European Green Bonds shall publish on their websites and make available, free of charge and in accordance with Article 21(3) and (4) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, until at least 12 months have elapsed after the maturity of those bonds, the following» The list that follows in the text includes the factsheet, the pre-issuance review, the allocation reports and the impact report. External reviewers register with ESMA (section 4). Member States have their own reporting step to the Commission and ESMA: «By 21 December 2024, Member States shall notify to the Commission and to ESMA, in detail, the rules referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.» That date has passed and the captured text does not say whether each Member State met it.

*Analytical inference:* the publication duty rests on the quoted sentence and sits with the issuer; a freight operator that is not an issuer files nothing under this regulation. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any registration or publication duty falls on a freight operator in its own right; the captured text names none.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the captured text sets no system for a freight operator to build unless it issues a bond under the label. An operator that does issue one needs an asset and spend record that can feed the allocation report in section 8, which uses the template in the regulation's annex.

- A finance lead at an operator that plans a European Green Bond, before the factsheet goes to the reviewer, assigns one owner to keep a ledger that ties each use of proceeds to an asset category from section 8, so that each annual allocation report can be drawn up from it.

*Analytical inference:* the ledger step rests on the quoted allocation-report duty in section 8; the regulation does not itself prescribe a ledger.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Three carve-outs sit in the text. State auditors: «State auditors shall not be subject to Titles IV and V of this Regulation.» Public issuers have a wider use of proceeds: «a sovereign or a third-country issuer which is a State, a member of a federation in the case of a federal State, or a regional or municipal entity, may also allocate the proceeds of European Green Bonds it has issued to tax relief, subsidies, intermediate consumption, current transfers within a general government, current international cooperation or other types of public expenditure» Reviewers had a transition period that ran to 21 June 2026 and has passed: «After 21 June 2026 the external reviewers referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall provide services in accordance with this Regulation only after registering in accordance with Article 23»

*Analytical inference:* none of the three is a route for a transport company; they rest on the quoted sentences, which name state auditors, sovereign and public issuers, and reviewers already operating.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 22 November 2023: the regulation is adopted: «Done at Strasbourg, 22 November 2023.»
- Twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»
- 20 December 2023: «Articles 68, 69 and 70 shall apply from 20 December 2023»
- 21 December 2024: the regulation applies: «This Regulation shall apply from 21 December 2024.» The Member State notification in section 10 and the Commission guidelines in section 6 carry the same date.
- 21 December 2025 (passed): ESMA's second set of draft technical standards in section 6 fell due; the captured text does not say whether it was delivered.
- 21 June 2026: «Article 40, Article 42(1) to (8) and Article 43 shall apply from 21 June 2026.» The transition for external reviewers in section 12 ended on this date (passed): from then reviewers may serve only once registered.
- 21 December 2026: «By 21 December 2026, the Commission shall publish a report on the need to regulate sustainability-linked bonds, accompanied by a legislative proposal, where appropriate.»
- 21 December 2028: the Commission's full review in section 6 is due.
- 21 December 2029: the possible further report in section 6.

What each date changes: the 2023 dates start the early provisions on delegated acts and transitions; the 2024 date makes the regulation apply to issuers; the June 2026 date moves reviewers from notification to registration; the December 2026 date brings the Commission's report on sustainability-linked bonds, which may carry a proposal; the 2028 and 2029 dates bring reviews that can lead to proposals.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/1488, an act of the European Commission that updates the list of harmonised standards for electrical equipment, including electric vehicle charging cables. Its jurisdiction is the European Union. Title: «COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2025/1488 of 22 July 2025 amending Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2723 as regards harmonised standards for flat flexible cables and charging cables for electric vehicles» Dated: «Done at Brussels, 22 July 2025.»

The Decision addresses standards references and does not name freight forwarders, carriers or shippers. The captured text states no review date.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Decision keeps the EU list of harmonised standards for electrical equipment up to date. A harmonised standard matters because of this rule: «electrical equipment which is in conformity with harmonised standards or parts thereof, the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union , is to be presumed to be in conformity with the safety objectives referred to in Article 3 of that Directive» What changed: «Cenelec revised the harmonised standard EN 50214:2006 as corrected by EN 50214:2006/AC:2007 on flat polyvinyl chloride sheathed flexible cables, the references of which are published in the Official Journal of the European Union by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2723 ( 3 ) . This resulted in the adoption of harmonised standard EN 50214:2024.» «Cenelec amended harmonised standard EN 50620:2017 as amended by EN 50620:2017/A1:2019 on charging cables for electric vehicles. This resulted in the adoption of the amending harmonised standard EN 50620:2017/A2:2024.» What it does: «Article 1 Annex I to Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/2723 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Decision»

Start dates: «This Decision shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» «Point (1) of the Annex shall apply from 23 January 2027.»

Who it touches: the manufacturers of flat flexible cables and electric vehicle charging cables and of equipment covered by the old standards. The text names no transport mode, route or freight service.

*Analytical inference:* because the Decision changes which standard editions carry the presumption of conformity, a freight business that moves these cables meets it through the conformity papers its customer holds, not through a duty of its own.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Decision falls to a freight operator within thirty days of the date of this document; the date that matters is 23 January 2027, when rows 31 and 107 of the list are deleted. Two steps a freight desk can start now:

- A compliance lead asks each customer that ships electric vehicle charging cables or flat flexible cables which edition of the standard its product papers cite (EN 50214:2006 or EN 50214:2024; EN 50620:2017 with A1:2019 alone, or with A1:2019 and A2:2024), and records the answer on the customer file before 23 January 2027.
- A sales lead tells those customers that from 23 January 2027 the list row for EN 50214:2006 and the row for EN 50620:2017 as amended by A1:2019 alone are deleted, replaced by EN 50214:2024 and by EN 50620:2017 with A1:2019 and A2:2024, and asks for updated product papers with the next quote.

The text names these parties: manufacturers, the Commission, and the standards bodies CEN, Cenelec and ETSI. «In order to give manufacturers sufficient time to adapt their electrical equipment» «the Commission made a request to the European Committee for Standardisation (CEN), the European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardisation (Cenelec) and the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI)»

The Decision names no forwarder, carrier, importer or shipper and states no rule on what a freight business records for these cables.

*Analytical inference:* the presumption of conformity runs to the equipment, so a freight business is affected where a customer's cable moves with product papers that cite an edition whose list row is deleted.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Document date:** 2026-11-01

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2019/631 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019, which sets CO 2 emission performance standards for new passenger cars and for new light commercial vehicles (vans) in the European Union, and repeals the two earlier regulations that covered cars and vans separately. It applies in the Union.

The captured text is the regulation as adopted on 17 April 2019 and carries no later amendment; changes made after that date, if any, are not covered here, and the statements below read the act as captured.

How to read it: statements of what the regulation says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation caps the average CO 2 emissions of the new cars and vans a vehicle maker sells in the Union. In its own words it «This Regulation establishes CO 2 emissions performance requirements for new passenger cars and for new light commercial vehicles in order to contribute to achieving the Union's target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions». The first caps: «From 1 January 2020, this Regulation sets an EU fleet-wide target of 95 g CO 2 /km for the average emissions of new passenger cars and an EU fleet-wide target of 147 g CO 2 /km for the average emissions of new light commercial vehicles registered in the Union». «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Where it applies: «This Regulation shall apply to the following motor vehicles: (a) category M 1 as defined in Annex II to Directive 2007/46/EC (‘passenger cars’)which are registered in the Union for the first time and which have not previously been registered outside the Union (‘new passenger cars’)» Light commercial vehicles are covered by the second limb, quoted in section 7.

Why it matters to a freight operator: the van fleets that deliver freight, parcels and last-mile loads are bought from the makers this regulation limits. The duty falls on the vehicle manufacturer, not on the operator that buys or runs the van; the regulation sets no price, surcharge or lease term for the buyer. Its effect reaches an operator through what the makers offer for sale, because the later targets in section 8 tighten the average a maker may sell.

*Analytical inference:* because the quoted targets are fleet averages for a maker's new registrations, a maker cannot meet them by one vehicle alone, so the mix of van types on offer to an operator can shift as the quoted 2025 and 2030 steps arrive; the regulation does not say how a change in the mix reaches vehicle prices, and no pass-through to price is stated.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this regulation falls due for a freight operator within 30 days, and the regulation sets duties on manufacturers, not on operators. The steps below use the dates that shape what vans are offered.

- A fleet-procurement lead, at the next light commercial vehicle tender, asks each manufacturer for the type-approved CO 2 value and the vehicle category of every offered model, because those values are what the maker's fleet average is built from (section 8).
- A fleet-planning lead, before the next multi-year van renewal plan is approved, sets the quoted 1 January 2030 targets for vans beside the planned purchase dates, and notes which purchases fall before and after that date.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation puts its duty on manufacturers. «The manufacturer shall ensure that its average specific emissions of CO 2 do not exceed the following specific emissions targets» Manufacturers may share the burden: «Manufacturers, other than manufacturers which have been granted a derogation under Article 10, may form a pool for the purposes of meeting their obligations under Article 4.» A pool names a contact: «the manufacturer nominated as the pool manager who will be the contact point for the pool and will be responsible for paying any excess emissions premium imposed on the pool in accordance with Article 8»

It also names the Commission, Member States, derogated niche manufacturers, designated importers and connected undertakings. The regulation names no freight operator, fleet owner or leasing company, and no freight forwarder. *Analytical inference:* the quoted duty rests on the maker's average specific emissions, so an operator that buys or runs vans has no duty of its own under the quoted sentence. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an operator that registers or imports vehicles for the first time in the Union in its own name could be treated as a manufacturer or designated importer under the quoted wording.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The regulation sets reviews and assessments that will change the analysis. Dates are quoted from the text. The ones before the date of this document are stated as past; the captured text does not say what each found.

- Review of the regulation (date passed): «The Commission shall, in 2023, thoroughly review the effectiveness of this Regulation and submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council with the result of the review.» The report may carry a proposal, including «the introduction of binding emissions reduction targets for 2035 and 2040 onwards for passenger cars and light commercial vehicles».
- Assessment of real-world emissions data (date passed): «the Commission shall, no later than 1 June 2023, assess how fuel and energy consumption data may be used to ensure that the vehicle CO 2 emissions and fuel or energy consumption values determined pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 715/2007 remain representative of real-world emissions over time for each manufacturer»
- Review of the consumer information directive (date passed): «By 31 December 2020, the Commission shall review Directive 1999/94/EC considering the need to provide consumers with accurate, robust and comparable information on the fuel consumption, CO 2 emissions and air pollutant emissions of new passenger cars placed on the market»
- Mechanism to adjust emissions as of 2030 (assessment date ahead): «The Commission shall monitor and report annually on how the gap referred to in the first subparagraph evolves over the period 2021 to 2026 and shall, with the view to preventing an increase in that gap, assess, in 2027, the feasibility of a mechanism to adjust the manufacturer's average specific emissions of CO 2 as of 2030, and, if appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to put such a mechanism in place.»
- Fund for the automotive transition (date ahead): «The Commission shall, if appropriate, make a legislative proposal to that effect by 2027 at the latest.»

What changes when these arrive: a revision of the 2030 targets or new 2035 and 2040 targets would change what vans are offered after 2030 (section 8); the 2027 assessment can lead to a mechanism that adjusts a maker's average from 2030. *Analytical inference:* the 2027 assessment rests on the quoted real-world emissions gap, so the captured text states a possible mechanism and not an adopted one.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: what counts as a light commercial vehicle? The regulation defines it by category and mass: «(b) category N 1 as defined in Annex II to Directive 2007/46/EC with a reference mass not exceeding 2 610 kg, and vehicles of category N 1 to which type-approval is extended in accordance with Article 2(2) of Regulation (EC) No 715/2007 (‘light commercial vehicles’), which are registered in the Union for the first time and which have not previously been registered outside the Union (‘new light commercial vehicles’)» A heavier zero-emission van can still count, as section 8 quotes.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted definition turns on the reference mass of 2 610 kg, so a van above that mass is outside it unless the zero-emission clause applies. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given van model is in category N 1 under the quoted definition, which depends on its type-approval and is not in the captured text.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The duties below are the manufacturer's. They shape the vans an operator can buy. *Legal Confirmation Required:* how each target applies to a given maker, and whether any step reaches an operator, is a question for counsel and is not settled here.

**Fleet-wide targets from 2025.** «From 1 January 2025, the following EU fleet-wide targets shall apply: (a) for the average emissions of the new passenger car fleet, an EU fleet-wide target equal to a 15 % reduction of the target in 2021determined in accordance with point 6.1.1 of Part A of Annex I; (b) for the average emissions of the new light commercial vehicles fleet, an EU fleet-wide target equal to a 15 % reduction of the target in 2021 determined in accordance with point 6.1.1 of Part B of Annex I.»

**Fleet-wide targets from 2030.** «From 1 January 2030, the following EU fleet-wide targets shall apply: (a) for the average emissions of the new passenger car fleet, an EU fleet-wide target equal to a 37,5 % reduction of the target in 2021 determined in accordance with point 6.1.2 of Part A of Annex I; (b) for the average emissions of the new light commercial vehicles fleet, an EU fleet- wide target equal to a 31 % reduction of the target in 2021 determined in accordance with point 6.1.2 of Part B of Annex I.»

**Share of zero- and low-emission vehicles.** «From 1 January 2025, a zero- and low-emission vehicles' benchmark equal to a 15 % share of the respective fleets of new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles shall apply in accordance with points 6.3 of Parts A and B of Annex I, respectively.» For 2030: «From 1 January 2030, the following zero- and low-emission vehicles' benchmarks shall apply in accordance with points 6.3 of Parts A and B of Annex I, respectively: (a) a benchmark equal to a 35 % share of the fleet of new passenger cars; and (b) a benchmark equal to a 30 % share of the fleet of new light commercial vehicles.»

**Heavier zero-emission vans.** «In the case of zero-emission vehicles of category N with a reference mass exceeding 2 610 kg or 2 840 kg, as the case may be, they shall, from 1 January 2025, for the purposes of this Regulation and without prejudice to Directive 2007/46/EC and Regulation (EC) No 715/2007, be counted as light commercial vehicles falling within the scope of this Regulation if the excess reference mass is due only to the mass of the energy storage system.»

**Each maker's own target.** «for each calendar year, starting from 2025, the specific emissions targets determined in accordance with point 6.3 of Part A or B of Annex I, or, where a manufacturer is granted a derogation under Article 10, in accordance with that derogation»

**Phase-in of the first year.** The percentage of cars taken into account rises: «the following percentages of each manufacturer's new passenger cars registered in the relevant year shall be taken into account: — 95 % in 2020, — 100 % from 2021 onwards.»

**Super-credits for low-emission cars.** «each new passenger car with specific emissions of CO 2 of less than 50 g CO 2 /km shall be counted as: — 2 passenger cars in 2020, — 1,67 passenger cars in 2021, — 1,33 passenger cars in 2022, — 1 passenger car from 2023, for the year in which it is registered in the period from 2020 to 2022, subject to a cap of 7,5 g CO 2 /km over that period for each manufacturer» *Analytical inference:* the quoted credit is for passenger cars and the captured text states none for vans.

**Penalty.** «In respect of each calendar year, the Commission shall impose an excess emissions premium on a manufacturer or pool manager, as appropriate, where a manufacturer's average specific emissions of CO 2 exceed its specific emissions target.» «The excess emissions premium under paragraph 1 shall be calculated using the following formula: (Excess emissions × EUR 95) × number of newly registered vehicles.» The captured text states no other sanction in the passages read.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reporting runs from Member States to the Commission, then to makers. Member States report once a year: «By 28 February of each year, each Member State shall determine and transmit to the Commission the information listed in Parts A of Annexes II and III in respect of the preceding calendar year.» The Commission publishes: «By 31 October of each year, the Commission shall publish, by means of implementing acts, a list indicating:» For real-world data the Commission collects, «starting from 1 January 2021, the Commission shall ensure that the following parameters relating to real-world CO 2 emissions and fuel or energy consumption of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles are made available at regular intervals to it, from manufacturers, national authorities or through direct data transfer from vehicles, as the case may be».

*Analytical inference:* the quoted reporting sentences name Member States, the Commission and manufacturers, and no sentence assigns a filing to an operator that buys or runs vans. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any filing falls on an operator that registers vehicles itself; the captured text names none.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the captured text sets no system for a freight operator to build.

- A fleet-data lead, at the next vehicle onboarding, records the category and reference mass of each van in the fleet register, because the 2 610 kg limit in section 7 decides whether a van is a light commercial vehicle under the regulation.

*Analytical inference:* the step rests on the quoted definition in section 7; the captured text does not require an operator to keep such a record.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The regulation carves out vehicles and makers. Special vehicles: «This Regulation shall not apply to special purpose vehicles as defined in point 5 of Part A of Annex II to Directive 2007/46/EC.» Small makers: the regulation says it «shall not apply to a manufacturer which, together with all of its connected undertakings, is responsible for fewer than 1 000 new passenger cars or for fewer than 1 000 new light commercial vehicles registered in the Union in the previous calendar year, unless that manufacturer applies for and is granted a derogation in accordance with Article 10». Niche makers can apply for a different target: «An application for a derogation from the specific emissions target calculated in accordance with Annex I may be made by a manufacturer of fewer than 10 000 new passenger cars or 22 000 new light commercial vehicles registered in the Union per calendar year»

*Analytical inference:* the carve-outs rest on the maker's volume and on the vehicle type, so they change which makers the targets reach and do not change what an operator is asked to do.

- 15 May 2019: the power to adopt delegated acts «shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of six years from 15 May 2019».
- 1 January 2020: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 January 2020.» «Regulations (EC) No 443/2009 and (EU) No 510/2011 are repealed with effect from 1 January 2020.»
- 31 October 2020: the first mass value adjustment; the adjusted value applies from 1 January 2022 until 31 December 2024: «(a) by 31 October 2020, the M 0 value in point 4 of Part A of Annex I shall be adjusted to the average mass in running order of all new passenger cars registered in 2017, 2018, and 2019. That new M 0 value shall apply from 1 January 2022 until 31 December 2024;»
- 31 December 2020: review of the consumer information directive (section 6).
- 1 January 2021: the real-world data collection starts (section 10) and all new cars are counted in full (section 8).
- 31 October 2022: «(b) by 31 October 2022, the M 0 value in point 4 of Part B of Annex I shall be adjusted to the average mass in running order of all new light commercial vehicles registered in 2019, 2020 and 2021. That new M 0 value shall apply in 2024; (c) by 31 October 2022, the indicative TM 0 value for 2025 shall be determined as the respective average test mass of all new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles registered in 2021;»
- 2023: a super-credited car counts as one car (section 8); the text gives the year only.
- 1 June 2023: assessment of real-world emissions data (section 6).
- 31 October 2024: «(d) by 31 October 2024, and every second year thereafter, the TM 0 value in point 6.2 of Parts A and B of Annex I shall be adjusted to the respective average test mass of all new passenger cars and new light commercial vehicles registered in the preceding two calendar years, starting with 2022 and 2023.»
- 1 January 2025: the 2025 fleet-wide targets and the 15 % benchmark start (section 8).
- 1 January 2027: read here as the first day of 2027, because the text gives only the year; it is the latest year for the possible proposal on the automotive transition fund, and the year of the assessment of an adjustment mechanism (section 6).
- 1 January 2030: the 2030 targets and benchmarks start (section 8).

What each date changes: the application date starts the 95 g and 147 g targets; the mass adjustments change the reference values in each maker's formula; the 2025 and 2030 dates tighten the average a maker may sell; the 2027 assessment can lead to a proposal that changes how a maker's average is adjusted from 2030.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Commission Delegated Decision (EU) 2025/934, an act of the European Commission that updates the European Union list of waste for batteries. Its jurisdiction is the European Union. Title: «COMMISSION DELEGATED DECISION (EU) 2025/934 of 5 March 2025 amending Decision 2000/532/EC as regards an update of the list of waste in relation to battery-related waste» Dated: «Done at Brussels, 5 March 2025.»

The Decision addresses waste codes and does not name freight forwarders, carriers or shippers. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. The captured text states no review date.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Decision rewrites the part of the waste list that covers batteries and the waste from making and recycling them. Why: «it is necessary to update the list of waste set out in Decision 2000/532/EC to take into account new battery chemistries and battery-related waste management, the evolving battery market and to improve the identification and classification of relevant waste streams as well as to support improved sorting, recycling and reporting of battery-related waste» «New battery chemistries, in particular as regards lithium-based, sodium-based and nickel-based batteries, have emerged during the past years» What it does: «Article 1 The Annex to Decision 2000/532/EC is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Decision» Issuer: «THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union»

Start dates: «shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» «It shall apply from 9 November 2026.» Reason for the wait: «In order to allow operators and authorities to adequately implement the new and modified waste codes, in particular for waste classified or re-classified as hazardous, and to make the necessary structural and operational changes in facilities managing battery-related waste, as well as to allow for the adaptation, submission and processing of waste permits, the application of this Decision should be deferred»

Who it touches: operators of facilities that manage battery-related waste, authorities that issue waste permits, and anyone who identifies or classifies battery waste. The text names no transport mode, route or freight service.

*Analytical inference:* because the codes name waste streams and the text defers application for facilities and permits, a freight business that moves waste batteries or battery production and recycling residues meets the Decision through the code its customer puts on the waste, not through a duty written for freight.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

ACTION REQUIRED: the new battery waste codes apply from 9 November 2026, which is days after the date of this document. Three steps a freight desk can start now:

- A compliance lead lists every customer and lane that moves waste batteries or battery production and recycling residues, with the waste code each now uses, and marks which of the three deleted codes (20 01 33*, 20 01 34, 19 02 11*) appear.
- A systems lead removes those three deleted codes from the code picklist and adds the new entries, including 20 01 43* for waste lithium-based batteries, before 9 November 2026.
- A customer-service lead asks each waste-battery customer to confirm the new code on its next booking after 9 November 2026 and records the confirmed code on the booking.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: operators and authorities, and facilities that manage battery-related waste. «operators and authorities to adequately implement the new and modified waste codes»

The Decision names no forwarder, carrier or shipper and states no rule on how waste codes are recorded in transport.

*Analytical inference:* the text addresses waste codes used by operators and authorities, so a freight business is affected where a customer's waste code, which the customer and its permit set, changes on the stated date.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that carries or arranges carriage of waste batteries must record the new code, and in what document, under the waste and transport rules that apply to it; this text does not say.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: which code does a given battery waste take? The Decision creates separate codes for different battery chemistries and for municipal collection. «a new hazardous waste code for lithium-based batteries, which covers separately collected fractions of municipal waste, should be introduced» The entries for batteries from municipal collection read: «20 01 42* waste batteries included in 16 06 01 to 16 06 04, 16 06 08 to 16 06 11 or 16 06 14 and mixed waste batteries containing those waste batteries including also 16 06 07» «20 01 43* waste lithium-based batteries included in 16 06 07» «20 01 44 waste batteries other than those mentioned in 20 01 42 and 20 01 43»

*Analytical inference:* the entries refer back to the chemistry entries in the 16 06 group, so the code of a waste battery depends on its chemistry and on whether it was separately collected from municipal waste.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which entry applies to a customer's waste batteries of mixed or unknown chemistry, which this text leaves to the classification rules cited in it.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Decision changes the list rather than setting duties on named parties; the amendments below bind whoever applies the list. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Main changes. «Chapter 16 06 is replaced by the following» «16 06 07 * waste lithium-based batteries» «16 06 13* mixed waste batteries» «16 06 24 * lithium-based battery manufacturing waste containing hazardous substances (for example cathode cut-offs, cathode slurry, off specification battery cells, modules and/or packs)» Recycling residues: «10 08 21 * slags from waste lithium-based battery recycling containing hazardous substances» «19 02 12 * solid salts and solutions containing heavy metals from battery recycling» «19 14 intermediate fractions from the thermal and/or mechanical treatment of waste batteries and of battery manufacturing waste» Other: «entry 09 01 11* is replaced by the following» «The classification of alkaline batteries should be adapted to technical and scientific progress by taking into account the concentration of relevant substances in batteries and their hazardous classification»

What this changes: each battery chemistry and each production or recycling residue has its own entry, and many entries carry an asterisk. *Analytical inference:* the asterisk on the new entry for lithium-based batteries from municipal collection matches the recital's statement that a new hazardous code is introduced for it, so the asterisk marks a hazardous entry. Effect by cargo vertical: not stated.

The Decision states no cost, fee or transport rule linked to the new waste codes, and no effect on a freight charge.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether each new asterisk entry brings a hazardous waste duty in the Member State where a customer's waste is produced or moved, which this text does not say.

No phase-in is stated in Article 2.
No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 and 2.
No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 and 2.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Council Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/1629, an act of the Council of the European Union that lets France tax electricity supplied to vessels at berth at a reduced rate. Its jurisdiction is France under European Union law. Title: «COUNCIL IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2020/1629 of 29 October 2020 authorising France to apply a reduced rate of taxation to electricity directly provided to vessels at berth in a port, in accordance with Article 19 of Directive 2003/96/EC» Dated: «Done at Brussels, 29 October 2020.»

The Decision addresses France and does not name freight forwarders, carriers or shippers. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. The captured text states no review date.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Decision lets one Member State cut the tax on shore-side electricity, the power a ship takes from the quay instead of running its own engines. What it permits: «France is authorised to apply a reduced rate of taxation to electricity directly supplied to vessels, other than private pleasure craft, at berth in a port (‘shore-side electricity’), provided that the minimum levels of taxation referred to in Article 10 of Directive 2003/96/EC are respected» Purpose: «France aims to further promote the deployment and the use of shore-side electricity» «The use of such electricity is considered to be an environmentally less harmful way of satisfying the electricity needs of vessels at berth in a port than the burning of bunker fuels by those vessels» Addressee: «This Decision is addressed to the French Republic.»

Dates: «This Decision shall apply from 1 January 2021 until 31 December 2026.» «This Decision shall apply from 1 January 2021» The captured text does not say when the Decision enters into force; the date it applies from is the one stated.

Cost context for a reader: the Council noted that «on-board generation of electricity will remain the more competitive alternative in most cases»

*Analytical inference:* the authorisation is a tax permission to France, not a duty on vessel operators, so a freight operator meets it through the electricity cost a carrier or port charges for vessels at berth in France, which the Decision does not state.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the French authorisation ends on 31 December 2026, or earlier if the Council adopts general provisions on shore-side electricity. Three steps a freight desk can start now:

- A pricing lead for services calling at French ports asks each carrier or vessel operator whether its shore-side electricity cost assumes the reduced tax rate and what it will assume after 31 December 2026, before the next rate review.
- A contracts lead adds 31 December 2026 as a review date to any clause or surcharge for French ports that assumes a reduced electricity tax on shore-side electricity.
- A sustainability lead tells customers who ask for shore-side electricity at French ports that the Council recorded on-board generation as the more competitive alternative in most cases, so the reduced rate is not a reason on its own to switch.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: France, which sought the authorisation, the Council and the Commission, and relevant economic operators. «France sought authorisation to apply a reduced rate of taxation to electricity directly provided to maritime and inland waterway vessels at berth in a port» «not to discourage relevant economic operators from making the necessary investments»

The Decision names no forwarder, carrier or shipper, and states neither the reduced rate nor who pays the tax on the electricity.

*Analytical inference:* the tax permission is granted to France for electricity supplied to vessels at berth, so whoever pays the electricity tax in a French port, a port operator, a supplier or a vessel operator, decides who feels the reduced rate; the text does not say who that is.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that is charged for shore-side electricity, directly or through a carrier surcharge, receives the reduced rate under French tax law, which this text does not state.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Decision names one event that can end it early. «should the Council, acting on the basis of Article 113 or any other relevant provision of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, adopt any general provisions on tax advantages for shore-side electricity, this Decision shall cease to apply on the day on which those general provisions become applicable» It also names its own end date: «This Decision shall apply from 1 January 2021 until 31 December 2026.» The Decision states no renewal or successor authorisation after 31 December 2026.

*Analytical inference:* a clause or surcharge that assumes the reduced tax rate has a stated end date and an early-end trigger, so a contract that runs past 31 December 2026 carries the risk that the rate is no longer authorised.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: which vessels does the authorisation cover? «electricity directly supplied to vessels, other than private pleasure craft, at berth in a port»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given vessel call falls within vessels at berth in a port under the French implementing rules, which this text does not state.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Decision permits a tax rate rather than setting duties on named parties; the points below bind France and whoever applies the French rate. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Limits on the permission. «provided that the minimum levels of taxation referred to in Article 10 of Directive 2003/96/EC are respected» «each authorisation granted under Article 19(1) of that Directive is to be strictly limited in time» «this Decision shall cease to apply on the day on which those general provisions become applicable» A qualification on the benefit: «Under the specific conditions of the electricity generation structure in France, the use of shore-side electricity instead of electricity generated by burning bunker fuels is furthermore expected to reduce CO 2 emissions, other air pollutants and noise» «This Decision is without prejudice to the application of Union rules regarding State aid»

What this changes: France may charge less tax on shore-side electricity for the stated period. Effect by cargo vertical: not stated.

The Decision states no reduced rate, no amount saved and no pass-through to a vessel operator's charges or a freight rate.

*Analytical inference:* a lower tax on shore-side electricity lowers a cost input for vessels using it; the text states no link from that input to a freight charge.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* what reduced rate France applies and whether the rate respects the minimum levels of taxation, which this text does not state.

WINDOW CLOSING: the Decision sets no build task for freight businesses. A pricing lead adds a field to French-port quotes that records whether the electricity tax basis is the reduced rate or the standard rate and the quote date, so quotes that run past 31 December 2026 can be repriced.

One exclusion and one competition finding bear on the dates above. «vessels, other than private pleasure craft» The Council also judged the competition effect: «the application of that reduced rate of taxation is unlikely to lead to significant distortions in competition during its lifetime» *Analytical inference:* the exclusion in Article 1 is limited to private pleasure craft; the text excludes no other vessel class.
