   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Climate Change Agreements (Administration and Eligible Facilities) (Amendment) Regulations 2025», United Kingdom statutory instrument 2025 No. 813, which amends two sets of 2012 regulations on climate change agreements. Date made: «Made 7th July 2025». Where it applies: «These Regulations extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.» The document is written for a forwarder with no background in the scheme. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which facilities, including any a forwarder operates or its customers operate, hold a climate change agreement is a question for counsel; the text does not list facilities.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The instrument sits inside a UK energy-tax scheme: «These Regulations concern the scheme providing for a reduced rate of climate change levy (“ CCL ”) established under Part IV of Schedule 6 to the Finance Act 2000 (c. 17)». How the scheme works: «A facility which receives supplies of energy and which has entered into a climate change agreement (a voluntary agreement between such a facility and the Environment Agency) must meet targets for energy use or emissions which are specified in the agreement during a target period.» «If it does, it is eligible for a reduced rate of CCL during the certification period» Effective date, in the instrument's words: «These Regulations may be cited as the Climate Change Agreements (Administration and Eligible Facilities) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 and come into force on 1st January 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the scheme concerns facilities that buy energy and agree targets, not goods in transit. The text names no freight activity, so it reaches a forwarder only through its own UK facilities or customers' facilities that hold such an agreement.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step is required of a forwarder that has no facility in a climate change agreement, and nothing in the text sets a freight charge.

- A UK site operations lead checks this month whether any facility the business operates is party to a climate change agreement and, if one is, diarises 1st May 2027 for the first information return (section 10).
- A sales lead asks UK customers with such agreements, at the next account review, whether their buy-out fee or information duties will change their warehousing or haulage volumes.

*Analytical inference:* resting on section 10 and the penalty sentence in section 8, the text prices three separate exposures, all falling on the facility operator: a missed target is settled by the buy-out fee, a failure or error on information terms can bring a financial penalty, and a gap between reported and actual emissions carries a per-tonne penalty amount.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names an operator, an administrator and the Secretary of State. The Secretary of State's duty: «The Secretary of State must operate an electronic system for the administration of agreements (“ the Register ”).» The operator's terms: «the operator must, in respect of each of its facilities». No freight forwarder, carrier or logistics provider is named.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder is the operator of any facility within the scheme, for example a site it runs for its own account, is for counsel; the text does not say.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Buy-out fee

Cause: «If a facility does not meet any target for a target period, it may pay a buy-out fee on each tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent by which it falls short of meeting that target, and thus remains eligible for the reduced CCL rate.» The formula uses «C is the carbon emission factor for electricity of 0.0274» and «H is the carbon emission factor for gas of 0.0497». The amount: «Application of the formula results in a number of pounds payable per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent, with that amount representing the weighted average of the CCL rates for gas and electricity which will apply for at least the first financial year of the new target periods.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the fee is a carbon-linked cost per tonne that a facility pays instead of losing the reduced rate; the text gives no pound figure and no link to freight rates.

### Facility-level targets and eligibility

Cause: «It also makes amendments so that targets for those target periods are set by reference to a facility, rather than by reference to a group of facilities operated by a single operator.» Eligible-facilities rules change too: «This multiplication factor is changed for grid electricity from 2.6 to 2.1.» «Electricity generated from solar, wind or water power and either generated on-site or not supplied through a distribution network is excluded from this multiplication factor.» The earlier eligibility regulations now run to «to extend their effect until 31st March 2033, when the certification period in respect of target period 9 will end». Scope limit: «This regulation does not apply where any of regulations 5A to 7B applies.» Condition: «Subject to paragraph (4), the following formula applies in respect of heat produced by the combined heat and power station». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, each site is judged on its own numbers, and on-site renewable power counts differently from grid power when eligibility is tested.

### Penalties

Cause: «The administrator may impose a financial penalty on an operator if the operator, in relation to one or more of its facilities» for failing or erring on information terms. A further amount: «an amount in pounds sterling per tCO 2 equivalent of the difference between the actual emissions and the reported emissions for target period 7, 8 or 9». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the administrator can price a facility's information failures and reported-emissions gaps; the text states no cap and no pound amount.

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any cargo vertical or transport mode; any effect needs customer-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any penalty or fee term reaches a forwarder through a customer contract or a site it operates is a question for counsel.

Target periods 7 to 9 and their dates are set out in section 14.
No exceptions beyond those above are stated in regulations 2 to 4.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Information duties fall on the operator, not on a forwarder. First annual return: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May 2027 and on or before 1st May in each subsequent year». Further returns: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May 2028, and on or before 1st May 2030, such information as has been requested by the administrator in order to determine whether progress towards meeting the facility’s target is, or is likely to be, taken to be satisfactory». After each period: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May following the end of a target period such information as has been requested by the administrator». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, an operator in the scheme has a fixed calendar of returns from 2027 to 2030, with the administrator able to request more at other times.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the operator's returns carry «confirmation that the facility meets the requirements of regulation 3(1)(a) of the Climate Change Agreements (Eligible Facilities) Regulations 2012» and «such information relating to the application of the UK ETS to the facility as has been requested by the administrator». A UK site operations lead, if a site is in the scheme, adds the 1st May returns to the site compliance calendar and assigns the energy data owner. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether those terms bind a forwarder's own site is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Transition: «The amendments made by these Regulations do not apply in relation to a target period ending before 1st January 2026.» Mixed use of a site: «Where the electricity is used on other parts of a site, the electricity generated must be attributed to the facility and the rest of the site on a pro rata basis.»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the pro rata attribution reaches a site that mixes a facility with other uses, such as warehousing, is for counsel.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2025/2650 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 19 December 2025 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as regards certain obligations of operators and traders», the Union act that changes the deforestation due diligence rules for importers, exporters, downstream businesses and traders. Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its stated aim: «certain procedures and requirements laid down in Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 should be simplified and unnecessary regulatory burdens for businesses should be removed, while maintaining the objectives of that Regulation». *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of its roles a forwarder holds on a given consignment, as trader, authorised representative or the person lodging a customs declaration, is a question for counsel; the text names no forwarder.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Effective date: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». What it amends: «It lays down rules regarding the placing and making available on the Union market as well as the export from the Union of relevant products, as listed in its Annex I, that contain, have been fed with or have been made using relevant commodities, namely cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood.» Under the amended rules, a product may only be placed or made available if «(c) they are covered by a due diligence statement or a simplified declaration, as required by the relevant provisions of this Regulation.» The change is a simplification: «most recent projections on the number of expected operations and interactions in the information system have led to a substantial reassessment of the load on the system».

*Analytical inference:* resting on the commodity list above, the rules reach cargo such as cattle products, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood products that cross the Union border or move within it. The amendment moves duties between roles and adds a customs check, so a forwarder that clears or books such cargo gains new questions to ask at entry and booking.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the main duties apply from 30 December 2026, about two months after this document, and the customs reference check starts with them.

- A customs-entry lead adds to the import and export entry templates, before 30 December 2026, a required field for the due diligence statement reference number or declaration identifier of each relevant product line.
- A commercial lead asks each client that ships the listed commodities, at the next account review, who the operator is, whether a due diligence statement will exist for each shipment, and whether an authorised representative holds a written mandate.
- A contract lead adds to the next booking terms a clause under which the client supplies those reference numbers with the shipping documents.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the customs and suspension sentences in section 8, a product that the authorities identify as needing a check is held at the border, and the reference number is the item customs is to receive first; the text does not say a missing number alone causes a hold and states no storage or demurrage charge, so who bears that cost is a contract matter.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text defines five roles. «“operator” means any natural or legal person who, in the course of a commercial activity, places relevant products on the market or exports them, excluding downstream operators». «“downstream operator” means any natural or legal person who, in the course of a commercial activity, places on the market or exports relevant products made using relevant products, all of which are covered by a due diligence statement or by a simplified declaration». «“trader” means any person in the supply chain other than the operator or downstream operator who, in the course of a commercial activity, makes relevant products available on the market». «“authorised representative” means any natural or legal person established in the Union who, in accordance with Article 6, has received a written mandate from an operator to act on its behalf». Delegation: «Operators may mandate an authorised representative to submit the due diligence statement pursuant to Article 4(2) or to submit a simplified declaration pursuant to Article 4a(2) on their behalf. In such cases, the operator shall retain responsibility for the compliance of the relevant product with Article 3.» The customs duty sits with a further actor, «the person lodging the customs declaration for release for free circulation or export of a relevant product». No freight forwarder or customs broker is named.

*Analytical inference:* resting on those definitions, a forwarder that only moves cargo for a client is not by this text an operator or downstream operator, but it may be a trader if it makes products available on the market, and it may be the person lodging the customs declaration.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which role a forwarder holds on each consignment, and whether a written mandate makes it an authorised representative, is for counsel.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

All issued by the Commission:

- Simplification review: «By 30 April 2026, the Commission shall carry out a simplification review of this Regulation and on this basis present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council accompanied, where appropriate, by a legislative proposal.» That date has passed and the text does not say whether the report was presented, so any proposal it carried is not known here.
- Customs interface: «The Commission shall develop an electronic interface based on the European Union Single Window Environment for Customs». «This electronic interface shall be in place by 1 December 2029.» Until then the customs link between national systems and the information system is not in place by this text.
- Information system rules: «The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish rules for the functioning of the information system under this Article». The text sets no date.
- General review: «By 30 June 2030 and at least every five years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out a general review of this Regulation»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a later review or interface changes a forwarder's entry duties is for counsel once those acts exist.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Operators (Article 4)

Cause: «the operator shall assume responsibility for the compliance of the relevant product with Article 3». Record: «Operators shall keep a record of the due diligence statements for five years from the date the statement is submitted through the information system referred to in Article 33.» Passing on numbers: «Operators shall communicate to downstream operators and to traders further down the supply chain of the relevant products they placed on the market or exported the reference numbers of the due diligence statements or, if applicable, the declaration identifiers associated to those products.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the operator's reference number is meant to travel down the chain with the goods.

### Downstream operators and traders (Article 5)

Cause: «Downstream operators and traders shall place or make available on the market or export relevant products only if they are in possession of the information required under paragraph 3.» *Analytical inference:* resting on that sentence, a trader that lacks the supplier details and the reference numbers may not place or make the products available.

### Customs (Article 26)

Cause: «The reference number of the due diligence statement or the declaration identifier for micro or small primary operators shall be made available to customs authorities before the release for free circulation or export of a relevant product entering or leaving the market.» Who: «the person lodging the customs declaration for release for free circulation or export of a relevant product shall make available to customs authorities the reference number of the due diligence statement or the declaration identifier for micro or small primary operators associated to that relevant product». Consequence: «customs authorities shall suspend the release for free circulation or export of that relevant product» where a product is identified as requiring a check. *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the party lodging the declaration must hold the reference number at entry or export, and a flagged product is held at the border.

### Penalties, checks and corrective action

Maximum fine: «in the case of a legal person, the maximum amount of such a fine shall be at least 4 % of the operator’s, downstream operator’s or trader’s total annual Union-wide turnover in the financial year preceding the fining decision». Also: «confiscation of the relevant products concerned from the operator, downstream operator and/or trader». Corrective action includes «preventing the relevant product from being placed or made available on the market or exported». Checks each year: «cover at least 3 % of the operators, non-SME downstream operators and non-SME traders placing or making available on the market or exporting relevant products that contain or have been made using relevant commodities produced in a country of production or parts thereof classified as standard risk»; «cover at least 9 % of the operators, non-SME downstream operators and non-SME traders placing or making available on the market or exporting relevant products that contain or have been made using relevant commodities as well as 9 % of the quantity of each of the relevant products»; «cover at least 1 % of the operators, non-SME downstream operators and non-SME traders placing or making available on the market or exporting relevant products that contain or have been made using relevant commodities produced in a country or parts thereof classified as low risk». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a high-risk origin draws the heaviest checking, and a fine can reach a share of Union-wide turnover, not only the value of the goods.

### Scope and later start

Scope: «All operators, regardless of their size, that place relevant products on the market or that export those products fall under the scope of Regulation (EU) 2023/1115.» Later start for small operators: «Except as regards the products covered by the Annex to Regulation (EU) No 995/2010, for operators, whether natural persons or micro- or small undertakings within the meaning of Article 3(1) or Article 3(2), first subparagraph, respectively, of Directive 2013/34/EU, irrespective of their legal form, who were established as such by 31 December 2024, the Articles referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article shall apply from 30 June 2027».

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any vertical other than the listed commodities, and no freight charge; any effect needs client-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the customs reference duty, the five-year record duty and the fine apply to a forwarder acting for a client are questions for counsel.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 4 to 6 beyond the dates in section 14.
Obligations surveyed: 14; workspace-adjacent: 6; extracted as FACT: 15.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the text covers relevant products of the listed commodities and holds no product list for a specific shipper.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

«Downstream operators that are not SMEs (“non-SME downstream operators”) and traders that are not SMEs (“non-SME traders”) shall register in the information system referred to in Article 33 prior to placing or making available on the market or exporting relevant products.» «Micro or small primary operators shall submit a one-time simplified declaration in the information system referred to in Article 33 before placing relevant products on the market or exporting them.» Access: «The Commission shall provide access to that information system to customs authorities, competent authorities, operators, downstream operators and traders and, if applicable, their authorised representatives». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, non-SME traders must be registered before they handle relevant products, and customs authorities are among those given access to the information system.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: «Downstream operators and traders shall collect and keep the following information relating to the relevant products they intend to place or make available on the market or export». «Downstream operators and traders shall keep the information referred to in paragraph 3 for at least five years from the date of the placing or making available on the market or export, and shall provide that information to the competent authorities upon request.» A booking lead adds supplier and customer name, postal address and email fields and a five-year retention rule to the booking record for relevant products, in time for 30 December 2026. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder is a trader for this record duty is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Postal address instead of geolocation for micro or small primary operators: «the geolocation referred to in Article 9(1), point (d), may be replaced by the postal address of all plots of land or the postal address of the establishment». Customs: «This paragraph shall not apply to the export of a relevant product by a downstream operator.» Old timber: «Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 shall continue to apply until 31 December 2029 to timber and timber products as defined in Article 2, point (a), of Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 that were produced before 29 June 2023 and placed on the market from 30 December 2026».

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a consignment of old timber falls under the earlier regulation or this one is for counsel.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2024/1789 of the European Parliament and of the Council, the European Union rulebook for the internal markets in renewable gas, natural gas and hydrogen. Its jurisdiction is the European Union. The title continues: «on the internal markets for renewable gas, natural gas and hydrogen, amending Regulations (EU) No 1227/2011, (EU) 2017/1938, (EU) 2019/942 and (EU) 2022/869 and Decision (EU) 2017/684 and repealing Regulation (EC) No 715/2009 (recast)» Adoption: «Done at Brussels, 13 June 2024.»

The Regulation addresses gas and hydrogen network operators and does not name freight forwarders, carriers or shippers. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. The next review date set by the Regulation is 31 December 2030, listed in section 6.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation is the EU's recast rulebook for how gas pipelines, LNG import terminals, gas storage and a new hydrogen network are opened to users and priced. What it sets: «establishes non-discriminatory rules for access conditions to natural gas and hydrogen systems taking into account the special characteristics of national and regional markets» Its stated aim: «This Regulation aims to facilitate the penetration of renewable gas and low-carbon gas and hydrogen into the energy system, enabling a shift away from fossil gas». Reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Start dates: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.» «It shall apply from 5 February 2025.»

Who it touches: the operators of gas and hydrogen networks and facilities, and the network users that buy access from them. The only cargo-side parties the text mentions are industrial gas users: «Industrial consumers which use natural gas intensively in their production processes, such as producers of fertilisers, steel, ceramic or glass, may also benefit from demand aggregation». The text names no transport mode, route or freight service.

*Analytical inference:* because the duty holders in the quoted text are network and facility operators, a freight operator meets this Regulation through the energy costs of its customers and fuel suppliers, not through a duty of its own.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Regulation falls to a freight operator within thirty days of 1 November 2026, because its duties sit with network and facility operators. Three actions a freight desk can start now:

- A pricing lead asks gas-intensive customers, at their next rate or surcharge review, whether their delivered gas price has changed since the border tariff discounts for renewable gas and low-carbon gas began on 5 August 2025, and records the answer beside the energy-cost assumption in their quotes.
- A contracts lead adds three dates to the contract calendar of any customer planning hydrogen supply: 31 December 2030, when the Commission reviews the Regulation, 1 January 2031, when hydrogen tariff derivation is published, and 1 January 2033, when hydrogen networks become entry-exit systems.
- A sustainability lead tags any customer enquiry about LNG or hydrogen fuel supply to this item, so that tariff and access changes are checked against it before a surcharge is quoted.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names these roles: transmission system operators, hydrogen network operators, LNG system operators, hydrogen terminal operators, hydrogen storage operators, natural gas storage system operators, regulatory authorities, ACER, the ENTSO for Gas, the ENNOH, and network users. Gas transmission: «Transmission system operators shall: (a) offer capacity and services on a non-discriminatory basis to all network users» Terminals and storage: «LNG system operators, hydrogen terminal operators, hydrogen storage operators and natural gas storage system operators shall: (a) offer services on a non-discriminatory basis to all network users that accommodate market demand» The network user definition is by reference only, and section 7 records the question it raises.

The Regulation names no forwarder, carrier or shipper, and this text does not say whether a freight business falls within the network user definition.

*Analytical inference:* the access duties above are owed to network users, so a freight business that buys gas or hydrogen capacity under its own contract could be one, while a business that buys energy only through a supplier is not named by the text.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any freight business, including one that books LNG or hydrogen terminal capacity for a customer, is a network user under Directive (EU) 2024/1788 and so holds the access rights above.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation sets dates for network bodies and the Commission. Through its amendment of Regulation (EU) 2017/1938 the nearest is the Union-wide simulation: «By 1 November 2026, ENTSOG shall carry out a Union-wide simulation of gas supply and infrastructure disruption scenarios, including scenarios of a prolonged disruption of a single supply source.» That date is the date of this document, and the text does not say whether ENTSOG has finished it. *Analytical inference:* the simulation tests supply disruption scenarios, including for gas storage and LNG, which a gas-dependent customer’s energy cost could follow; the text states no freight effect.

Next, hydrogen planning moves to another body: «The ENTSO for Gas shall without delay transfer to the ENNOH all the information, including data and analyses it collected during the preparation of the Union-wide network development plans for hydrogen by 1 January 2027.» *Analytical inference:* after that date the ENNOH holds the hydrogen planning information the ENTSO for Gas collected, so questions about hydrogen network plans go to the ENNOH.

Review points: «By 5 August 2029, the Commission may prepare a report assessing how to enable stronger system integration and harness further synergies across the hydrogen, electricity and natural gas sectors» Then: «By 31 December 2030, the Commission shall review this Regulation and shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council» *Analytical inference:* these are the points at which the tariff discounts and network rules can be reconsidered, so a customer contract that assumes the current discounts has a stated review date to test them against.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: who counts as a network user? The access rights, tariff discounts and non-discrimination duties in this Regulation are all written for network users. «‘network user’ means network user as defined in Article 2, point (60), of Directive (EU) 2024/1788» The question therefore decides who can rely on them, and the text points to the Directive without restating the definition.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that books gas, LNG or hydrogen capacity, for itself or for a customer, is a network user under Directive (EU) 2024/1788.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The requirements below bind network and facility operators, regulators and Member States. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Access and pricing for natural gas. «the price of interruptible capacity shall reflect the probability of interruption» «shall be transparent, take into account the need for system integrity and its improvement and reflect the actual costs incurred, insofar as such costs correspond to those of an efficient and structurally comparable network operator» What this changes: tariffs follow the actual costs of an efficient operator; the text states no effect by cargo vertical.

Border tariff discounts. «From 5 August 2025, network users shall obtain a discount of 100 % on the capacity-based tariff from the transmission system operator at interconnection points between Member States, for renewable gas and 75 % for low-carbon gas» Condition: «after providing the transmission system operator concerned with a proof of sustainability, on the basis of a valid sustainability certificate». What this changes: certified renewable and low-carbon gas pays a lower capacity tariff at borders; the text states no effect by cargo vertical.

Hydrogen. «Hydrogen network operators shall offer their services on a non-discriminatory basis to all network users, subject to equivalent contractual terms and conditions for the same service.» «The maximum duration for capacity contracts shall be 20 years for infrastructure completed before 1 January 2028 and 15 years for infrastructure completed on or after that date.» «From 1 January 2033, hydrogen networks shall be organised as entry-exit systems.» Principle: «natural gas and, from 2033, hydrogen shall be transported by means of the entry-exit system, rather than contractual paths».

Scope and limits. «Article 1 Subject matter and scope This Regulation: (a) establishes non-discriminatory rules for access conditions to natural gas and hydrogen systems». «This Regulation, with the exception of Article 34(5) thereof, shall apply only to the natural gas storage facilities and hydrogen storage facilities referred to in Article 33(3) or (4) or Article 37 of Directive (EU) 2024/1788.»

The Regulation states no pass-through of network tariffs or tariff discounts to delivered gas or hydrogen prices or to freight charges.

*Analytical inference:* the discounts and cost-reflective tariffs change what network users pay for gas capacity, which is an input cost for gas-intensive customers; the text states no link from that input cost to a freight rate.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a customer's gas or hydrogen supply contract falls within the network access and tariff duties above, and who bears the tariff under that contract.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties sit with network operators and public bodies. «The transmission system operator shall make public detailed information regarding the capacity and services it offers and the relevant conditions applied» «all data shall be made available from 1 October 2026 on one Union-wide central platform, established by the ENNOH on a cost-efficient basis» The Regulation states no registration duty for a freight business; its reporting duties fall on network operators, regulatory authorities, ACER and the Commission.

Enforcement: «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation» «The Commission may, by decision, impose on undertakings fines not exceeding 1 % of the total turnover in the preceding business year where, intentionally or negligently, those undertakings supply incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in response to a request for information» *Analytical inference:* the fine the text names is for undertakings that give incorrect information to the Commission; the text names no fine for any freight activity.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which national penalty rules each Member State has notified, since this text leaves them to Member States.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text sets a build task for operators, not for freight businesses. «by 5 February 2026, LNG system operators, hydrogen terminal operators, hydrogen storage operators and natural gas storage system operators, individually or jointly with other such operators, shall ensure that a transparent and non-discriminatory booking platform» «users may resell their contracted capacity on the secondary market» *Analytical inference:* the same quoted provision lets users resell their contracted capacity on the secondary market, so a customer that holds contracted capacity at such a facility can resell it; the text does not say how the booking platform is used.

A pricing lead adds an energy-cost basis field to the cargo record, filled from the customer's own supply contract, before a surcharge tied to gas or hydrogen costs is quoted.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Two carve-outs matter to the dates above. «regulatory authorities may decide not to apply discounts or to lay down discounts lower than those laid down in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this Article» «Member States may decide not to apply paragraph 6 of this Article to hydrogen networks that benefit from a derogation pursuant to Article 52 Directive (EU) 2024/1788 and are not connected to another hydrogen network.» *Analytical inference:* a customer in a Member State that applies either carve-out may not see the discount or the entry-exit system on the stated dates, so that Member State's regulator decides what changes for it.

- 5 February 2025: The Regulation applies. «It shall apply from 5 February 2025.»
- 5 August 2025: Border capacity tariff discount for renewable and low-carbon gas starts. «From 5 August 2025, network users shall obtain a discount of 100 %»

- 1 October 2026: Hydrogen network data on one central platform. «all data shall be made available from 1 October 2026 on one Union-wide central platform»

- 1 January 2027: ENTSO for Gas hands its hydrogen planning information to the ENNOH. «by 1 January 2027»

What changes for a freight desk on these dates: nothing directly. *Analytical inference:* the dates that can move a customer's energy cost are 5 August 2025 for the border tariff discounts and 1 January 2031 and 1 January 2033 for hydrogen tariffs and network organisation, because those are the steps the quoted text ties to tariffs and access.

The Regulation also carries earlier deadlines for authorities and network bodies: certification decisions on gas storage operators, consultation and methodology steps under the trans-European energy infrastructure text, a Commission report on regulatory authority independence, a Commission report on gas security of supply, and the draft statutes of the ENNOH. They are past, the text does not say which were completed, and none changes a freight decision. Dates before 1 November 2026 in the rows above are likewise past steps. The recitals also name a 2050 climate-neutrality target; it is a target and not a step of this Regulation, so it is not a row.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Document date:** 2026-11-01

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2024/2865 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024, which amends Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 on the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (known as CLP). It is a European Union regulation and applies in the Union. It changes who is answerable for a chemical product on the EU market, how labels look and are provided, what is said in advertising and online offers, and who sends emergency health information to national bodies.

How to read it: statements of what the regulation says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation updates the Union's chemical labelling rules for online sales and new technology. The Union's reason, in recital 1: «economic operators established outside the Union sell chemicals online directly to the general public in the Union.» The cure it chooses: «It is therefore necessary to require that there be a supplier established in the Union which ensures that the substance or the mixture in question meets the requirements set out in Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 when it is being placed on the market, including via distance sales, such as via online market places.» It also adds new definitions, for example: «“data carrier” means a linear bar code symbol, a two-dimensional symbol or other automatic identification data capture medium that can be read by a device» «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Why it matters to a freight operator: chemical products reach the Union through importers, distributors and online sales. Three changes land on those chains. A supplier established in the Union must be identified on the label (section 8); importers, downstream users and distributors of hazardous mixtures must submit information to national bodies (section 10); and stock that was already labelled under the listed earlier provisions keeps those label rules for a period (section 12). The regulation sets no freight rate or surcharge and names no carrier.

*Analytical inference:* because the quoted recital describes sales to the general public from outside the Union, a consignment of chemical products bound for a buyer in the Union can bring the sender's customer under the supplier rule; the text does not say a carrier is a supplier.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the period in which products may still follow the old rules for several of the new items ends on 31 December 2026, less than two months after the date of this document, and the submission duty for importers, downstream users and distributors applies from 1 January 2027 (section 14). The steps below follow from those dates.

- A product-compliance lead, before 31 December 2026, asks each client that places hazardous mixtures on the EU market whether it distributes in another Member State, or rebrands or relabels a mixture, because the section 10 submission duty reaches distributors on those facts from 1 January 2027.
- A customer-onboarding lead, at the next contract with a seller outside the Union that ships chemicals to buyers in the Union, records which supplier established in the Union is identified on the label, because the supplier rule in section 4 applies from 1 July 2026.
- A warehouse operations lead, at the next stock review of labelled chemical goods, lists lots by the date placed on the market and by whether they were labelled under the provisions listed in section 12, against the dates 1 July 2026 and 1 January 2027, because the section 12 transitions cover only lots meeting both conditions.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation names these parties. The supplier established in the Union: «A substance or a mixture shall not be placed on the market unless a supplier established in the Union, which shall be identified on the label, in the course of an industrial or professional activity fulfils the requirements set out in this Regulation with regard to the substances or mixture in question» The text also names manufacturers, importers, downstream users, distributors, the supplier of a substance in the scope of the plant protection and biocides rules («The supplier of a substance or mixture that falls within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 or Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 shall update the label in accordance with those Regulations»), consumers, the general public, online market places, appointed national bodies and the European Chemicals Agency.

The regulation names no freight forwarder, carrier or customs broker. *Analytical inference:* the quoted supplier rule rests on a supplier acting in an industrial or professional activity and fulfilling the Regulation's requirements, so a freight operator is in the chain only if, in a given job, it is itself the importer, downstream user, distributor or supplier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator that clears or stores chemical goods in its own name is an importer, a distributor or a supplier under the quoted wording, and which duty then follows.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text holds no published guidance document; the guidance the regulation provides for is listed in section 6.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dates are quoted from the text; the first below is before the date of this document and is stated as past.

- Delegated acts: the power to adopt them «shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 10 December 2024», so the Commission can add to the rules by act after that date.
- Guidance: «The Agency shall provide further guidance for the application of paragraphs 1, 2 and 3.» The captured text gives no date for it.
- Scientific report: «By 11 December 2029, the Commission shall present a scientific report to the European Parliament and to the Council regarding the examination of the information on substances containing more than one constituent extracted from plants.»
- Evaluation report: «By 11 December 2029, the Commission shall present an evaluation report to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee, assessing the need to extend requirements in sections 3.1 and 3.2 of Annex II on child-resistant fastenings and tactile warnings to other hazard classes.»

What changes when these arrive: a delegated act can change the criteria in the substantive rules (section 8); the guidance, once issued, explains how the concentration limits are to be applied; the December 2029 reports may carry a legislative proposal and are the next point at which the child-resistant fastening rules could reach other hazard classes. *Analytical inference:* the 2029 evaluation rests on the quoted need to assess extension to other hazard classes, so no extension is in force from it.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: who counts as the "supplier" that must be established in the Union? The recital answers for online sales: «In order to avoid situations where a consumer becomes de jure and de facto an importer when buying the substance or the mixture via distance sales from economic operators established outside the Union, it is necessary to specify that the supplier which ensures that the substance or the mixture in question meets the requirements set out in Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 acts in the course of an industrial or professional activity.»

*Analytical inference:* the quoted recital rests on the aim of keeping a consumer from becoming an importer, so the supplier is the industrial or professional party that ensures compliance. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator that handles the goods for such a seller is outside the supplier role, which the captured text does not state.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties below apply to suppliers, importers, downstream users and distributors as the quoted articles describe them; whether and how each applies to a given operator is a question for counsel and is not settled here.

**Labels.** «The label elements referred to in Article 17(1) shall be clearly and indelibly marked. They shall stand out clearly from the background and they shall be of such a size and be spaced in such a way as to be easily read.» For digital labels: «The label elements for substances and mixtures referred to in Article 17 shall be provided on a label in a physical form (“physical label”). In addition to the physical label, the label elements referred to in Article 17 may be provided in a digital form (“digital label”).» «Where a digital label as provided for in Article 34a(1) is used, a data carrier linking to that digital label shall be firmly affixed or printed on the physical label or on the packaging next to the label in such a way that it can be processed automatically by digital devices that are widely used.»

**Updating a label after a change.** «In the event of a change regarding the classification or labelling of a substance or a mixture, which results in the addition of a new hazard class or in a more severe classification, or which requires new supplemental information on the label in accordance with Article 25, the supplier of that substance or that mixture shall ensure that the label is updated without undue delay and in any event no later than 6 months after the results of the new evaluation referred to in Article 15(4) are obtained by, or communicated to, that supplier.» For other changes: «no later than 18 months after the results of the new evaluation referred to in Article 15(4) are obtained by, or communicated to, that supplier»

**Advertising and online offers.** «Any advertisement for a substance classified as hazardous shall indicate, as applicable, the hazard pictograms, signal words, hazard statements and supplemental EUH statements set out in Annex II.» For distance sales: «When substances or mixtures are placed on the market through distance sales, the offer shall clearly and visibly indicate the label elements referred to in Article 17.»

**Active substances.** «Substances that are active substances falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 or Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 shall be subject to harmonised classification and labelling.»

**One exemption.** For ammunition that is a substance or mixture and is used by defence forces, the recital says «it is necessary to provide for an exemption from the labelling requirements and allow for alternative ways of communicating the hazard information».

**Penalty.** No penalty: the amending text states no penalty, fine or sanction; it names the authorities responsible for enforcement and states no consequence of its own.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Importers, downstream users and distributors of hazardous mixtures must send information to bodies the Member States appoint. For importers and downstream users: «Importers and downstream users placing on the market mixtures that are classified as hazardous on the basis of their health or physical effects, shall submit to the body or bodies appointed in accordance with paragraph 1 the information referred to in Part B of Annex VIII.» For distributors: «Distributors placing on the market mixtures that are classified as hazardous on the basis of their health or physical effects shall submit to the body or bodies appointed in accordance with paragraph 1 the information referred to in Part B of Annex VIII where they subsequently distribute those mixtures in other Member States, or where they rebrand or relabel the mixtures.»

The information is set by Annex VIII. Its start dates are stated in the replaced section 1 of Annex VIII: for mixtures for consumer use, «Importers, downstream users and distributors referred to in Article 45(1b) and (1c) placing on the market mixtures for consumer use, within the meaning of section 2.4 of Part A of this Annex, shall comply with this Annex from 1 January 2021.» For mixtures for industrial use: «Importers, downstream users and distributors referred to in Article 45(1b) and (1c) placing on the market mixtures for industrial use or mixtures with an end use not subject to notification within the meaning of section 2.4 of Part A of this Annex, shall comply with this Annex from 1 January 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the quoted distributor duty is triggered by distributing in other Member States or rebranding or relabelling, so a distributor that sells only in one Member State and does not rebrand is not reached by the quoted sentence. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator that stores and moves mixtures between Member States for a client is a distributor under the quoted wording, and when the information must be sent.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the captured text sets no system for a freight operator to build unless it is itself an importer, distributor or supplier. For those that are, the data to carry is set by the quoted label and submission rules.

- An e-commerce operations lead at a seller that ships chemicals, at the next change to online offers, adds the label elements of Article 17 to each offer, because section 8 quotes that rule for distance sales and Article 1 points (26) and (27) apply from 1 July 2026.
- A product-compliance lead, at the next product data refresh before 1 January 2027, adds a field for the Annex VIII submission status of each hazardous mixture to the product record, because the section 10 duty applies from that date.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the quoted duties; the captured text does not tell an operator how to build them.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The regulation lets some stock already on the market keep the old rules for a time, but only stock labelled under the listed provisions as they applied before the amendment. First group: «Substances and mixtures which have been classified, labelled and packaged in accordance with Article 5, Article 6(3) and (4), Article 9(3) and (4), Article 10, Article 25(3), Articles 29 and section 1.5.1.2 of Annex I, section 1.5.2.4.1 of Annex I as applicable on 9 December 2024 and which were placed on the market before 1 July 2026 shall not be required to be classified, labelled and packaged in accordance with this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2865 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *3 ) until 1 July 2028.» Second group: «Substances and mixtures which have been classified, labelled and packaged in accordance with Article 18(3), Article 31(3) and section 1.2.1 of Annex I, as applicable on 9 December 2024 and which were placed on the market before 1 January 2027 shall not be required to be classified, labelled and packaged in accordance with this Regulation as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/2865 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *3 ) until 1 January 2029.» For distributors the submission duty has one carve-out: «That obligation shall not apply if the distributors can demonstrate that the appointed body or bodies already received the same information from importers and downstream users.»

*Analytical inference:* the two stock transitions rest on two conditions in the quoted sentences, that the lot was labelled under the listed provisions as applicable on the earlier date and that it was placed on the market before the later date; a lot that fails either condition is not covered by the quoted transition, and the date is that of placing on the market, not of shipment.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 23 October 2024: the regulation is adopted: «Done at Strasbourg, 23 October 2024.»
- Twentieth day after publication: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»
- 10 December 2024: the delegation of power to the Commission starts (section 6).
- 1 January 2021 and 1 January 2024: the Annex VIII start dates for consumer-use and industrial-use mixtures stated in the replaced text (section 10).
- 1 July 2026: «points (4), (8), (10) and (11) of Annex I and Annex II shall apply from 1 July 2026.»
- 31 December 2026: «substances and mixtures may until 31 December 2026 be classified, labelled and packaged in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 as amended by Article 1, points (1) and (9), Article 1, point (15)(c), Article 1, point (24)(b) and (d) of this Regulation, points (2) and (3) of Annex I and Annex IV to this Regulation»
- 1 January 2027: «Article 1, point (1), Article 1, point (9), Article 1, point (15)(c), Article 1, points (24)(b) and (d), points (2) and (3) of Annex I and Annex IV shall apply from 1 January 2027.»
- 1 July 2028: end of the first stock transition, for lots labelled under the listed provisions and placed on the market before 1 July 2026 (section 12).
- 1 January 2029: end of the second stock transition, for lots labelled under the listed provisions and placed on the market before 1 January 2027 (section 12).
- 11 December 2029: the Commission's reports are due (section 6).

What each date changes: the 2026 date brings the supplier-in-the-Union rule, advertising and distance-sales rules into use; the December 2026 date is the last day on which the old rules may be used for the later group of items; the 2027 date brings the submission duty for importers, downstream users and distributors; the 2028 and 2029 dates end the stock transitions; the 2029 reports may lead to a proposal.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1787 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 on the reduction of methane emissions in the energy sector and amending Regulation (EU) 2019/942», the Union rules on methane leaks from oil, gas and coal, including the oil, gas and coal that is imported. Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its stated purpose: «This Regulation lays down rules for the accurate measurement, quantification, monitoring, reporting and verification of methane emissions in the energy sector in the Union, as well as the reduction of those emissions». *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of its duties fall on a forwarder or customs agent that handles an import of oil, gas or coal for a client is a question for counsel; the text names no forwarder.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Methane is a greenhouse gas that leaks from wells, pipelines, coal mines and flares. Most of the regulation sets rules for sites in the Union. The part that reaches freight is Chapter 5: «This Regulation applies also to methane emissions occurring outside the Union, with respect to crude oil, natural gas and coal placed on the Union market, as referred to in Chapter 5.» Effective date: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* resting on that sentence, the rules follow the cargo back to its producer, so a forwarder or customs agent that moves or clears crude oil, natural gas or coal into the Union meets them as a question about the producer's measurement, not only about the voyage. The text does not say how a cargo of liquefied natural gas is treated, so that case is open.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: from 1 January 2027, about two months after this document, importers must show their supply contracts cover only equivalently monitored oil, gas and coal.

- A customs-entry lead lists, before 1 January 2027, every import of crude oil, natural gas or coal where the business, or a client that appointed it, is the importer, and records the exporter, the producer and the producing and transit regions that Annex IX asks for.
- A contract lead adds, at each renewal of a supply or transport contract that names the producer, a clause under which the exporter supplies the Annex IX data and its latest methane emissions report.
- A commercial lead asks each such client, at the next account review, for the supply contracts concluded or renewed on or after 4 August 2024, so that the equivalence evidence can be assembled before 1 January 2027.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the importer definition and the equivalence sentence in section 8, the 1 January 2027 proof needs a contract and a producer record for each supply contract concluded or renewed on or after 4 August 2024; a contract with no such record is a gap, and the duty sits with the importer or the appointed person.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text defines three roles. «‘importer’ means a natural or legal person who, in the course of a commercial activity, places crude oil, natural gas or coal originating from a third country on the Union market, including any natural or legal person established in the Union appointed to carry out acts and formalities required under Chapter 5». «‘exporter’ means the contractual counterparty to the importer in each contract concluded for the supply of crude oil, natural gas or coal into the Union». Upstream: «‘operator’ means any natural or legal person who operates or controls an asset». No freight forwarder, carrier or customs broker is named.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the importer definition, a forwarder appointed to file the Chapter 5 information for a client is itself within the importer definition, while a forwarder that only carries the cargo is not named.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder is the importer, or a person appointed under Chapter 5, on a given import is for counsel.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: no authoritative guidance document is held for this regulation.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

All issued by the Commission:

- Equivalence procedure: «the Commission shall set out, by means of an implementing act, the procedure and requirements concerning evidence to be provided by a third country for establishing equivalence». Until that act sets the evidence, equivalence for a country is not established by this text. Limit: «The Commission shall refrain from adopting such implementing acts where their adoption would circumvent restrictive measures adopted under Article 215 TFEU restricting the import of crude oil, natural gas or coal.»
- Model clauses: «The Commission shall issue recommendations containing optional model clauses related to the information to be provided for the purposes of paragraphs 1 and 2». These are meant for contract renewals.
- Methodology: «By 5 August 2027, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 34 to supplement this Regulation by setting out the methodology for calculating, at the level of the producer, the methane intensity of the production of crude oil, natural gas and coal placed on the Union market.»
- Maximum values: «the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 34 to supplement this Regulation by setting out the maximum methane intensity values associated with crude oil, natural gas and coal placed on the Union market at the level of the producer». The text gives no date for these acts.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* once adopted, whether each act changes an importer's or appointed person's evidence duties is for counsel.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the text sets no threshold question for importers beyond the importer definition in section 4.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Who is covered

Scope: «This Regulation applies to: (a) oil and fossil gas exploration and production, and fossil gas gathering and processing». Importers join through Chapter 5 (section 2).

### Importer information (Article 27)

Cause: «By 5 May 2025 and by 31 May every year thereafter, importers shall provide the information set out in Annex IX to the competent authorities of the Member State in which they are established.» Gaps: «Where importers fail to provide that information, in whole or in part, they shall provide sound justification to those competent authorities for such failure and set out the actions that they have undertaken to obtain that information.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the annual return is due each year by 31 May, and a missing item needs a stated reason and the steps taken to get it.

### Equivalent monitoring (Article 28)

Cause: «From 1 January 2027, importers shall demonstrate, and report in accordance with Article 27(1), to the competent authorities of the Member State in which they are established that the contracts concluded or renewed on or after 4 August 2024 for the supply of crude oil, natural gas or coal produced outside the Union cover only crude oil, natural gas or coal that is subject to monitoring, reporting and verification measures applied at the level of the producer that are equivalent to those set out in this Regulation.» Older contracts: «For contracts concluded before 4 August 2024 for the supply of crude oil, natural gas or coal produced outside the Union, importers shall undertake all reasonable efforts to require that crude oil, natural gas or coal is subject to monitoring, reporting and verification measures applied at the level of the producer that are equivalent to those set out in this Regulation.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, contracts signed or renewed after 4 August 2024 carry the full proof duty, while older contracts carry an effort duty.

### Methane intensity (Article 29)

Reporting: «By 5 August 2028 and every year thereafter, for the supply contracts concluded or renewed on or after 4 August 2024, Union producers and, pursuant to Article 27(1), importers shall report to the competent authorities of the Member State in which they are established the methane intensity of the production of crude oil, natural gas and coal placed by them on the Union market». From 2030 the importer must show: «shall demonstrate to the competent authorities of the Member State in which they are established that the methane intensity of the production of crude oil, natural gas and coal placed by them on the Union market, calculated in accordance with the methodology set out pursuant to paragraph 4, is below the maximum methane intensity values» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, supply contracts renewed after 5 August 2030 face a ceiling on the producer's methane intensity, so source choices become a compliance question.

### Upstream duties and penalties

Operators: «By 5 August 2025, operators shall submit a report to the competent authorities containing the quantification of source-level methane emissions»; «By 5 May 2025 for existing sites and within 6 months from the date of start of operations for new sites, operators shall submit a leak detection and repair programme». Penalties: «periodic penalty payments to compel operators, undertakings, mine operators or importers to put an end to an infringement». Fines: «In the case of legal persons, the amount of the administrative fines referred to in point (e) shall not exceed 20 % of the annual turnover in the preceding business year.» Importer infringements named: «failure of importers to provide the information required in accordance with Article 27(1) and Annex IX»; «failure of importers to provide the information required in accordance with Article 28(1) and (2)». Exemption: «Importers shall be exempt from the reporting obligations set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 where they import crude oil, natural gas or coal from a third country for which equivalence has been established in accordance with paragraph 6.»

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any cargo vertical other than crude oil, natural gas and coal, and no freight charge; any effect needs client-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the importer, equivalence and intensity duties and the fine apply to a forwarder acting for an importer, and which Member State's rules apply, are questions for counsel.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 27 to 29 beyond the dates in section 14.
Obligations surveyed: 13; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 14.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the text covers crude oil, natural gas and coal and holds no product list for a specific shipper.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Annex IX asks for «name and address of the exporter and, if different from the exporter, name and address of the producer», and the «countries and regions, as classified in the NUTS level 1, through which the products were transported before they were placed on the Union market». Member States then pass the data on: «By 5 August 2025 and by 31 August every year thereafter, Member States shall submit to the Commission the information provided by importers.» Confidentiality: «The competent authorities of the Member States shall protect the confidentiality of the information received from importers under this Article, in accordance with Union law.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the route data a forwarder holds, the regions the cargo passed through before reaching the Union market, is part of the return.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: the return also asks «information whether the producer or the exporter, as applicable, is carrying out source- and site-level measurement and quantification». A documentation lead adds fields for exporter, producer, producing region and transit region to the import file and requests the producer's latest methane report from the exporter, in time for 1 January 2027. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder must collect these items itself is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Equivalence can be lost: «Equivalence may be revoked at any time by the Commission, by means of an implementing act, where the third country no longer complies, in law or in practice, with the conditions set out in paragraph 5, point (b), of this Article during a period of at least 12 months.» Fines and orders apply «provided that they do not endanger the security of energy supply». Sanctions limit: see the equivalence limit in section 6.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an exemption by equivalence covers a cargo from a country whose equivalence is later revoked is for counsel.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

Entries dated before this document are past; the text states what was due, not whether it was done.

- 13 June 2024: adopted. «Done at Brussels, 13 June 2024.»
- 4 August 2024: the date after which new import contracts carry the full proof duty; the Commission to seek producer-country frameworks. «From 4 August 2024, where appropriate and subject to the applicable procedures, the Commission shall propose and aim for the Union to enter into cooperation frameworks with third countries from which the Union imports crude oil, natural gas or coal»
- 1 January 2025: coal-mine flaring and drainage venting limits start. «Flaring with a destruction and removal efficiency by design level below 99 % and venting of methane from drainage systems shall be prohibited from 1 January 2025»
- 5 February 2025: Member States name their authorities, so an importer knows where to file. «Member States shall notify the Commission of the names and contact details of their competent authorities by 5 February 2025.»
- 5 May 2025: first importer return due, and by 31 May each year. «By 5 May 2025 and by 31 May every year thereafter, importers shall provide the information set out in Annex IX»
- 5 August 2025: Member States notify their penalty rules to the Commission. «By 5 August 2025, Member States shall notify the Commission of those rules and those measures»
- 5 February 2026: Commission opens the methane transparency database. «By 5 February 2026, the Commission shall establish and maintain a methane transparency database»
- 5 May 2026: first routine inspection of upstream sites completed. «The first routine inspection shall be completed by 5 May 2026.»
- 5 August 2026: Commission global monitoring tool due. «By 5 August 2026, the Commission shall establish a global methane monitoring tool based on satellite data»
- 1 January 2027: importers are to demonstrate equivalence for new contracts. «From 1 January 2027, importers shall demonstrate, and report in accordance with Article 27(1)»
- 5 February 2027: coal-mine mitigation plans due. «That mitigation plan shall be submitted to the competent authorities by 5 February 2027.»
- 5 August 2027: methane-intensity methodology due. «By 5 August 2027, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 34 to supplement this Regulation by setting out the methodology for calculating»
- 1 January 2028: first Commission review report. «The Commission shall monitor and review the application of this Regulation and submit, by 1 January 2028 and every 5 years thereafter, a report to the European Parliament and to the Council.»
- 5 August 2028: first methane-intensity report from importers. «From 5 August 2028, Union producers and importers placing crude oil, natural gas or coal on the Union market shall report annually to the competent authorities»
- 5 August 2029: Commission assesses maximum intensity values. «By 5 August 2029, the Commission shall assess the potential impact of various levels of maximum methane intensity values»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2025/2365 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 12 November 2025 on preventing plastic pellet losses to reduce microplastic pollution», the Union rules that stop plastic pellets spilling from handling sites, vehicles and ships. Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its aim: «This Regulation lays down obligations for the handling of plastic pellets to prevent losses at all stages of the plastic pellet supply chain, with the aim of achieving zero plastic pellet losses.» *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of its duties fall on a forwarder that books or arranges pellet transport but does not itself carry, ship or handle the pellets is a question for counsel; the text names no forwarder.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Pellets are the small plastic granules that factories melt and mould: «‘plastic pellets’ means a mass of polymer-containing material, regardless of its shape, form, or size, that is produced for moulding in plastic product manufacturing operations, irrespective of its actual use». Effective date: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». Main application: «It shall apply from 17 December 2027.» Some Articles apply earlier and the sea rules later (sections 8 and 14).

*Analytical inference:* resting on the carrier and shipper definitions in section 4, the rules follow the pellets onto road, rail, inland waterway and sea legs, so a forwarder moving polymer cargo meets them as a booking question on every mode, not only on one.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COMPETITIVE EDGE: the loss-avoidance duty for carriers already applies, and the notification and sea duties start later, so the edge is being ready before shippers ask.

- A road-haulage procurement lead adds to carrier contracts for pellet loads this quarter a clause requiring the Annex III actions: check packaging before the journey, clean loading compartments and carry closed collection containers.
- A sea-freight documentation lead builds, before 17 December 2028, a pellet flag on the booking record and a template for the transport information and special stowage request that must reach the vessel before loading.
- A sales lead asks plastics clients, at the next account review, whether they handle 5 tonnes or more of pellets a year, which brings them within the economic-operator duties from 17 December 2027.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the Article 3 and Article 15 sentences in section 8, a carrier that loses pellets must clean up and report, and an authority may hold its vehicles, so a pellet load is a delay risk as well as a clean-up risk.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text defines the roles. «‘EU carrier’ means any natural or legal person established in a Member State, engaged in the transport of plastic pellets as part of its economic activity by using road vehicles, rail wagons or inland waterway vessels». «‘non-EU carrier’ means any natural or legal person established in a third country, engaged in the transport of plastic pellets as part of its economic activity in the Union by using road vehicles, rail wagons or inland waterway vessels». «‘shipper’ means any natural or legal person by whom or in whose name or on whose behalf a contract of carriage of goods has been concluded with any natural or legal person engaged in the transport of plastic pellets as part of its economic activity by using seagoing vessels». Seagoing vessels: «‘operator’ means the owner or manager of a seagoing vessel». Non-EU carriers: «Non-EU carriers shall designate in writing an authorised representative in at least one Member State where the non-EU carrier is engaged in the transport of plastic pellets.» No freight forwarder or booking agent is named.

*Analytical inference:* resting on those definitions, a forwarder that holds the contract of carriage with a sea carrier on the cargo owner's behalf may fall inside the shipper definition, and one that arranges road, rail or inland waterway legs sits with the carrier it hires.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder is a shipper, or is responsible for a carrier's duties, on a given booking is for counsel.
