## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

All issued by the Commission:

- Training material: «By 17 December 2026, the Commission shall develop and make available to the public, including via the internet, on a website which is easy to find, free of charge and without restricting access to registered users, awareness-raising and training material on the appropriate implementation of the obligations laid down in this Regulation».
- Loss-estimate standards: «The Commission shall submit the request for the development of harmonised standards to one or more European standardisation organisations by 17 December 2026.» The method: «a methodology to estimate quantities of losses shall be developed in harmonised standards in accordance with the procedures established by Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012».
- Delegated acts: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 22(1) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 2 January 2028.» The text names no act yet.
- IMO alignment: «In the event of the adoption by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) of measures for the safe transport of plastic pellets by ships and for the prevention of marine pollution caused by plastic pellets transported by ships, the Commission shall assess those measures».

*Analytical inference:* resting on the stored text of two linked briefs on this site, one holding an excess emissions premium per gCO2/tkm that the Commission imposes on manufacturers and one holding a Commission report on ships due by the end of 2026, those briefs carry their own dated steps near the end of 2026; this Regulation states no link to either.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission's training material changes the duties of a forwarder is for counsel once it is published.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the 5 tonne and 1 500 tonne handling thresholds sit in section 8 and bind operators, and the text sets no carrier threshold.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Who is covered

Scope: «This Regulation applies to the following natural and legal persons: (a) economic operators handling plastic pellets in the Union in quantities equal to or above a threshold of 5 tonnes in the previous calendar year», and carriers: «EU carriers and non-EU carriers transporting plastic pellets in the Union». Certificates and yearly checks turn on size of handling: «operating installations where plastic pellets in quantities equal to or above a threshold of 1 500 tonnes have been handled in the previous calendar year». Sea: «Article 12, Article 13(1), Article 17(2) and (3) and Article 19 shall apply, as far as shippers and operators, agents and masters of seagoing vessels are concerned, from 17 December 2028».

### Loss avoidance and clean-up (Article 3)

Cause: «Economic operators, EU carriers and non-EU carriers shall ensure that losses are avoided.» «Where losses occur, economic operators, EU carriers and non-EU carriers shall take immediate action to contain and clean up those losses in accordance with environmentally sustainable practices.» First notice by carriers: «Before the transport of plastic pellets in the Union for the first time, EU carriers or authorised representatives referred to in Article 4, as applicable, shall notify the competent authorities of the Member State in which the EU carrier or the authorised representative is established about their involvement in the transport of plastic pellets within the Union and the means of transport used.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a carrier must avoid losses from now and must notify the authority before its first pellet journey in the Union.

### Carrier actions and records (Article 5 and Annex III)

Cause: «EU carriers and non-EU carriers shall ensure that the actions set out in Annex III are implemented.» Annex III includes «verification, during and after loading and unloading, that plastic pellets are properly removed from the outside of the transport means and freight containers before leaving the installation» and equipment: «at least one portable lighting device, hand tools (e.g. brooms, dustpans and brushes, buckets, repair tapes, etc.); closed collection containers/reinforced collection bags». Records: «keep records of annually estimated quantities of losses and of the total quantities of plastic pellets handled», kept «Economic operators and EU carriers and authorised representatives shall retain records referred to in point (b) of the first subparagraph for a period of five years». Incidents: «without delay and no later than 30 days after the incident or accident that causes a loss affecting human health or the environment, provide the following information to the competent authorities in whose territories the incident or accident occurred». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a carrier needs a cleaning routine, a spill kit and a five-year loss log.

### Sea shipments in containers (Article 12)

Shippers shall ensure that «plastic pellets are packed in good-quality packaging that is strong enough to withstand the shocks and loadings normally encountered during transport»; «transport information identifying the freight containers containing plastic pellets is delivered to the operator, agent and master of the seagoing vessel as an addition to the cargo information required by Regulation VI/2 of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), before plastic pellets are taken on board»; and «cargo information referred to in point (b) of this paragraph is accompanied by a special stowage request». Ships: «Operators and masters of seagoing vessels shall ensure that freight containers containing plastic pellets are stowed under deck, wherever reasonably practicable, or inboard in sheltered areas of exposed decks.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the shipper must get the pellet container marking and stowage request to the vessel before loading.

### Penalties and holds

Fine: «For the most serious infringements committed by a legal person, the maximum level of the administrative financial penalties referred to in paragraph 2 shall be at least 3 % of its annual Union turnover in the financial year preceding the year in which the administrative financial penalty is imposed.» Authority power: «suspend the operation of the installation or part of it, and immobilise or prevent the movement of road vehicles, rail wagons or inland waterway vessels until compliance is restored». Exemption by permit: «Member States may exempt economic operators from the obligations laid down in Article 5(1), point (c), and Article 5(2) as well as from the obligation to obtain a certificate pursuant to Article 6(1), (2) and (3)». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a serious breach can cost a share of Union turnover and, for road, rail and inland waterway carriers, can stop the vehicle moving.

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any cargo vertical other than plastic pellets, and no freight charge; any effect needs client-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the carrier, shipper and fine provisions reach a forwarder acting for a cargo owner, and which Member State's penalty rules apply, are questions for counsel.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 3 and 5 beyond the dates in section 14.
Obligations surveyed: 14; workspace-adjacent: 8; extracted as FACT: 20.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Operators notify each installation: «Economic operators shall notify the competent authorities of the Member State about each installation located in that Member State which they operate or control». Carriers' notice is in section 8. Member State reports: «By 1 January 2030, and every three years thereafter, Member States shall submit a report to the Commission containing qualitative and quantitative information on the implementation of this Regulation». Public lists: «The Commission shall make a list of designated authorised representatives of non-EU carriers based on the information submitted to it pursuant to Article 4(3) and shall make that list available to the public». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a non-EU carrier's representative is publicly listed, so a client can check whether a haulier named one.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COMPETITIVE EDGE: carriers must have «ensure that their staff are trained according to their specific roles and responsibilities and that they are aware of and are able to use the relevant equipment and execute the procedures set out to ensure compliance with this Regulation». On infringement: «In the event of an infringement of the rules laid down in this Regulation, economic operators, EU carriers, non-EU carriers and authorised representatives, as applicable, shall immediately». A road-haulage procurement lead adds a pellet-load checklist and a trained-driver record to the subcontractor file. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder has to evidence a carrier's training is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Management-system exemption: «Economic operators which are registered with the Community eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS) in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009 shall be exempt from compliance with the obligations laid down in Article 5(2) and in Article 6(1), (2) and (3) of this Regulation». Carrier threshold open: «an assessment of the impact on the implementation of this Regulation of excluding from certain obligations under this Regulation economic operators handling plastic pellets below certain thresholds, and the relevance of establishing a threshold for carriers». Stowage under deck applies only where reasonably practicable (section 8).

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an exemption reaches a carrier, rather than an operator, is for counsel.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/3005 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 November 2024 on the transparency and integrity of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) rating activities», published in the Official Journal of the European Union and closed with «Done at Strasbourg, 27 November 2024.» Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation applies to ESG ratings issued by ESG rating providers operating in the Union.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text. What it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The Regulation sets its own review point: «The Commission shall evaluate the application of this Regulation by 2 January 2029.»

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets one set of rules for the companies that sell ESG ratings. It defines an ESG rating as «‘ESG rating’ means an opinion or a score, or a combination of both, regarding a rated item’s profile or characteristics with regard to environmental, social and human rights, or governance factors,» and an ESG rating provider as «‘ESG rating provider’ means a legal person whose activities include the issuance, and the publication or distribution, of ESG ratings on a professional basis». A rating provider that wants to operate in the Union must come under one of four routes: authorisation by ESMA, the European Securities and Markets Authority, an equivalence route, an authorisation for endorsement, or recognition. On equivalence the text says «The Commission may adopt an equivalence decision by means of an implementing act», so that route is the Commission's, not ESMA's. ESMA also supervises and fines providers. On entry into force the text says «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union», and the Official Journal header reads «L series 2024/3005 12.12.2024». On application it says «It shall apply from 2 July 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the twentieth day after the publication date 12.12.2024 is 1 January 2025, which matches the first date of the delegation of power in the Regulation, so the Regulation is in force and the rules on providers apply from 2 July 2026, a date now past.

Why this reaches a freight business: the Regulation puts its duties on rating providers, not on the companies they rate, and the text names no freight role, cargo vertical, transport mode or trade lane. *Analytical inference:* the link is indirect and rests on the recitals. The recitals state that «investors, borrowers and issuers increasingly use ESG ratings as part of the process of making informed decisions relating to sustainable investment and financing» and that in the issuer-paid model «undertakings purchase ESG ratings for the purpose of assessing risks and opportunities within their operations». A freight operator therefore meets this Regulation as a buyer of ESG ratings, as a company that is scored by one, or as a supplier whose customers hold a rating of it. The Regulation does not say that a freight business is in any of these roles.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator that is neither an ESG rating provider nor a regulated financial undertaking within the next 30 days. The nearest date in the Regulation, 2 November 2026, falls on small ESG rating providers: «shall notify ESMA in accordance with Article 5 no later than 2 November 2026 if they wish to continue operating in the Union».

- A sustainability reporting lead lists the ESG ratings the business buys or is scored on and, before the next subscription renewal, checks each provider against the ESMA list, because «The register referred to in paragraph 1 shall be publicly accessible on the website of ESMA».
- A customer-facing lead who shows a purchased ESG rating to a customer, at the next questionnaire or tender that cites one, asks the provider for the Annex III link that the provider must attach when it authorises disclosure: «a link to the information referred to in point 1 of Annex III is attached to the ESG rating».

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the register and the link duty stated above; the Regulation does not require the buyer to do either. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that only buys or shows ESG ratings carries any duty under this Regulation.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names these roles: ESG rating providers, users of ESG ratings, rated items and issuers of rated items, regulated financial undertakings, ESMA and the Member State competent authorities. Providers must disclose their minimum information «to users of ESG ratings, rated items and issuers of rated items on an ongoing basis». The complaints route is open to rated items and issuers: «Complaints may be submitted in respect of any of the following: (a) the sources of data used for an individual ESG rating, factual errors and mistakes; (b) the way in which the rating methodology in relation to an individual ESG rating has been applied;».

*Analytical inference:* a freight operator is not one of the named providers. If it is scored by a provider it is a rated item or an issuer of a rated item, and if it buys a rating it is a user. No source here places a freight forwarder, carrier or shipper in any role, so the placement is open. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role a freight business holds for each rating it buys or is scored by, and whether a Member State competent authority or ESMA is its point of contact.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Several implementing steps carry dates, and most are now past. The stored text does not say whether they were delivered, so this brief states the date and the gap.

- ESMA technical standards: «ESMA shall submit the draft regulatory technical standards referred to in the first subparagraph to the Commission by 2 October 2025.» The date has passed; the delivery is not stated.
- ESMA guidelines: ESMA must «issue and update guidelines on the application of the endorsement regime referred to in Article 11 of this Regulation by 2 October 2025». The date has passed; whether they were issued is not stated.
- Supervisory fees: «By 2 January 2026, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 47 to supplement this Regulation by specifying the type of fees». The date has passed; whether the acts were adopted is not stated.
- Delegated acts: the power runs «for a period of five years from 1 January 2025».
- Competent authorities: «By 2 April 2026, each Member State shall designate a competent authority for the purposes of this Regulation.» The date has passed.
- Single access point: «From 1 January 2028, the information referred to in paragraph 1 and in Article 11(3), Article 35(6) and Article 38(1) of this Regulation shall be made accessible on ESAP.»
- Evaluation: the Commission evaluates the Regulation by 2 January 2029, which may bring a legislative proposal.

*Analytical inference:* the sections most likely to change when these steps land are 8, 10 and 11, because they hold the disclosure and application content. A freight operator would see the change in what a provider must publish about its method.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a provider is inside the Regulation is whether it is operating in the Union. The text answers: «ESG rating providers are considered to be operating in the Union in the following cases: (a) for ESG rating providers established in the Union: (i) when they issue and publish their ESG ratings on their website or through other means; or (ii) when they issue and distribute their ESG ratings by subscription or other contractual relationships to regulated financial undertakings in the Union, to undertakings that fall within the scope of Directive 2013/34/EU, to undertakings that fall within the scope of Directive 2004/109/EC, or to Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies or Member State public authorities;». A second question is whether a provider is small: «an ESG rating provider categorised as a small undertaking or as a small group within the meaning of Article 3(2), first subparagraph, or Article 3(5), first subparagraph, respectively, of Directive 2013/34/EU (the ‘small ESG rating provider’)».

*Analytical inference:* both questions concern the provider, not the buyer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a rating that a freight business buys from a provider outside the Union falls in the covered cases.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Authorisation. «Any legal person that wishes to operate as an ESG rating provider in the Union shall be subject to one of the following: (a) an authorisation issued by ESMA as referred to in Article 6; (b) an equivalence decision as referred to in Article 10 and fulfilment of the conditions referred to in that Article; (c) an authorisation for endorsement as referred to in Article 11; (d) a recognition as referred to in Article 12». Scope: «This Regulation applies to ESG ratings issued by ESG rating providers operating in the Union.»

Small providers. An ESG rating provider that is a small undertaking «shall only be subject to Article 15(1), (5) and (7), Articles 23 and 24 and Articles 32 to 37 of this Regulation, provided that it: (a) notifies ESMA of its intention to operate in the Union; and (b) has been registered by ESMA before it starts operating in the Union». The temporary regime ends: «or three years after its registration in accordance with paragraph 1, point (b), of this Article, whichever occurs first, the ESG rating provider shall become subject to all provisions of this Regulation and shall within six months apply for authorisation to operate in the Union».

Disclosure. «ESG rating providers shall disclose on their website, as a minimum, the methodologies, models and key rating assumptions that they use in their ESG rating activities». Providers must also have a complaints route: «ESG rating providers shall have in place and publish on their website procedures for receiving, investigating and retaining records concerning complaints made by users of ESG ratings, by rated items and by issuers of rated items.»

Independence. «ESMA, the Commission or any Member State public authorities shall not interfere with the content of ESG ratings or methodologies.»

Reporting to the public register. «From 1 January 2028, when making public any information referred to in Article 19(1) and Article 23(1) of this Regulation, the ESG rating provider shall submit that information at the same time to the collection body».

Penalties. «Where ESMA finds that an ESG rating provider, or, where applicable, its legal representative, has, intentionally or negligently, infringed this Regulation», and «it shall adopt a decision imposing a fine. The maximum amount of the fine shall be 10 % of the total annual net turnover of the ESG rating provider».

*Analytical inference:* each duty above falls on the provider and so reaches a freight business only through what the provider publishes and how it handles a complaint; no cost to a buyer or to a rated company is stated. The source states no pass-through of fines or fees to a customer. No phase-in is stated in Articles 4, 19 and 36.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these provider duties creates a duty, a right or a liability for a freight business that buys, shows or is scored by an ESG rating.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation covers ESG rating providers, not products sold by a freight business.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Providers apply to ESMA: «shall apply to ESMA for authorisation. 2. An application for authorisation as referred to in paragraph 1 shall contain all of the information listed in Annex I to this Regulation». Providers that were already operating «ESG rating providers which operated in the Union at the date of entry into force of this Regulation shall notify ESMA by 2 August 2026 if they wish to continue operating in the Union and apply for authorisation or recognition in accordance with Title II. In that case, they shall apply for authorisation or recognition within four months of 2 July 2026.» Small providers that were already operating: «shall notify ESMA in accordance with Article 5 no later than 2 November 2026 if they wish to continue operating in the Union. In the absence of such notification by that date, they shall cease their activities.» ESMA decides on a small provider's notice within a set time: «Within 90 working days of receipt of the notification referred to in paragraph 1, point (a), ESMA shall decide whether to register the notifier as a small ESG rating provider.»

The public list: «The register referred to in paragraph 1 shall be publicly accessible on the website of ESMA and shall be updated without delay, as necessary.»

*Analytical inference:* these registration duties fall on providers; the text states none on a buyer or a rated company. The next dated step is 2 November 2026.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text places the operational duties on the provider. A provider must keep a complaints process, and stakeholders can raise concerns: «ESG rating providers shall have in place procedures for receiving reasoned concerns from stakeholders that provide their names and position.» Providers «shall endeavour to reply to the reasoned concerns within 30 working days of receipt thereof», other than small providers. When a provider authorises a user to disclose a rating, «An ESG rating provider shall ensure that when it authorises a user of ESG ratings to disclose an ESG rating, a link to the information referred to in point 1 of Annex III is attached to the ESG rating.»

*Analytical inference:* a business that reuses a purchased rating in its own material should keep the provider's Annex III link with it, and one that is scored should keep a record of the data it wants corrected. The source states no duty on either. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether showing a purchased rating to a customer is a disclosure the provider must authorise.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Regulation excludes some ratings: «This Regulation does not apply to any of the following: (a) private ESG ratings that are not intended for public disclosure or for distribution;» and «(b) ESG ratings issued by regulated financial undertakings in the Union that are used exclusively for internal purposes or for providing in-house or intragroup financial services or products;»

*Analytical inference:* a rating a company builds only for its own use is not what the Regulation targets; the text does not discuss freight uses.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Document date:** 2026-11-01

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation. It sets a framework for ecodesign requirements on products sold in the European Union, creates a digital product passport, and bans the destruction of certain unsold consumer products. It replaces the earlier Ecodesign Directive in the way Article 79 describes (section 14).

How to read it: statements of what the regulation says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation is the Union's rulebook for how physical goods are designed and documented before they can be sold. In its first article it «This Regulation establishes a framework for the setting of ecodesign requirements that products have to comply with to be placed on the market or put into service». It then adds three tools: «This Regulation also establishes a digital product passport, provides for the setting of mandatory green public procurement requirements and creates a framework to prevent unsold consumer products from being destroyed.» «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Its reach is wide: «This Regulation applies to any physical goods that are placed on the market or put into service, including components and intermediate products.» The product-by-product rules do not sit in this text; they come in later Commission acts, so the detailed requirements for a given good depend on whether an act covers it (section 7).

Why it matters to a freight operator: the duties land on the people who bring goods into the Union, who store and ship them, and who clear them through customs. Importers, fulfilment service providers and the customs step each have their own quoted duty (sections 4, 8 and 10). Two dated items are close: the ban on destroying certain unsold goods that began on 19 July 2026, and the end on 31 December 2026 of the transition for a list of product groups (section 14). The regulation sets no freight rate or surcharge.

*Analytical inference:* because the quoted scope covers any physical goods placed on the market, a consignment of goods can fall under it whatever the mode of transport; whether a given consignment is covered depends on a later Commission act for that product group.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the transition for a list of product groups ends on 31 December 2026, less than two months after the date of this document. Quoted in section 14, the earlier Directive keeps applying to those groups only until that date. The steps below come from that date and from the customs and unsold-goods duties.

- A customs-compliance lead, before 31 December 2026, asks each importing client whether any consignment is a product group listed in the section 14 quote (photovoltaic panels, heaters, air conditioners, vacuum cleaners, computers and the other listed groups) and which paperwork regime the client expects to use after that date, because the listed groups are the ones the earlier Directive covers until then.
- A returns and disposal lead, before the next instruction to scrap or dispose of apparel, clothing accessories or footwear for a client, checks the instruction against the ban in section 8 and the carve-outs in section 12, and records the client's stated reason on the job.
- A customs-systems lead adds a field for the unique registration identifier of covered products to import data held for each declaration, so it can be supplied once the registry is operational (section 10).

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation names these parties and gives each its own duty.

- Importers: «Importers shall, with regard to products covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4, only place on the market products that comply with the requirements set out in the applicable delegated acts.»
- Importers or distributors in a manufacturer's place: «Importers or distributors shall be considered manufacturers for the purposes of this Regulation where they: (a) place a product covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4 on the market under their name or trademark»
- Fulfilment service providers: «Fulfilment service providers shall ensure that, for products that they handle that are covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4, the conditions during warehousing, packaging, addressing or dispatching do not jeopardise the products’ compliance with that delegated act.»
- Any person at the customs step: «Any person intending to place a product covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4 under the customs procedure ‘release for free circulation’ shall provide or make available to customs authorities the unique registration identifier of that product referred to in Article 13(5).»

It also names manufacturers, authorised representatives, distributors, dealers, online marketplaces and customs authorities. The regulation names no freight forwarder, carrier or customs broker as such.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted fulfilment duty covers warehousing, packaging, addressing and dispatching, so a logistics business doing those tasks for covered products is in the chain as the text describes; the quoted customs sentence says "any person", so who files the declaration for a covered product is a question the text leaves to the filer's role. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator in a given job is a fulfilment service provider, an importer, a distributor treated as a manufacturer, or the person at the customs step, and which of the quoted duties then apply.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text holds no authoritative guidance document on this regulation beyond the regulation itself; the first working plan and the first acts it requires are listed as events in section 6.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The regulation sets a long list of acts and reviews that will change the analysis. Dates are quoted from the text. Those before the date of this document are stated as past: the captured text does not say whether each was delivered.

- First working plan (date passed): «In the first working plan, which shall be adopted by 19 April 2025, the Commission shall prioritise the following product groups: (a) iron and steel; (b) aluminium; (c) textiles, in particular garments and footwear; (d) furniture, including mattresses; (e) tyres; (f) detergents; (g) paints; (h) lubricants; (i) chemicals;» The groups show which kinds of goods the Commission put first.
- First delegated act (date passed): «The first delegated act referred to in the first subparagraph shall be adopted by 19 July 2025.» Linked: «The first delegated act to be adopted under this Article shall not enter into force before 19 July 2025.»
- First implementing act on disclosure of unsold goods (date passed): «The first such implementing act shall be adopted by 19 July 2025.»
- Cement, if requirements are missing under the construction products Regulation: «Where there is an absence of adequate performance requirements and information requirements concerning the environmental footprint and carbon footprint of cement under the construction products Regulation, the Commission shall set ecodesign requirements for cement in a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4 not earlier than 31 December 2028 and not later than 1 January 2030.»
- Consolidated information on destruction (next date ahead): «By 19 July 2027 and every 36 months thereafter, the Commission shall publish on its website consolidated information on the destruction of unsold consumer products»
- Social sustainability evaluation (date ahead): «By 19 July 2028, the Commission shall evaluate the potential benefits of the inclusion of social sustainability requirements within the scope of this Regulation.»
- First market surveillance report (date ahead): «The first of those reports shall be published by 19 July 2028.»
- Full evaluation of the regulation (date ahead): «By 19 July 2030, and every six years thereafter, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation and of its contribution to the functioning of the internal market»
- Customs interconnection: «That interconnection shall be operational within four years of the date of entry into force of the implementing act referred to in Article 13(5).»

What changes when these arrive: each delegated act for a product group fixes the ecodesign and passport duties for that group, so an importer, fulfilment service provider or customs filer learns which of the section 8 duties bite on a given good only when the act for that group applies. The customs interconnection date depends on an implementing act that carries no date in the captured text. *Analytical inference:* the quoted product-group list orders the Commission's first priorities and does not itself apply any duty to those goods.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: which goods does the regulation actually cover in a given job? The text answers in two steps. The Commission acts product group by group: «The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 72 to supplement this Regulation by setting ecodesign requirements.» The importer, fulfilment and customs duties in section 4 then attach only to a "product covered by a delegated act", as each quoted sentence says.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted wording of those duties rests on a delegated act existing for the product group, so a good outside every delegated act is outside those duties. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular good is covered by a delegated act, which depends on acts that are not in the captured text.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties below apply to products covered by a delegated act or to the unsold goods named; whether and how each applies to a given operator and good is a question for counsel and is not settled here.

**Digital product passport.** «The information requirements shall provide that products can only be placed on the market or put into service if a digital product passport is available in accordance with the applicable delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4 and with Articles 10 and 11.»

**Importer checks.** «Before placing a product covered by a delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4 on the market, importers shall ensure that: (a) the appropriate conformity assessment procedure has been carried out by the manufacturer and that the manufacturer has drawn up the technical documentation; (b) the product is accompanied by the information required under Article 7 and the delegated acts adopted pursuant to Article 4; and (c) a digital product passport is available in accordance with Article 9»

**Preventing destruction.** «Economic operators shall take necessary measures which can reasonably be expected to prevent the need to destroy unsold consumer products.» The ban itself: «From 19 July 2026, the destruction of unsold consumer products as listed in Annex VII shall be prohibited.» Annex VII lists, as groups, «Apparel and clothing accessories» and «Footwear».

**Disclosure of discarded goods.** «Economic operators that discard unsold consumer products directly or have unsold consumer products discarded on their behalf shall disclose: (a) the number and weight of unsold consumer products discarded per year, differentiated per type or category of products;» One option: «Economic operators that are subject to the obligation to publish the sustainability reporting in their management report pursuant to Article 19a or 29a of Directive 2013/34/EU may also include that information in that sustainability reporting.» *Analytical inference:* the disclosure duty sits with the economic operator that discards or has goods discarded on its behalf, so a disposal contractor may be asked for the quoted figures by the operator that owns the goods.

**What is outside the regulation.** «However, it does not apply to: (a) food as defined in Article 2 of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (b) feed as defined in Article 3(4) of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (c) medicinal products as defined in Article 1(2) of Directive 2001/83/EC;» The remaining exclusions, including vehicles, are in section 12.

**Penalties.** «Member States shall at least be able to impose the following penalties in the event of infringements of this Regulation: (a) fines; (b) time-limited exclusion from public procurement procedures.» The captured text states no fine amount; the penalty rules are set by each Member State.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The regulation sets up a registry and ties it to customs. The Commission's side: «By 19 July 2026, the Commission shall set up a digital registry (the ‘registry’) which stores in a secure manner at least the unique identifiers.» The economic operator's side: «The economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service shall upload, in the registry, the data referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.» The customs side: «Customs authorities may release a product for free circulation only after having verified as a minimum that the unique registration identifier referred to in Article 13(5) and the commodity code provided or made available to them correspond to the data stored in the registry.»

What this means in practice: once the registry is operational, a covered product cannot be released for free circulation unless the identifier the operator received matches the data stored in the registry. The quoted first sentence gives 19 July 2026 as the date the Commission was to set the registry up; the captured text does not say whether it did, and the quoted customs rule starts only when the registry is operational.

*Analytical inference:* the customs sentence rests on the registry being operational and on a verification step done electronically, so the practical change for a filer is a data field at the declaration, not a new certificate. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the filer of a customs declaration for a covered product has a duty of its own under the customs sentence quoted in section 4, or the duty sits only with the importer.

This paragraph shall apply to medium-sized enterprises from 19 July 2030.» Vehicles are carved out for the aspects other Union acts already cover: «(h) vehicles as referred to in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) No 167/2013, in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 and in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/858, in respect of those product aspects for which requirements are set under sector-specific Union legislative acts applicable to those vehicles» For destruction, further derogations are to come: «derogations from the prohibition of destruction of unsold consumer products listed in Annex VII where it is appropriate for any of the following reasons: (a) health, hygiene and safety reasons;» The text lists more reasons after that one.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 13 June 2024: the regulation is adopted: «Done at Brussels, 13 June 2024.»
- Twentieth day after publication: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»
- 18 July 2024: «Directive 2009/125/EC is repealed with effect from 18 July 2024» and the delegation of power to the Commission runs «shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 18 July 2024». The text lists exceptions to the repeal, which continue until the dates below.
- 19 April 2025 (passed): the first working plan fell due (section 6); the captured text does not say whether it was adopted.
- 19 July 2025 (passed): the first delegated act and the first implementing act on unsold goods fell due (section 6); the captured text does not say whether they were adopted.
- 19 July 2026 (passed): the Commission's registry fell due (section 10) and the destruction ban began (section 8); the captured text does not say whether the registry was set up.
- 31 December 2026: «(i) until 31 December 2026, as regards photovoltaic panels, space and combination heaters, water heaters, solid fuel local space heaters, air conditioners including air-to-air heat pumps and comfort fans, solid fuel boilers, air heating and cooling products, ventilation units, vacuum cleaners, cooking appliances, water pumps, industrial fans, circulators, external power supplies, computers, servers and data storage products, power transformers, professional refrigeration equipment and imaging equipment;»
- 19 July 2027: the Commission's consolidated information on destruction is due (section 6).
- 19 July 2028: the social sustainability evaluation and the first market surveillance report are due (section 6).
- 31 December 2028: the earliest date for the cement act (section 6).
- 1 January 2030: the latest date for the cement act (section 6).
- 19 July 2030: the full evaluation falls due, and medium-sized businesses come under the ban and disclosure sentences (sections 6 and 12).
- 31 December 2030: «(ii) until 31 December 2030, as regards products regulated by implementing measures that are adopted pursuant to Article 15 of Directive 2009/125/EC, however only insofar as amendments are necessary to address technical issues with regard to those implementing measures;»

What each date changes: the 2024 dates end the old Directive except for the listed products and start the Commission's rule-making power; the 2025 dates start the working plan and the first acts; the 2026 dates bring the registry, the ban and the end of the first transition; the 2028 to 2030 dates bring reports, evaluations and the second transition end.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

**Document date:** 2026-11-01

This document covers Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485 of 27 June 2023, an act of the European Union that changes the technical rules deciding whether an economic activity counts as environmentally sustainable under the Taxonomy framework of Regulation (EU) 2020/852. It amends Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 and was published in the Official Journal of the European Union. It applies across the Union.

How to read it: statements of what the act says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here. The act sets technical criteria and no price; the review points still to come are in section 6.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2485 is a European Commission act that adds and rewrites technical screening criteria. The base act it amends does this: «Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139 ( 3 ) establishes the technical screening criteria for determining the conditions under which a specific economic activity qualifies as contributing substantially to climate change mitigation or climate change adaptation.» The Commission explains where freight sits in the new text: «The additional economic activities that contribute substantially to climate change mitigation cover largely the transport sector and its value chain.»

For a freight operator the practical meaning is a classification test. Vessels, aircraft, road vehicles and transhipment terminals are tested against these criteria to decide whether the activity can be called environmentally sustainable in financial products and company disclosures. The act sets no charge on a shipment. Its reach is the money and reporting that sit behind the operators of those vessels, aircraft and vehicles; the criteria are listed in section 8 by mode (sea, air, road, and rail and water transhipment).

Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* because the quoted recital says the added activities cover largely the transport sector and its value chain, the operator of a vessel, aircraft or road vehicle that a freight operator uses may be asked to show its assets against these criteria; the act itself does not say that any freight service is rated, so what a client asks of a freight operator depends on that client's own financial products and reports.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: nothing in this act falls due for a freight operator within 30 days. One dated condition sits close, on 11 December 2026, and it concerns aircraft manufacturers; the two steps below follow from it and from the way the criteria are used.

- A sustainability-reporting lead, when a client or financier asks whether a sea, air, road, or rail and water transhipment service is aligned with the Taxonomy, tests the carrier's asset against the matching criteria in section 8 and records which criterion it meets and which evidence the carrier supplied.
- An air freight procurement lead, before 11 December 2026, asks each aircraft manufacturer in a purchase discussion whether the aircraft's CO 2 margin rests on a certificate or on the declaration that depends on certification by that date (the text is in section 14).

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The act names the parties it reaches through the base Taxonomy rules: «That Regulation applies to measures adopted by the Union or by Member States that set out requirements for financial market participants or issuers in respect of financial products or corporate bonds that are made available as environmentally sustainable» «Economic operators or public authorities that are not covered by Regulation (EU) 2020/852 may also apply that Regulation on a voluntary basis.»

The act names no freight forwarder, customs broker or shipper, and no carrier class. It does name the aircraft manufacturer, which delivers a declaration (section 14), and the operators who assess and document their use of certain substances (section 8). Everything else in the compliance chain is reached through the financial products and company reports that use the criteria.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted scope sentence rests on financial market participants, issuers and undertakings that publish a non-financial statement, so a freight operator is in the chain as a company that is itself such an undertaking, as a business that applies the Taxonomy voluntarily, or as a counterparty whose carrier or client supplies Taxonomy data. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the freight operator is itself an undertaking subject to the non-financial statement obligation named in the quoted scope sentence, and in which role it would use these criteria.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The act points to reviews and publications still to come. Each is stated as the act states it, with no date beyond what is quoted.

- Transitional activities: «the technical screening criteria for transitional activities should be reviewed every three years as set out Article 19(5) of Regulation (EU) 2020/852»
- Aircraft manufacturing: «the technical screening criteria for aircraft manufacturing should be applicable until 2032, and by that date those technical screening criteria should be reviewed»
- Sustainable aviation fuel level: «the level of the use or blending of sustainable aviation fuels represented in the technical screening criteria should be reviewed every three years»
- Replacement ratio: «The Commission, with support of the European Union Aviation Safety Agency established by Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 8 ) , may publish the replacement ratio to support the economic operators in their disclosures.»
- Chemicals exceptions: «The Commission will review the exceptions from the prohibition from manufacturing, placing on the market or use of the substances referred to in point (f) once it will have published horizontal principles on essential use of chemicals.»

What changes when these arrive: a review of the transitional criteria or of the aviation fuel level can move the thresholds in section 8 for air operators and aircraft makers; the replacement ratio, if published, is a figure the aircraft criteria use. *Analytical inference:* the review wording is the Commission's stated expectation in the recitals, and the captured text names no review date other than the year quoted for aircraft manufacturing.

## 7. Threshold Questions

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The act amends Annex I and Annex II to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2139. The freight-relevant criteria the captured text sets are below, by mode. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which criteria apply to a given vessel, aircraft, vehicle or terminal, and whether a given asset meets them, is a question for counsel and the asset's certifier and is not settled here.

**Sea freight: greenhouse gas intensity of ship energy.** For ships that cannot meet the first criterion, the amended text sets a falling limit: «the yearly average greenhouse gas intensity of the energy used on-board by a ship during a reporting period *4 does not exceed the following limits: (a) 76,4 g CO 2 e/MJ from 1 January 2026 until 31 December 2029; (b) 61,1 g CO 2 e/MJ from 1 January 2030 until 31 December 2034; (c) 45,8 g CO 2 e/MJ from 1 January 2035 until 31 December 2039; (d) 30,6 g CO 2 e/MJ from 1 January 2040 until 31 December 2044; (e) 15,3 g CO 2 e/MJ from 1 January 2045.» *Analytical inference:* the quoted limits fall in steps, so the same ship energy intensity can meet the limit for one period and miss the next. Recital 12 ties the update to maritime freight and passenger transport.

**Sea freight: design efficiency.** «where technologically and economically not feasible to comply with point (a), from 1 January 2026, the vessels that are able to run on zero direct (tailpipe) CO 2 emission fuels or on fuels from renewable sources *1 have an attained Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) value equivalent to reducing the EEDI reference line by at least 20 percentage points below the EEDI requirements applicable on 1 April 2022 *2 , and: (a) are able to plug-in at berth» *Analytical inference:* being able to plug in at berth is part of the quoted test for those vessels.

**Air freight: sustainable aviation fuel share.** «(e) the aircraft operated with a minimum share of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF), corresponding to 5 % SAF in 2022, with the percentage of SAF increasing by 2 percentage points annually thereafter.» For later years: «(d) from 1 January 2030, the aircraft meeting technical screening criteria specified in points (b) or (c) above and operated with a minimum share of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF), corresponding to 15 % in 2030 and increased by 2 percentage points annually thereafter»

**Aircraft makers: CO 2 margin.** For manufacturers, one margin is: «(i) having maximum take-off mass greater than 5,7 t and less than or equal to 60 t and a certified metric value of CO 2 emissions of at least 11 % less than the New Type limit of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) standard» Where a compliant aircraft is delivered and another is withdrawn: «(i) permanently withdrawn from use within 6 months of delivery of the compliant aircraft in which case, the replacement ratio does not apply»

**Road freight: tyres and engines.** «For road vehicles of categories M and N, tyres comply with external rolling noise requirements in the highest populated class and with Rolling Resistance Coefficient (influencing the vehicle energy efficiency) in the highest two populated classes as set out in Regulation (EU) 2020/740» «Vehicles comply with the requirements of the most recent applicable stage of the Euro VI heavy duty emission type-approval *1 set out in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 595/2009.»

**Transhipment infrastructure.** «(d) the infrastructure and installations are dedicated to transhipping freight with rail and water transport: terminal infrastructure and superstructures for loading, unloading and transhipment of goods.»

**Chemicals, all activities.** The no-significant-harm text on chemicals is rewritten: «substances, whether on their own, or in mixtures or in an article, in a concentration above 0,1 % weight by weight (w/w), and meeting the criteria laid down in Article 57 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 and that were identified in accordance with Article 59(1) of that Regulation for a period of at least eighteen months, except if it is assessed and documented by the operators that no other suitable alternative substances or technologies are available on the market, and that they are used under controlled conditions»

**Penalty.** No penalty: the instrument text read sets technical screening criteria and a date of application and states no penalty, fine, sanction or enforcement consequence of its own.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The act creates no registration. Its reporting link is one sentence about timing: «To synchronise the application of this Regulation with the reporting under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/2178 ( 15 ) , this Regulation should apply from 1 January 2024, with the exception of the amendment to point (g) of Appendix C.»

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the captured text sets no system for a freight operator to build. Where an operator wants Taxonomy evidence from air carriers, the data to ask for is set by this sentence: «Operators calculate compliance as the ratio of the quantity (expressed in tonnes) of SAF purchased at the fleet level divided by the total aviation fuel used by the compliant aircraft multiplied by 100.»

*Analytical inference:* the calculation is stated for the operators of aircraft at fleet level, so a freight operator reads the carrier's figure and does not compute it; the quoted sentence rests on the operators calculating the ratio.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 27 June 2023: the act is adopted: «Done at Brussels, 27 June 2023.»
- 1 January 2024: the act applies: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 January 2024.»
- 1 January 2025: «However, point (28) of Annex I and point (26) of Annex II shall apply from 1 January 2025.» Recital 24 ties the later date to the amendment to point (g) of Appendix C and says it gives undertakings time to comply (see section 8).
- 1 January 2026: the ship criteria in section 8 begin to count from this date.
- 11 December 2026: aircraft manufacturers' declaration of CO 2 performance: «the aircraft manufacturer shall deliver a declaration that the aircraft meets the required level of performance and margins of improvement with the condition that the aircraft is certified by 11 December 2026»
- 31 December 2027: «(b) until 31 December 2027, the aircraft, other than produced for private or commercial business aviation, meeting the margins specified below» The next aircraft step follows: «(c) from 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2032, the aircraft meeting the technical screening criteria set out in point (b) of this subsection that is certified to operate on 100 % blend of sustainable aviation fuels.»
- 1 January 2030: the higher sustainable aviation fuel share in section 8 begins.

Reference date inside the criteria, for ships: the text refers to «the Energy Efficiency Index of Existing Ships ( 10 ) that entered into force on 1 January 2023». That date belongs to the ship efficiency index the criteria are aligned to and is not a step of this act.

What each date changes: the application date moves the criteria into use for reporting; the 2025 date moves the one chemicals point; the 2026 ship dates start the greenhouse gas intensity limits; the 11 December 2026 date is the date the declaration's condition names for certification of the aircraft; the 2027 and 2028 dates change which aircraft test covers manufacturers.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2022/2387 of 30 August 2022 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/655 as regards the adaptation of the provisions on monitoring of gaseous pollutant emissions from in-service internal combustion engines installed in non-road mobile machinery to include engines with power of less than 56 kW and more than 560 kW», an amendment to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/655, the European Union rules on monitoring exhaust emissions of engines while they are in use in non-road mobile machinery. Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» The text ends «Done at Brussels, 30 August 2022.» Statements of what the Regulation requires come from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Engine makers must test a sample of their engines while those engines work in machinery, to measure the emissions of non-road mobile machinery in actual operation. This Regulation widens that in-service monitoring to engines below 56 kW and above 560 kW and resets its deadlines. It says why: «Taking into account the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact on the manufacturers’ ability to perform in-service monitoring tests, in order to provide sufficient time to manufacturers to perform the tests and to the Commission to assess the test results and produce the report to the European Parliament and the Council as required under Regulation (EU) 2016/1628, it is necessary to modify the deadlines for submitting in-service monitoring test reports». The scope clause reads «This Regulation applies to monitoring of the gaseous pollutant emissions from the following categories of in-service engines of emission Stage V installed in non-road mobile machinery regardless of when the EU type-approval for those engines was granted:» The categories include «(c) IWP and IWA (all sub-categories); (d) RLL and RLR (all sub-categories);», and one clause of the text refers to an engine «installed in an inland waterway vessel or a railway vehicle». The text does not say what the codes IWP, IWA, RLL and RLR stand for. The Regulation takes effect as the text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* the engines the text mentions as installed in an inland waterway vessel or a railway vehicle are the ones a freight business is most likely to run, and the codes IWP, IWA, RLL and RLR may denote such engines, but the text does not say so. The duty is on the engine manufacturer, not on the fleet owner, and the text names no freight role, trade lane or cargo vertical. What the owner meets is a possible request to make a machine available for testing: the text says the plan lists the «the list of particular engine(s) and non-road mobile machinery selected is completed or revised», but does not say how the manufacturer gets access to a machine.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest date in the text is a manufacturer's: «Test reports shall be submitted to the approval authority by 26 December 2026.»

- A fleet technical lead lists the engines in its own inland waterway vessels, railway vehicles and other machinery and, before that date, asks each engine maker whether the engine falls in the categories of Article 2(1) and whether it is selected for in-service testing.
- A purchasing lead adds to the next engine or machine purchase terms a question on whether the engine is in an in-service monitoring group and what access the maker needs.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the plan clause quoted above and on the categories in section 2; the Regulation does not require the fleet owner to do either. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any duty or cost of in-service testing can fall on the owner of the machine.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the engine manufacturer, the approval authority and the Commission. It also mentions the machinery user: «the non-road mobile machinery operator is clearly notified of that malfunction by the on-board diagnostics system». The authority in charge is set by who approved the engine: «The approval authority ensuring the compliance with this Regulation shall be either: a) the approval authority that granted the type-approval of the engine type or engine family».

*Analytical inference:* a freight operator holding vessels, rail vehicles or machines would be the machinery operator, who is named only for malfunction warnings. No source here names a forwarder, carrier or shipper. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an operator that owns the machine is a party to the manufacturer's test plan.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets one recurring event and refers to one report. The Commission side: «the Commission shall, every 5 years, in cooperation with manufacturers, conduct a pilot programme involving the most recent engine types», for the engines outside the monitoring annex. The report: the Commission needs time to «produce the report to the European Parliament and the Council as required under Regulation (EU) 2016/1628». The date of that report is not stated.

*Analytical inference:* the sections most likely to change are 7 and 8, if the pilot programme or the report leads to new test rules. The text states no date for either.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Which engines are inside the monitoring rules decides everything. The text covers the categories of Article 2(1). It keeps the existing arrangement for mid-size engines: «The amendments set out in this Regulation should not influence the monitoring of gaseous pollutant emissions from in-service internal combustion engines with power between 56 kW and 560 kW». For two groups the testing annex is switched off: «For those engines referred to in Article 2(1), points (g) and (h): (i) the Annex to this Regulation shall not apply.».

*Analytical inference:* an engine below 56 kW or above 560 kW in a listed category is newly in scope. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular engine category in a fleet falls under points (a) to (h).

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «This Regulation applies to monitoring of the gaseous pollutant emissions from the following categories of in-service engines of emission Stage V».

Initial plan. «The manufacturer shall submit the initial plan for monitoring each ISM Group to the approval authority within: (a) for ISM Group A, one month of the start of production of any engine type or engine family within the ISM Group; (b) for any other ISM Group, the later date of the following: (i) 26 June 2023; (ii) 1 month after the start of production of any engine type or engine family within the ISM Group.»

Testing by service accumulation, for the first group of engines. «2.6.1.1.1. Testing 9 engines from the ISM group with an accumulated service of less than a % of the EDP, in accordance with Table 2. Test results shall be submitted to the approval authority by 26 December 2024.» «Testing 9 engines from the ISM group with an accumulated service higher than b % of the EDP, in accordance with Table 2. Test reports shall be submitted to the approval authority by 26 December 2026.» Where engines with the needed service are not available the approval authority can accept less, but only on conditions: «the approval authority may permit testing of engines under this point with an accumulated service between 2 times a % and b % of the EDP, subject to the manufacturer providing robust evidence that they have selected engines with the highest available service accumulation».

Testing over four years. «Every manufacturer shall test an average of nine engines per year from the ISM group during 4 consecutive years.» «The test results of the first nine engines shall be submitted not later than 24 months after the first engine was installed in non-road mobile machinery and not later than 30 months after starting the production of an approved engine type or engine family within the ISM group.»

Small manufacturers. «manufacturers producing a total between 25 and 50 engines per year for the Union market across all families in a given ISM group shall submit either: (i) one engine test results with an accumulated service between c % and d % of EDP as defined in Table 3 by 26 December 2025». Smaller still: «manufacturers producing a total of fewer than 25 engines per year for the EU market across all families in a given ISM group need not submit any engine test unless the production exceeds 35 engines in a two-year rolling period».

Engine data and flow measurement. An engine without the needed data link is not eligible: «shall not be eligible for in-service monitoring test, and an alternative engine shall be selected». For engines in inland waterway vessels or railway vehicles an exhaust flow meter can be omitted: «the engine to be tested is of a reference power greater than 560 kW or is installed in an inland waterway vessel or a railway vehicle and the manufacturer demonstrates to the approval authority that installation of an EFM is impractical due to either the size or location of the exhaust on the NRMM».

*Analytical inference:* the cost of the tests falls on the manufacturers; the source states no pass-through to machine buyers, so none is asserted. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the testing duties above create any obligation for the owner of an engine selected for testing.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets duties for engine manufacturers, not for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Manufacturers report to the approval authority. The plan: «Manufacturers shall submit to the approval authority an updated plan for monitoring in-service engines whenever the list of engine families in the ISM Group changes». The test reports: «Test reports shall be submitted to the approval authority every year for the tests that have been performed.»

*Analytical inference:* these reports go from manufacturer to approval authority; the text states no filing by a machine owner.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text places the operating steps on the manufacturer. During a test, a data link records the engine: «a data logger shall be connected with the engine ECU to record the available engine parameters».

*Analytical inference:* a machine owner whose machine is used for a test would see a data logger fitted to the engine and a test run on normal work; the text does not state how long a run lasts for the owner or who covers the downtime. *Legal Confirmation Required:* who bears the cost and downtime of a test on a machine in service.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Engines approved before the change are protected: «EU type-approvals of an engine type or engine family approved in accordance with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/655 before the day of entry into force of this Regulation remain valid». A second carve-out: «EU type-approvals of an engine type or engine family approved in accordance with this Regulation before 26 December 2022 shall not be required to be revised or extended as a result of the testing carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Annex.»

*Analytical inference:* an engine type approved before these dates is not forced into a revised approval by the test results, which limits what the tests can change for fleets already built.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 30 August 2022: Regulation adopted at Brussels
- 26 December 2022: type-approvals granted before this date need not be revised (in force)
- 26 June 2023: for groups other than the first, the initial plan is due by the later of this date and one month after production starts (date passed)
- 26 December 2024: first test results due under the service-accumulation schemes, and the earliest limit for the four-year scheme of groups B, F, G, J, K, L, M and N (date passed)
- 26 December 2025: small manufacturers with 25 to 50 engines submit one engine test (date passed)
- 26 December 2026: test reports for engines with higher service accumulation due to the approval authority

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2025/2551 of 20 November 2025 supplementing Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council by specifying the conditions for granting accreditation to verifiers, for the control and oversight of accredited verifiers, for the withdrawal of accreditation and for mutual recognition and peer evaluation of accreditation bodies», the European Union rules on who may verify the emissions data behind the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

CBAM requires the emissions embedded in certain imported goods to be reported, and the recitals say when a check by an outside party is needed: «where embedded emissions in goods imported into the customs territory of the Union from 2026 are determined based on actual values, they are to be verified by a verifier». This Regulation sets how those outside checkers, called verifiers, are accredited. A verifier is «‘verifier’ means a legal person carrying out verification activities pursuant to this Regulation and accredited by a national accreditation body for the purpose of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 at the time a verification report is issued». The accreditors are national bodies: «national accreditation bodies, as appointed by each Member State pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) , are to accredit verifiers». This Regulation enters into force and applies as the text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . This Regulation shall apply from 1 January 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is not an accredited verifier, but the goods it carries and the customs filings it supports may rely on a verified emissions report. The Regulation decides who is allowed to produce that report and how their work is supervised. The text names no importer, declarant, forwarder, carrier or trade lane.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest date in the text is the recurring verifier duty: «By 15 November of each year, verifiers shall send the following information covering the next calendar year to the national accreditation body that has accredited them». The next 15 November falls in two weeks. The registry date comes after it: «From 1 January 2027, the verifier shall issue the verification report in the CBAM registry.»

- A customs compliance lead asks each client that imports goods in the CBAM activity groups of Annex I, before the client's next declaration, whether the emissions report for its non-EU supplier's installation was checked by an accredited verifier.
- A client-service lead notes in client files that from 1 January 2027 a verification report is issued in the CBAM registry and, where the operator is registered, transmitted to the operator there; the text does not say whether anyone else receives it: «Where the operator is registered in the CBAM registry pursuant to Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956, the verification report shall be transmitted to the operator via the CBAM registry.»

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the verification and registry rules above; the Regulation requires neither of a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder or customs broker that files for a client has any duty to check a verifier's accreditation.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names applicants and verifiers, national accreditation bodies, competent authorities, the Commission and the operator of the installation. Where to apply: «An applicant that is established under the national law of a Member State shall request the national accreditation body of that Member State to grant accreditation in accordance with this Regulation.». Recognition across borders: «Member States and competent authorities shall recognise the equivalence of the services delivered by those national accreditation bodies which have successfully undergone peer evaluation in accordance with Article 24.». Suspension is also possible at the verifier's own request: «The national accreditation body shall suspend or withdraw an accreditation or reduce the scope of accreditation of a verifier, where the verifier so requests.»

*Analytical inference:* the chain runs from the installation operator to the verifier, to the national accreditation body, to the competent authority and the Commission through the CBAM registry. A freight business is not placed in it by the text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party in a client's import chain receives a verification report and who may rely on it.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis
