## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Two dated steps lie ahead. The nearer is the recurring one, by 15 November of each year, which is set out in section 10. The other is: «From 1 January 2027, the verifier shall issue the verification report in the CBAM registry.» A second concerns the bodies that accredit: «a national accreditation body has successfully undergone a peer evaluation in the field of verification before 1 January 2026, the national accreditation body shall be exempted from undergoing a new peer evaluation from that date if it can demonstrate conformity with this Regulation».

*Analytical inference:* from 1 January 2027 the verifier issues the report in the registry; the text sends it to the operator and does not say who else sees it. The peer evaluation steps decide whether other Member States accept a verifier's certificate. The text states no date for a new peer evaluation.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a verifier may check a given installation is whether the installation's goods fall in an accredited activity group: «Requests for accreditation shall cover one or more CBAM activities groups listed in Annex I.». The Annex lists the groups, including «II Hydrogen Ammonia 1a, 1b, 8, 98 III Nitric acid 1a, 1b, 9, 98 IV Urea Mixed fertilisers 1a, 1b, 98 V Sintered ore Pig iron DRI (direct reduced iron) Crude steel» and «VII Unwrought aluminium 1a, 1b, 4, 5, 98 VIII Iron or steel products Aluminium products 1a, 1b, 4, 98», and «LI Electricity imported into the customs territory of the Union».

*Analytical inference:* a verifier accredited for one group may not be accredited for another, so a client importing several goods categories may need more than one verifier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which Annex I group covers a client's goods and which verifier holds that group.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Assessment. «The national accreditation body shall assess whether the legal person applying for accreditation (‘the applicant’) or the verifier: (a) meets the competence requirements laid down in Section 1 of Annex II»

Certificate and reassessment. «The accreditation certificate shall be valid for a period not exceeding five years from the date on which the national accreditation body has issued it.» «Before the expiry of an accreditation certificate which it has issued, the national accreditation body shall reassess the verifier in question».

Surveillance. «The national accreditation body shall carry out the first surveillance of a verifier in accordance with paragraph 1 within 12 months of the date on which its accreditation certificate was issued.»

Recognition between Member States. «Where a national accreditation body has not undergone the complete peer evaluation process, Member States shall accept the accreditation certificates and recognise the verification reports of verifiers accredited by that national accreditation body provided that» The peer evaluation exemption: «the national accreditation body shall be exempted from undergoing a new peer evaluation from that date if it can demonstrate conformity with this Regulation».

Reports. «From 1 January 2027, the verifier shall issue the verification report in the CBAM registry.»

Consequences for a verifier. «the national accreditation body may suspend or withdraw an accreditation or reduce the scope of accreditation of a verifier, where the verifier does not meet the requirements set out in this Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2023/956, or in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2546». And: «The national accreditation body shall withdraw an accreditation of a verifier where: (a) the verifier has failed to remedy the shortcomings that constituted the grounds for a decision to suspend the accreditation; (b) a member of the management of the verifier, or a member of the verifier’s staff involved in verification activities under Regulation (EU) 2023/956, has been found guilty of fraud».

*Analytical inference:* all duties above fall on national accreditation bodies and verifiers. The source states no pass-through of verifier costs to importers, so none is asserted. No phase-in is stated in Articles 6 to 9.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client that relies on a report from a verifier whose accreditation is later suspended or withdrawn must redo the verification.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets accreditation rules for verifiers, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Verifiers report to their accreditor each year: «By 15 November of each year, verifiers shall send the following information covering the next calendar year to the national accreditation body that has accredited them». The report lists «the name and identification information of the operators whose emissions reports are subject to its verification, and the identification of the installations». Changes follow: «Verifiers shall notify the national accreditation body of any significant changes that might affect their accreditation concerning any aspect of their status or operation, without delay.». Where the operator is outside the registry: «Where the operator is not registered in the CBAM registry, the verifier shall export and transmit the verification report in its original standard software format to the operator via other means.»

*Analytical inference:* these duties fall on verifiers; the text states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text places the operating work on verifiers: «The verifier shall establish, document, implement and maintain a competence process to ensure that all personnel entrusted with verification activities are competent for the tasks that are allocated to them.».

*Analytical inference:* a client that depends on verification needs a verifier accredited for the activity group of its goods under Annex I. The text states no lead time for a verification.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Two easements are stated. Verifiers already accredited under the EU Emissions Trading System route can extend: «verifiers that are already accredited for a relevant group of activities under the EU ETS pursuant to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/2067 ( 5 ) should be able to apply for an extension of the scope of their accreditation». Verifiers outside the Union can apply: «it should be possible for a legal person not established in a Member State to apply for accreditation with any national accreditation body».

*Analytical inference:* this widens the pool of verifiers for goods made outside the Union, which affects how many verifiers a client can choose from. The text states no number of verifiers.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) (No. 2) Order 2025 Made 5th February 2025 Laid before Parliament 12th February 2025 Laid before the Northern Ireland Assembly 12th February 2025 Laid before the Scottish Parliament 12th February 2025 Laid before Senedd Cymru 12th February 2025 Coming into force 31st March 2025», an Order that changes the rules of the United Kingdom Emissions Trading Scheme, the system under which industrial installations hold and surrender allowances for their greenhouse gas emissions. Its jurisdiction is the whole of the United Kingdom: «This Order extends to the whole of the United Kingdom.» What the Order requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The scheme works this way: «Operators of certain industrial installations are required to monitor, submit verified reports on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions each scheme year.» Some of those allowances are given free: «Allowances are sold at auction, but some operators of installations and aircraft operators receive an allocation of allowances free of charge for each scheme year.» This Order changes how free allowances are given for 2026 and afterwards. The Order enters into force on the date the text states: «This Order comes into force on 31st March 2025.»

*Analytical inference:* the Order is a rule change between the UK Government, the regulator and installation operators, so a freight business meets it indirectly. Its allowance costs, if they move, would reach a freight business only through the price a UK industrial customer or supplier charges, and the text states no such pass-through. The text mentions aircraft operators only in the free-allocation sentence above and in the heading «Article 12 amended (aircraft operator: change in regulator)», and it names no freight role, cargo vertical, trade lane or transport mode.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator that is not an installation operator within the next 30 days. The nearest date in the text falls on one group of installation operators: «the operator must apply for a greenhouse gas emissions permit and comply with the conditions of the permit from 1st January 2027».

- A carbon cost lead lists the UK industrial customers and suppliers of the business and, at the next price or contract review, asks each whether its installation is in the main scheme, in the hospital and small emitter scheme, or in the ultra-small emitter scheme.
- A pricing lead notes beside each UK allowance-linked cost claim from a supplier whether the installation received free allocation, since the Order sets that out for 2026 and for 2027 to 2030.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the scheme structure the Order amends; the Order does not require them of a non-installation business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that owns or operates an installation covered by the scheme falls under Part 2 of the Order.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Order's duties are between the regulator, the UK ETS authority and installation operators. For example: «The regulator must— (a) calculate the preliminary and final annual number of allowances to be allocated in respect of each sub-installation of the installation for the 2026 scheme year;». The text also changes the rules for another group of scheme participants: «Article 12 amended (aircraft operator: change in regulator)».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is not named in the chain. It would be an operator only if it runs an installation, and an aircraft operator only if the scheme counts it as one. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of the business's own sites or aircraft operations fall in the scheme.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The Order's explanatory note, which the page marks as not part of the Order, describes the change: «The process for “incumbent” installations to apply for free allocation in the 2027-2030 allocation period consists of two stages, to be completed between 1 April-30 June 2025 and 1 April-30 June 2026». It adds: «During the first stage, operators are required to submit data.». It also states the expected effect: «No impact assessment has been produced for this instrument as no, or no significant, impact on the private, voluntary or public sector is foreseen.»

*Analytical inference:* the note says no significant impact on the private sector is foreseen, which supports reading the Order as an administrative reset of free allocation timing, not a new cost on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether that statement covers a business that buys goods from UK installations.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Order changes dates in the allocation process. The allocation table for the 2026 allocation period had to be published «The UK ETS authority must publish the allocation table for the 2026 allocation period as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2026.» The table for the 2027-2030 allocation period moves to a later date: «for “28th February 2026” substitute “1st January 2027”».

*Analytical inference:* from that later date, installations and the market can see the allowances allocated for 2027 to 2030. The text does not say what an allocation table shows for any one industry.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides who gets free allocation in 2026 is whether an installation is a 2026 incumbent: «An installation is a “2026 incumbent” if— (a) the installation is either— (i) an FA installation for the 2021-2025 allocation period( 5 ); or (ii) an installation other than an FA installation for the 2021-2025 allocation period whose operator completes the first stage of an Article 4 application; (b) the installation is not included in the hospital and small emitter list for 2026-2030 or the ultra-small emitter list for 2026-2030; (c) the operator has not given a renunciation notice under Article 24 of the Free Allocation Regulation in respect of the installation as a whole; and (d) the operator does not give a renunciation notice under article 9 of this Order on or before 30th June 2025». Eligibility for the ultra-small emitter scheme was widened: «installations that began operating between 2 January 2021 and 1 January 2024 are eligible to be in the USE scheme».

*Analytical inference:* both questions concern installations. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an installation that a freight business uses or supplies is a 2026 incumbent.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Type 1 incumbents. «This article applies to an installation that is a type 1 2026 incumbent after the question of whether any adjustment to free allocation under the Activity Level Changes Regulation». The 2026 figure follows the 2025 one: «the preliminary annual number of allowances to be allocated in respect of a sub-installation for the 2026 scheme year is the same as the preliminary annual number of allowances to be allocated in respect of the sub-installation for the 2025 scheme year».

Type 2 incumbents. «The regulator must determine, in accordance with Article 15 of the Free Allocation Regulation, the historical activity level of each sub-installation of the installation on the basis of the baseline data report and verification report submitted as part of the first stage of the Article 4 application».

Industry cap. If allocations exceed the cap, «exceeds 31,623,876 (industry cap for 2026 scheme year( 7 )), the difference must be allocated from the flexible reserve».

Renunciation. «The operator of the following installations may renounce free allocation in the 2026 allocation period by giving notice (a “renunciation notice”) to the regulator»

Lime benchmark. For 2026: «the product benchmark for lime were 0.798 (and not 0.725)».

Wording changes. «Except as provided in paragraph (7), for “2026-2030 allocation period” in each place» A national security carve-out is added: «This paragraph is subject to article 75C (national security).»

*Analytical inference:* each duty falls on the regulator or the installation operator; the source states no cost to a buyer of the installation's goods. No phase-in is stated in Articles 6 to 10.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these allocation rules creates a duty, right or cost for a freight business that is not an installation operator.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 8.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Order sets scheme rules for installation operators, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Operators notify the regulator and the regulator passes notices on: «The regulator must notify the UK ETS authority of each renunciation notice given.» The regulator also gives notices on status: «The regulator must, as soon as reasonably practicable, give a notice to the operator stating that— (a) the installation is not an ultra-small emitter for the 2027 scheme year;» The Order also requires more published information on allowance transfers: «(c) the number of allowances transferred; (d) which one of the following categories the transfer falls into—»

*Analytical inference:* these duties fall on the regulator and installation operators; none is stated for a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Order places the data work on installation operators. «During the first stage, operators are required to submit data. During the second stage, operators are required to confirm that they wish the application to proceed».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that is not an installation operator builds nothing for this Order. Both stages have closed: the first ran to the end of June 2025 and the second to the end of June 2026, per the note's stated windows (1 April-30 June 2025 and 1 April-30 June 2026). A UK site that is an installation had to submit data in the first stage and confirm in the second; the text does not say how many sites did.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Installations in the smaller schemes are treated differently: «Installations that are in either the HSE or USE scheme for 2026-2030 will receive no free allocation in the 2026 allocation period, but operators may opt to join the main scheme for the 2027-2030 allocation period and receive free allocation for that allocation period in the event of a successful application for free allocation». An ultra-small emitter could leave that status, but the window has passed: the operator «notifies the regulator on or before 30th June 2026 as part of the second stage of an application for free allocation in the 2027-2030 allocation period» (the date 30th June 2026 has passed).

*Analytical inference:* an installation that used the exit route before that closing date becomes a full permit holder from 1st January 2027, which could change that installation's cost position; the source states no cost figure and does not say which installations used the route.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 5th February 2025: Order made
- 31st March 2025: Order comes into force
- 30th June 2025: last day for a renunciation notice for the 2026 allocation period (date passed)
- 1st January 2026: allocation table for the 2026 allocation period published before this date (date passed)
- 30th June 2026: operators notify the regulator as part of the second stage of the free allocation application (date passed)
- 1st January 2027: operators leaving ultra-small emitter status apply for a permit and comply with it from this date; the 2027-2030 allocation table date is set to this date

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/787, an act of the European Commission that changes how greenhouse gas emission allowances are auctioned, including for the separate emissions trading system for fuels used in road transport. Its jurisdiction is the European Union. Title: «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2026/787 of 8 April 2026 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2830 as regards rules on the timing, administration and other aspects of auctioning of greenhouse gas emission allowances» Dated: «Done at Brussels, 8 April 2026.»

The Regulation addresses auction platforms, Member States and bidders and does not name freight forwarders, carriers or shippers. Lines marked *Analytical inference:* are this document's reading of the quoted text beside them, and lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* are questions for counsel. The captured text states no review date.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets rules for the auctions through which allowances for a new carbon pricing system are sold. The system: «Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC provides for a separate emissions trading system for fuels used for combustion in buildings, road transport and additional sectors» Purpose: «To ensure a smooth start of the separate emissions trading system, several provisions on the timing and administration of the auctions for these allowances should be amended and clarified» Start: «auctioning for allowances covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC should start as from 2027» Why the early start matters: «The good functioning of the market for allowances covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC will depend on ensuring adequate liquidity early on so that a clear and predictable price signal for market participants is provided from the start»

Start dates of the Regulation itself: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» Urgency: «this Regulation should enter into force urgently» Reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

Who it touches: auction platforms, Member States that appoint auctioneers, bidders and the entities that must surrender allowances. The text names no transport mode, route or freight service.

*Analytical inference:* because road transport fuels are inside the separate system and its auctions start as from 2027, a road freight operator meets this Regulation through the cost of fuel allowances in a supplier's price, not through a duty of its own; the text states no such price.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in this Regulation falls to a freight operator within thirty days of the date of this document; the date that matters is 1 January 2027, when the first year of auctioning for the separate system begins. Two steps a freight desk can start now:

- A pricing lead asks each road fuel supplier or fuel card provider, before the next road rate round, whether it will show a separate line for the cost of allowances in the separate emissions trading system and from what date.
- A contracts lead adds 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2028 to the fuel surcharge clauses of road contracts as the dates from which an allowance cost line could arise and the end of the first distribution period.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names these parties: the common auction platform and opt-out auction platforms, Member States and their auctioneers, bidders, persons bidding on behalf of others, competent national authorities, regulated entities, and the Commission. «Each Member State should appoint at least one auctioneer, who should be responsible for the auctioning of allowances on behalf of the appointing Member State» «The participation of bidders in auctions for allowances covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC is linked to the level of demand from regulated entities to surrender allowances in order to meet their compliance obligations»

The Regulation names no forwarder, carrier or shipper and does not define who a regulated entity is.

*Analytical inference:* regulated entities create the demand for allowances, so fuel costs in road transport reach a freight operator only if a regulated entity passes its allowance cost on, which the text does not say.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that buys, stores or supplies fuel falls within regulated entities for emissions reported under Chapter IVa, which this text does not define.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation names several adjustment points. Recital 8 recalls a date in the act this Regulation amends, Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2830: «the common auction platform shall publish the 2027 auction calendar for allowances covered by Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC by 31 July 2026 or as soon as practicable thereafter, after having consulted the Commission» That date is past; the text does not say whether the calendar was published. The Regulation states no allowance price and no date on which a price will first form.

Later adjustments: «Once the legislation referred to in the first subparagraph has been implemented, the volume of allowances referred to in the first subparagraph which was withheld for the period between the year from when emissions are subject to such legislation and the date of application of that legislation shall be added to the auction calendars» *Analytical inference:* where a Member State's legislation is late, its allowances are withheld and then added back, so the supply of allowances in the early years can differ between Member States.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: who must hold and surrender allowances? The Regulation ties auction demand to national laws on surrender and on penalties: «Member State does not yet have national laws in place on the surrendering of allowances by regulated entities under Article 30e(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC and on penalties for excess emissions under Article 16(1) to (4) of that Directive for emissions reported under Chapter IVa of Directive 2003/87/EC»

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business is a regulated entity or only buys fuel from one, which depends on the Directive and on each Member State's law, not on this text.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

The Regulation changes auction rules and binds platforms, Member States and bidders. Where the text is silent on an effect for freight, this section says so.

Auction days: «Where the common auction platform conducts auctions of the allowances referred to in Articles 10 and 11 in one or two days a week, no opt-out auction platform shall conduct an auction on those days» First year: «By way of derogation from the second subparagraph, the volume of allowances referred to in Article 13 to be auctioned for the first year of auctioning in accordance with Article 30d(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC, shall be distributed in the period from 1 January 2027 up to 31 December 2028» Initial volume: «The initial volume of allowances to be auctioned from 1 January 2027 up to 31 December 2028 pursuant to Article 30d(3) and (4) of Directive 2003/87/EC shall be 450 000 000 allowances» Adjustment: «the revenue already obtained, the average auction clearing price for the six preceding calendar months, and the time remaining until 31 December 2032 shall be taken into account» Member State supply: «The volume of allowances to be auctioned on behalf of a Member State pursuant to paragraph 2 of this Article shall only be auctioned once that Member State has implemented national legislation on the obligation of regulated entities to surrender the amount of allowances set out in Article 30e(2) of Directive 2003/87/EC and on the penalties for excess emissions under Article 16(1) to (4) of Directive 2003/87/EC» Bidders: «The persons referred to in paragraph 1 shall fulfil the following conditions: (a) they are of sufficiently good repute and sufficiently experienced as to ensure proper respect of the conduct rules provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3» Auctioneers: «Each Member State shall appoint at least one auctioneer. No Member State shall auction allowances without appointing an auctioneer.»

What this changes: allowance supply in the first two years is set, and a Member State's allowances reach the market only when its surrender and penalty laws are in place. Effect by cargo vertical: not stated.

The Regulation states no pass-through of the allowance cost to fuel prices, road haulage rates or any freight charge.

*Analytical inference:* the supply rules decide how many allowances are offered and when, which feeds the price that regulated entities face; the text states no price and no link from that price to a freight rate.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* in which Member States the surrender and penalty laws are in place, since a Member State's allowances are auctioned only once they are.

No scope limits are stated in Article 2.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting and registration rules sit with bidders, auctioneers and authorities. «it is appropriate to remove the requirement to obtain an authorisation from competent national authorities for persons to be able to bid on behalf of others under the EU ETS framework» The Regulation states no registration or reporting duty for a freight business.

Enforcement: «to prohibit the persons referred to in paragraph 1 from bidding on behalf of clients where those persons have seriously and systematically breached their obligations»

Penalties: «its competent national authorities have at their disposal investigative powers and sanctions that are effective, proportionate and dissuasive» *Analytical inference:* sanctions here are set by Member States for bidders and for breaches of the conduct rules, not for freight activity.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text sets no build task for freight businesses. A pricing lead keeps a blank line for a fuel allowance cost on road quotes that run past 1 January 2027, filled only when a customer's fuel supplier states a charge, because this text states none.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

One carve-out and one derogation bear on the dates above. «persons covered by the exemption in Article 2(1), point (j), of Directive 2014/65/EU shall be eligible to apply for admission to bid directly in the auctions either on their own account or on behalf of clients of their main business» The first year is also treated differently from later years: the volume for the first year of auctioning is spread over a two-year period (see section 8).

- 8 April 2026: Regulation dated. «Done at Brussels, 8 April 2026.»
- 1 January 2027: first-year volume starts to be distributed. «in the period from 1 January 2027 up to 31 December 2028»
- 31 December 2028: end of the initial period for the first-year and initial volumes. «from 1 January 2027 up to 31 December 2028»

What changes for a freight desk on these dates: nothing directly. *Analytical inference:* 1 January 2027 is the date from which allowances for road transport fuels are offered, so it is the earliest date from which a fuel supplier could carry an allowance cost.

This document covers Regulation (EU) 2024/573 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 7 February 2024 on fluorinated greenhouse gases (F-gases), the gases used in refrigeration, air conditioning, heat pumps, insulation and electrical equipment. It repeals Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 and applies in the European Union. For freight it matters in three places: refrigeration units on trucks, trailers, reefers and train wagons, the import and export of the gases and of equipment that contains them, and the customs declaration that carries them.

How to read it: statements of what the regulation says are quoted from its own text; lines marked *Analytical inference:* are the author's reading and name the quoted fact they rest on; lines marked *Legal Confirmation Required:* name a question for counsel and are not settled here.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation is the Union's rulebook for F-gases. In its own words it «lays down rules on containment, use, recovery, recycling, reclamation and destruction of fluorinated greenhouse gases and on related ancillary measures», and it «imposes conditions on the production, import, export, placing on the market, subsequent supply and use of fluorinated greenhouse gases, and of specific products and equipment containing fluorinated greenhouse gases or whose functioning relies upon those gases». «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

For a freight operator the recital explains why transport is named: «Refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment contained in a means of transport have particularly high leakage rates due to the vibrations that occur during transport.» The same recitals say that operators of refrigeration and air conditioning equipment on ships should take precautions against leakage. The quoted scope covers the gases and the equipment that contains them, so the duties in this document fall in three places: leak checks and recovery on the listed mobile refrigeration units (section 7), a licence and a registration for imports and exports, and customs declaration data (section 10).

The regulation sets no freight rate or surcharge, and the captured text states no cost to an operator. *Analytical inference:* an operator that runs the listed mobile units or files declarations for covered goods carries the work in section 8, the records and the border permits, which rests on the quoted duties in sections 7, 8 and 10; what that work costs is not stated.

*Analytical inference:* because the quoted recital ties high leakage to vibration in a means of transport, the leak check and recovery duties for mobile equipment in section 7 are aimed at the operator of the unit; the regulation does not say how the cost of that work reaches a client's rate.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the delay for leak checks and recovery on refrigeration units of refrigerated light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers (including reefers) and train wagons ends on 12 March 2027, about four months after the date of this document (section 8). The steps below follow from that date and from the customs rules.

- A cold-chain equipment lead, before 12 March 2027, lists every refrigerated light-duty vehicle, intermodal container including reefer, and train wagon unit that holds a covered gas, and books certified or training-attested technicians for its first leak check and its recovery work, because the leak check and recovery duties reach those units from that date.
- A customs-systems lead, before the next import of a covered gas or of equipment that contains one, confirms that the declaration carries the F-gas Portal registration identification number, the net mass, the commodity code and the tonnes of CO 2 equivalent, because section 10 quotes that list for the customs declaration.
- An export desk lead, before the next export of stationary refrigeration or air-conditioning equipment, checks the equipment against Annex IV and the quoted GWP limit, because export of listed equipment with a GWP of 1 000 or more has been prohibited since 12 March 2025 (section 8).

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The regulation names these parties. Operators and manufacturers of equipment with a covered charge: «Operators and manufacturers of equipment that contains 5 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent or more of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I or 1 kilogram or more of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Section 1 of Annex II that is not contained in foams, shall ensure that the equipment is checked for leaks.» At the border, the regulation fixes who is the legal counterpart on the customs declaration: «For the purposes of release for free circulation, the undertaking holding quota or authorisations to use quota as required under this Regulation, and registered in the F-gas Portal pursuant to Article 20 shall be the importer indicated in the customs declaration.» «In the case of transit procedure, the undertaking holding quota or authorisations to use quota as required under this Regulation shall be the holder of the procedure.» «For the purposes of exports, the undertaking registered in the F-gas Portal pursuant to Article 20 shall be the exporter indicated in the customs declaration.» An importer with no establishment in the Union needs a local representative: «An importer of products or equipment referred to in paragraph 1, which has no establishment in the Union, shall appoint an only representative with an establishment within the Union that assumes the full responsibility of complying with this Regulation.»

It also names undertakings, producers, certified natural persons, independent auditors, customs authorities and market surveillance authorities. The regulation names no freight forwarder, carrier or customs broker as such.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted customs sentences put the duty on the importer or declarant named in the customs declaration, so a business that files the declaration for a client can be the party the customs authority looks to; whether it is the importer or only the declarant depends on how the declaration is made. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator that files import or export declarations, holds a transit procedure, or runs refrigerated units for others is an operator, importer, declarant, exporter or holder of the procedure under the quoted sentences, and which duty then follows.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text holds no published guidance document beyond the regulation; the Commission's acts that will follow are listed as events in section 6.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The regulation sets acts and reports that will change the analysis. Dates are quoted from the text; the first two below fall before the date of this document and are stated as past: the captured text does not say whether each was delivered.

- Certification and training minimums (date passed): «By 12 March 2026, the Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, establish the minimum requirements for certification programmes and training attestations referred to in paragraphs 3 and 4 for the activities referred to in paragraph 1.»
- Reference values for hydrofluorocarbon quota (date passed, then at least every 3 years): «By 31 October 2024 and at least every 3 years thereafter, the Commission shall determine reference values for producers and importers in accordance with Annex VII for the placing on the market of hydrofluorocarbons.»
- Alternatives for mobile refrigeration (date ahead): «By 1 July 2027, the Commission shall publish a report assessing whether cost-effective, technically feasible, energy-efficient and reliable alternatives exist, which make the replacement of fluorinated greenhouse gases possible in mobile refrigeration and mobile air-conditioning equipment, and where appropriate, put forward a legislative proposal to the European Parliament and to the Council to amend the list set out in Annex IV.»
- Health sector and battery cooling report (date ahead): «By 1 July 2028, the Commission shall publish a report assessing the impact of this Regulation on the health sector, particularly the availability of metered dose inhalers for the delivery of pharmaceutical ingredients, as well as the impact on the market of cooling equipment used in conjunction with batteries.»
- Report on the effects of the regulation (date ahead): «By 1 January 2030, the Commission shall publish a report on the effects of this Regulation.»
- Ships: the recital says «When reviewing the implementation of this Regulation, the Commission should assess the feasibility of extending the scope of containment measures to ships.»

What changes when these arrive: the 1 July 2027 report, and any legislative proposal it carries, bears on whether the list of banned products in Annex IV is amended for mobile refrigeration and mobile air conditioning, which are the units on trucks, trailers, reefers and wagons; the certification acts fix what a technician needs for the work in section 8. *Analytical inference:* the 2027 report rests on the quoted question of whether alternatives exist, so the captured text states a possible change to the Annex IV list and no adopted one.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Threshold question: which transport equipment is covered by the leak check duty? The regulation lists it. «Paragraph 1 shall apply to operators and manufacturers of the following mobile equipment that contains fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I or in Section 1 of Annex II: (a) refrigeration units of refrigerated trucks and refrigerated trailers; (b) refrigeration units of refrigerated light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers, including reefers, and train wagons; (c) air-conditioning equipment and heat pumps in heavy duty vehicles, vans, non-road mobile machinery used in agriculture, mining and construction operations, trains, metros, trams and aircraft.» The charge threshold in section 4 also applies.

*Analytical inference:* the quoted list names refrigerated trucks and trailers, refrigerated light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers including reefers, and train wagons, and the air-conditioning of heavy duty vehicles, vans and aircraft, so a freight operator's reefer fleet and refrigerated road fleet fall in the list; whether a given unit holds a covered charge depends on the gas it contains. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given unit is "mobile equipment" under the quoted list and whether its charge crosses the quoted threshold.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the duties below apply to operators, manufacturers, importers and exporters as the quoted articles describe them; whether and how each applies to a given operator and unit is a question for counsel and is not settled here.

**Scope.** «This Regulation applies to: (a) the fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annexes I, II and III, whether alone or as mixtures; and (b) products and equipment, and parts thereof, containing fluorinated greenhouse gases or whose functioning relies upon those gases.»

**Leak checks.** Operators and manufacturers of equipment above the charge threshold must have it checked, as quoted in section 4.

**Equipment that is not checked.** «Hermetically sealed equipment shall not be checked for leaks provided that it is labelled as hermetically sealed equipment and that it complies with one of the following conditions: (a) it contains less than 10 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I; or (b) it contains less than 2 kilograms of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Section 1 of Annex II.»

**Who checks.** «As regards the equipment referred to in paragraph 2, points (a) to (e), and points (a) and (b) of this paragraph, the checks shall be carried out by natural persons certified in accordance with Article 10.» Recovery from some mobile units has a lower bar: the recovery article says that for the mobile equipment of its paragraph 3, points (b) and (c), «only natural persons holding at least a training attestation in accordance with Article 10(1), second subparagraph, of this Regulation, shall be considered to be appropriately qualified». *Analytical inference:* the two quotes rest on different activities, so leak checks on refrigeration units of refrigerated trucks and trailers, light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers and train wagons need certified persons, while recovery from the light-duty vehicle, intermodal container and train wagon units needs at least a training attestation.

**How often.** «(a) for equipment that contains less than 50 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I or less than 10 kilograms of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Section 1 of Annex II: at least every 12 months; or where a leakage detection system is installed in such equipment, at least every 24 months;» For the largest charges: «(c) for equipment that contains 500 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent or more of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I or 100 kilograms or more of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Section 1 of Annex II: at least every 3 months or, where a leakage detection system is installed in such equipment, at least every 6 months.»

**The delay for some mobile equipment.** «Paragraphs 1 and 6 shall not apply to operators of mobile equipment under paragraph 3, points (b) and (c), until 12 March 2027.»

**Recovery at decommissioning.** «Operators of equipment that contain fluorinated greenhouse gases, not contained in foams, shall ensure that those substances are recovered and, after the decommissioning of the equipment, they are recycled, reclaimed or destroyed.» It applies to mobile units: «The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 shall apply to operators of any of the following mobile equipment: (a) the cooling circuits of refrigeration units of refrigerated trucks and refrigerated trailers; (b) the cooling circuits of refrigeration units of refrigerated light-duty vehicles and intermodal containers, including reefers, and train wagons;» For some of them: «The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 shall apply to operators of the mobile equipment under paragraph 3, points (b) and (c), from 12 March 2027.»

**Records.** «Operators of equipment which is required to be checked for leaks pursuant to Article 5(1) shall establish and keep records for each piece of such equipment» «the operators referred to in paragraph 1 shall keep the records referred to in that paragraph for at least 5 years»

**Servicing bans on high-GWP gases.** «From 1 January 2025, the use of fluorinated greenhouse gases, with a global warming potential of 2 500 or more, for the maintenance or servicing of any refrigeration equipment shall be prohibited.» «From 1 January 2026, the use of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I, with a global warming potential of 2 500 or more, for the maintenance or servicing of air-conditioning equipment and heat pumps shall be prohibited.» «From 1 January 2032, the use of fluorinated greenhouse gases listed in Annex I, with a global warming potential of 750 or more, for the maintenance or servicing of stationary refrigeration equipment, with the exclusion of chillers, shall be prohibited.» «From 1 January 2035, the use of SF 6 for the maintenance or servicing of electrical switchgear equipment shall be prohibited unless it is reclaimed or recycled»

**Import and export licence.** «The import and export of fluorinated greenhouse gases, and products and equipment containing those gases or whose functioning relies upon those gases shall be subject to the presentation of a valid licence to customs authorities issued by the Commission pursuant to Article 20(4) and (5), except in the case of temporary storage.» For export: «From 12 March 2025 the export of foams, technical aerosols, stationary refrigeration and stationary air-conditioning equipment and stationary heat pumps as referred to in Annex IV that contain, or whose functioning relies upon, fluorinated greenhouse gases with a GWP of 1 000 or more shall be prohibited.»

**Quota.** «The amount of reduction shall be calculated as 200 % of the amount by which the quota was exceeded.»

**Penalty.** Member States set penalties; the floor for the maximum is: «In the case of unlawful production, import, export, placing on the market or use of fluorinated greenhouse gases, or of products and equipment containing those gases or whose functioning relies upon those gases, the maximum amount of the administrative financial penalty shall be at least five times the market value of the gases or products and equipment concerned. Where such infringements are repeated within a five-year period, the maximum amount of the administrative financial penalty shall be at least eight times the market value of the gases or products and equipment concerned.»

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the captured text does not address a product sold by a freight operator under its own name.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Registration and reporting are mostly about the gases and the border.

- Registration in the F-gas Portal: «Undertakings shall have a valid registration in the F-gas Portal prior to carrying out any of the following activities: (a) the import or export of fluorinated greenhouse gases, and products and equipment containing fluorinated greenhouse gases, except in the case of temporary storage as defined in Article 5, point (17), of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013;» «A valid registration in the F-Gas Portal at the moment of import or export constitutes a licence required under Article 22.»
- Customs declaration data: for imports the importer or declarant provides, where relevant, «(a) F-gas Portal registration identification number; (b) Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number; (c) net mass of bulk gases and of gases contained in products and equipment, and in parts thereof; (d) commodity code under which the goods are classified; (e) tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of bulk gases and of gases contained in products or equipment, and in parts thereof.»
- Documents at customs: «The declaration of conformity and the documentation referred to in Article 19(2) shall be made available to customs authorities at the time when the customs declaration related to the release for free circulation is submitted.»
- Pre-charged equipment: «Refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment, heat pumps and metered dose inhalers pre-charged with substances listed in Section 1 of Annex I shall not be placed on the market unless those substances with which the products or equipment have been pre-charged are accounted for within the quota system referred to in this Chapter.» Importers confirm by audit: «importers of those products or equipment shall ensure that, by 30 April 2025 and every year thereafter, the accuracy of the documentation, the declaration of conformity and the veracity of their report pursuant to Article 26(7) is confirmed, for the preceding calendar year, at a reasonable level of assurance by an independent auditor registered in the F-gas Portal.»
- Reports: «By 31 March 2025 and every year thereafter, each producer, importer and exporter that produced, imported or exported hydrofluorocarbons or quantities exceeding one metric tonne or 100 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of other fluorinated greenhouse gases during the preceding calendar year shall report to the Commission the data specified in Annex IX on each of those substances for that calendar year.»

*Analytical inference:* the quoted customs list rests on the declaration at release for free circulation, so the data fields are a customs data task for the declarant. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight operator that is not itself the importer or exporter must hold an F-gas Portal registration to file a declaration for a client; the captured text names undertakings that carry out the quoted activities.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: the captured text sets record and certification duties that start on 12 March 2027 for part of the mobile fleet. The records are set by the quoted record article in section 8.

- A fleet-maintenance records lead, before 12 March 2027, sets up a record for each covered unit that holds the quantity and type of gas, the gas added with dates, the gas recovered, the identity and certificate number of the servicing undertaking, and the dates and results of leak checks, and sets a retention period of at least five years, because section 8 quotes that list and period.
- A training lead, before 12 March 2027, checks that each technician who will leak-check the reefer, intermodal, light-duty vehicle and wagon units is a certified person and that each technician who will recover gas from the intermodal, light-duty vehicle and wagon units holds at least a training attestation, because section 8 quotes those two different qualifications.

*Analytical inference:* the record steps rest on the quoted record and retention sentences; the captured text does not say how an operator keeps the records or whether a national database replaces them.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The regulation lets some earlier rules run on and carves out some cases. The old regulation: «Article 12 of Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 as applicable on 10 March 2024 shall continue to apply until 31 December 2024.» The older reporting rules: «Article 14(2), second subparagraph, and Article 19 of Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 as applicable on 10 March 2024 shall continue to apply with regard to the reporting period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023.» Small importers of pre-charged equipment: «This Article shall not apply to undertakings that placed on the market less than 10 tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of hydrofluorocarbons, per year, contained in the products or equipment referred to in paragraph 1.» Military and listed equipment on export: «The prohibition set out in the first subparagraph shall not apply to military equipment or to products and equipment that can be placed on the market in the Union in accordance with Annex IV.»

*Analytical inference:* the transitions rest on the quoted dates for the repealed regulation, so reporting for the earlier period follows the old rules; the carve-out for small importers rests on the quoted tonnage and is unrelated to the mobile equipment duties in section 7.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 7 February 2024: the regulation is adopted: «Done at Strasbourg, 7 February 2024.»
- Twentieth day after publication: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»
- 11 March 2024: the Commission's power to adopt delegated acts runs «shall be conferred on the Commission for an indeterminate period of time from 11 March 2024».
- 31 October 2024: the Commission determines reference values for hydrofluorocarbon quota (section 6).
- 31 December 2024: «By 31 December 2024 and every year thereafter, the Commission shall allocate quota for each producer and importer for placing on the market of hydrofluorocarbons, pursuant to Annex VIII.» The old regulation's Article 12 runs until then (section 12).
- 1 January 2025: «Article 12 and Article 17(5) shall apply from 1 January 2025.» Servicing with gases of GWP 2 500 or more in any refrigeration equipment is prohibited from this date (section 8).
- 3 March 2025: «Article 20(2), Article 20(3) and Article 23(5) shall apply from 3 March 2025 for release for free circulation referred to in Article 201 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013 and for all other import procedures and for export.»
- 31 March 2025 (passed): the first annual report to the Commission fell due (section 10); the captured text does not say whether each undertaking filed.
- 30 April 2025 (passed): the first annual audit confirmation for importers of pre-charged equipment fell due (section 10); the audit repeats each year.
- 1 January 2026: servicing of air-conditioning equipment and heat pumps with gases of GWP 2 500 or more is prohibited; «Before 1 January 2026, Member States shall notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures»
- 12 March 2026 (passed): the Commission's acts on certification and training fell due (section 6); the captured text does not say whether they were adopted.
- 12 March 2027: leak checks and recovery start for refrigerated light-duty vehicles, intermodal containers including reefers, and train wagons (section 8).
- 1 July 2027: the Commission's report on alternatives for mobile refrigeration is due (section 6).
- 31 December 2027: «Member States shall ensure that by 31 December 2027, the financing obligations for waste electrical and electronic equipment referred to in Articles 12 and 13 of Directive 2012/19/EU include the financing of the recovery»
- 1 January 2028: «From 1 January 2028, the quota for which a payment has not been made by the set deadline shall be cancelled.»
- 1 July 2028: the Commission's report on the health sector is due (section 6).
- 12 March 2029: «Member States shall ensure that natural persons who hold a certificate or training attestation under Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 shall participate in such refreshment training courses or complete such evaluation processes for the first time no later than 12 March 2029.»
- 1 January 2030: the Commission's report on the effects of the regulation is due (section 6).
- 1 January 2032: the ban on servicing stationary refrigeration with gases of GWP 750 or more starts (section 8).
- 1 January 2035: the ban on servicing switchgear with SF 6 unless reclaimed or recycled starts (section 8).

What each date changes: the 2024 dates start the quota and delegated powers; the 2025 dates start the customs interconnection, the first reports and audits, and the first servicing ban; the 2026 date adds the air-conditioning servicing ban and the Member State penalty notification; the March 2027 date brings the mobile fleet under leak checks and recovery; 1 July 2027, 1 July 2028 and 1 January 2030 are Commission reports that can lead to proposals; 31 December 2027 is the date by which Member States are to make the producer-responsibility financing for waste electrical equipment cover recovery of the gases, which decides who pays for end-of-life recovery from covered electrical equipment (an inference on the quoted sentence, no payer is stated); 1 January 2028 cancels quota not paid for by the set deadline, so a gas importer holding unpaid quota loses it; 12 March 2029 is the last date for technicians certified under the old regulation to complete refresher training, so a technician an operator relies on needs that training by then; the 2032 and 2035 dates are later servicing bans.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2023/2055 of 25 September 2023 amending Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) as regards synthetic polymer microparticles», the European Union restriction on microplastics added to the chemicals law known as REACH. Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation adds entry 78 to Annex XVII of REACH and bans the sale of tiny plastic particles. It gives its reason: «They accumulate in the environment and contribute to microplastic pollution.» It defines the particles: «Synthetic polymer microparticles: polymers that are solid and which fulfil both of the following conditions: (a) are contained in particles and constitute at least 1 % by weight of those particles; or build a continuous surface coating on particles; (b) at least 1 % by weight of the particles referred to in point (a) fulfil either of the following conditions: (i) all dimensions of the particles are equal to or less than 5 mm; (ii) the length of the particles is equal to or less than 15 mm and their length to diameter ratio is greater than 3.» The ban reads: «Shall not be placed on the market as substances on their own or, where the synthetic polymer microparticles are present to confer a sought-after characteristic, in mixtures in a concentration equal to or greater than 0,01 % by weight.» This Regulation enters into force as the text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* the duties fall on suppliers, manufacturers, importers and industrial users of the particles and the products that contain them. A freight business meets the Regulation as the carrier of those goods and, where it places goods on the market itself, as an importer. The text names no freight role, but it mentions releases «during transportation». The cargo it touches includes plastic feedstock, cosmetics, detergents, agricultural products and sports-surface infill, all named in the text.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step in the staged ban is «from 17 October 2027 for “rinse-off products”», and the annual reports to the European Chemicals Agency already run for feedstock users.

- A compliance lead lists the pellet, flake and powder, cosmetic, detergent, agricultural and sports-surface infill consignments the business handles and, at the next booking from each shipper, asks whether the supplier information required by the text goes with the goods: «The text or pictograms shall be placed on the label, the packaging, or the package leaflet of the products containing synthetic polymer microparticles or, regarding the information in paragraph 7, on the safety data sheet.»
- A customer-facing lead asks each pellet or powder client, before its next annual report, whether it needs transport loss figures from the business, because the report must include «the quantity of synthetic polymer microparticles released to the environment during transportation».

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the label and report rules above; the Regulation requires neither of a carrier. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that imports or ships the goods counts as a supplier or importer under entry 78.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names manufacturers, importers, suppliers, industrial downstream users, the European Chemicals Agency and the competent authorities. On request they must provide identity information: «Manufacturers, importers and industrial downstream users of products containing synthetic polymer microparticles shall provide specific information on the identity of polymers covered by this entry contained in those products». The timing: «If the information is not available to industrial downstream users, they shall request it from their supplier within 7 days from the receipt of the request from the competent authorities»; «the suppliers shall provide the requested information within 30 days to the industrial downstream user or directly to the competent authority requesting it».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is not named. It would be an importer only if it places the goods on the market. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which role a forwarder or carrier holds for goods it imports or ships for a client, and whether a client may pass on the information request.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The recitals foresee reviews without dates. On tests: «it may be necessary to review the standardised test methods and pass criteria to demonstrate degradability or solubility». On the definition: «the Forum recommended a review of the definition after the entry into force of the restriction to reflect the latest scientific and technological developments».

*Analytical inference:* a review could change the test methods or the definition in section 7. The text states no date and no body for either review.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a product is caught is whether it holds synthetic polymer microparticles. The size test: «(i) all dimensions of the particles are equal to or less than 5 mm; (ii) the length of the particles is equal to or less than 15 mm and their length to diameter ratio is greater than 3.». Some polymers are excluded: «The following polymers are excluded from this designation: (a) polymers that are the result of a polymerisation process that has taken place in nature, independently of the process through which they have been extracted, which are not chemically modified substances; (b) polymers that are degradable as proved in accordance with Appendix 15; (c) polymers that have a solubility greater than 2 g/L as proved in accordance with Appendix 16; (d) polymers that do not contain carbon atoms in their chemical structure.».

*Analytical inference:* a pellet, powder or filler shipment is caught only if the polymer meets the definition and no exclusion applies. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular polymer shipped by a client is a synthetic polymer microparticle under entry 78.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Sales ban and exceptions. The ban in paragraph 1 does not apply to every use: «Paragraph 1 shall not apply to the placing on the market of: (a) synthetic polymer microparticles, as substances on their own or in mixtures, for use at industrial sites; (b) medicinal products within the scope of Directive 2001/83/EC».

Staged dates. «Paragraph 1 shall apply as follows regarding the following uses: (a) from 17 October 2029 to synthetic polymer microparticles for use in the encapsulation of fragrances; (b) from 17 October 2027 for “rinse-off products”», and «(e) from 17 October 2028 for detergents, as defined in Article 2(1) of Regulation (EC) No 648/2004, waxes, polishes and air care products» The last of the staged dates: «(j) from 17 October 2031 for granular infill for use on synthetic sports surfaces.»

Supplier information. «From 17 October 2025 suppliers of synthetic polymer microparticles referred to in paragraph 4, point (a), shall provide the following information: (a) instructions for use and disposal explaining to industrial downstream users how to prevent releases of synthetic polymer microparticles to the environment; (b) the following statement: “The synthetic polymer microparticles supplied is subject to conditions laid down by entry 78 of Annex XVII». For products: «From 17 October 2026 suppliers of products containing synthetic polymer microparticles referred to in paragraph 4, point (e), and from 17 October 2025 suppliers of products containing synthetic polymer microparticles referred to in paragraph 4, point (d), and paragraph 5, shall provide instructions for use and disposal» A microplastics statement applies later: «From 17 October 2031 until 16 October 2035 suppliers of products referred to in paragraph 6, point (c), containing synthetic polymer microparticles shall provide the following statement: “This product contains microplastics.” However, products placed on the market before 17 October 2031 are not required to bear that statement until 17 December 2031.»

Annual reports. «Starting from 2026 manufacturers and industrial downstream users of synthetic polymer microparticles in the form of pellets, flakes, and powders used as feedstock in plastic manufacturing at industrial sites, and, starting from 2027, other manufacturers of synthetic polymer microparticles and other industrial downstream users using synthetic polymer microparticles at industrial sites shall submit the following information to the Agency by 31 May of each year». The year-only start for other manufacturers and users, the text's «starting from 2027, other manufacturers of synthetic polymer microparticles and other industrial downstream users», is read here as the year beginning 1 January 2027.

Old stock. «Paragraph 1 shall not apply to placing on the market of synthetic polymers microparticles, on their own or in mixtures, placed on the market before 17 October 2023.»

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the restriction sets duties for suppliers and users of the listed products, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Suppliers of products report to the European Chemicals Agency each year: «From 2027, suppliers of products containing synthetic polymer microparticles referred to in paragraphs 4, points (b), (d) and (e), and paragraph 5, placed on the market for the first time to professional users and the general public, shall submit the following information to the Agency by 31 May of each year». The report content includes «an estimate of the quantity of synthetic polymer microparticles released to the environment in the previous calendar year, which shall include also the quantity of synthetic polymer microparticles released to the environment during transportation». The Agency passes the data on: «The Agency shall make the information submitted under paragraphs 11 and 12 available to the Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* these reports go from suppliers and users to the Agency; the text states no filing by a carrier.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the text puts the labelling and data work on suppliers. Languages: «they shall be in the official languages of the Member States where the substance or mixture is placed on the market, unless the Member States concerned provide otherwise». A digital route is allowed: «suppliers may provide a digital tool that gives access to an electronic version of that information». On request a supplier or user must prove a polymer is excluded: «shall provide, without delay, information proving that those polymers are degradable in accordance with Appendix 15 or soluble in accordance with Appendix 16, as applicable, to competent authorities upon their request».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business that handles these goods sees the effect as labels, safety data sheets and a client request for transport loss figures. The text states no loss-reporting method for carriers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a carrier must supply transport release figures to a client.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The ban has exceptions for contained or locked-in particles: «synthetic polymer microparticles which are contained by technical means so that releases to the environment are prevented when used in accordance with the instructions for use during the intended end use» and «synthetic polymer microparticles which are permanently incorporated into a solid matrix during intended end use». The recitals tie the staged dates to enforcement readiness: «Such transitional periods are also necessary for the Member States to prepare for the enforcement of the restriction.»

*Analytical inference:* goods that fit an exception still carry paragraph 6 dates and information duties only where the text says so; the exception wording decides, not the product label.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1252 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 April 2024 establishing a framework for ensuring a secure and sustainable supply of critical raw materials», the Union framework for the supply of critical raw materials. Where it applies: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its stated aim: «The general objective of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market by establishing a framework to ensure the Union’s access to a secure, resilient and sustainable supply of critical raw materials». Its dated steps run for years ahead (section 14). *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of its duties fall on a given forwarder, shipper or consignee is a question for counsel; the text names no forwarder.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The regulation reaches cargo in two ways. It lists the raw materials the Union treats as strategic, among them «(d) cobalt (e) copper (f) gallium (g) germanium» and «(n) rare earth elements for permanent magnets (Nd, Pr, Tb, Dy, Gd, Sm, and Ce)», and it sets duties for the finished products that carry magnets (section 8). It also lets the Commission back extraction and processing projects: «the Commission shall recognise as Strategic Projects raw material projects that meet the following criteria». In force: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* resting on the Annex I list above and the product list in section 8, the regulation’s subject matter includes the listed materials and the products named in Article 28(1), such as motor vehicles, electric motors and heat pumps, and both are goods that move as cargo. Whether a given consignment triggers a duty depends on who first makes the goods available in the Union (section 4).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

COMPETITIVE EDGE: the text puts no duty on a forwarder as such (section 4); the product duties fall on those placing goods on the market and start two years after the Commission's labelling act enters into force, so the edge is being ready to ask shippers for the right data first.

- A documentation lead adds to the cargo-intake form this month a field asking whether goods are among the products in Article 28(1) and whether they incorporate permanent magnets.
- A sales lead raises with shippers of those products, at the next client review, that the labelling format is due on 24 November 2026 and asks which product models they will have to label.
- A contract lead adds to the next shipper agreement a clause under which the shipper supplies the magnet label and data carrier details with the shipping documents.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the data carrier and customs access sentences quoted in sections 4 and 8, customs authorities are among the readers of the product data, so a forwarder that has the identifier and data carrier details to hand is placed to support a customs query; the text itself asks nothing of forwarders here.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text addresses Member States, the Commission, large companies that Member States identify, operators of extractive waste facilities, scheme owners, project promoters and those who place magnet-bearing products on the market. Definitions: «‘placing on the market’ means the first making available of a product on the Union market»; «‘large company’ means a company with more than 500 employees on average and a net worldwide turnover of more than EUR 150 million in the most recent financial year». Customs authorities are readers of product data: «The information referred to in paragraph 4 shall be accessible to repairers, recyclers, market surveillance authorities and customs authorities.» No freight forwarder, carrier or transport operator is named as a duty holder.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that moves, stores or clears goods for a shipper is ever the person who places them on the market, for example where it is the party first making them available in the Union, is for counsel; the text does not say.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis
