## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

All issued by the Commission:

- Labelling format: «By 24 November 2026, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act establishing the format for the labelling referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article.» Product duties in Article 28 start two years after that act enters into force (section 8), so shippers need the format before they can label.
- Customs: the Commission has the power to list codes for the products («The Commission is empowered to adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 38 to supplement this Regulation by providing a list of Combined Nomenclature codes») and to adopt delegated acts that «establish requirements related to customs controls related to the data carrier and unique product identifier referred to in Article 28(3) and (4)». The text sets no date for either.
- Recycled-content rules: «By 24 May 2026, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 38 to supplement this Regulation by establishing rules for the calculation and verification of the share of neodymium» That date has passed and the text does not say whether the act was adopted, so the disclosure date in section 8 cannot be fixed from this text.
- Recycling benchmarks: «By 1 January 2027, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 38 to supplement this Regulation by providing for Union recycling capacity benchmarks»
- Footprint report: «The Commission shall by 24 November 2026 submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council setting out which critical raw materials are to be prioritised» A later footprint declaration duty depends on that report.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* once adopted, whether each act changes a forwarder's data or customs-document duties is for counsel.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the text sets no threshold question beyond the definitions in section 4.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Product label and data carrier (Article 28)

Cause: «From two years after the date of entry into force of the implementing act referred to in paragraph 2, any natural or legal person that places on the market magnetic resonance imaging devices, wind energy generators, industrial robots, motor vehicles, light means of transport, cooling generators, heat pumps, electric motors» must label products for permanent magnets, and «shall ensure that a data carrier is present on or in the product» linked to a unique product identifier. The information «remains available for a period at least equal to the product’s typical lifetime plus 10 years». Exemption: «Products primarily designed for defence or space applications shall be exempt from the requirements laid down in this Article.» Later start: «From 24 May 2029, this Article shall apply to magnetic resonance imaging devices, motor vehicles and light means of transport that are type-approved vehicles of category L.»

*Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a magnet-bearing product in the listed groups carries its label and identifier from the point it is first made available in the Union, so the details have to exist before the goods ship, not after arrival.

### Recycled content disclosure (Article 29)

Cause: the disclosure date is «By 24 May 2027 or two years from the entry into force of the delegated act referred to in paragraph 2, whichever is later»; the duty falls on those placing the products on the market «for which the total weight of all such permanent magnets exceeds 0,2 kg shall make publicly available on a free-access website the share of neodymium, dysprosium, praseodymium, terbium, boron, samarium, nickel and cobalt recovered from post-consumer waste». *Analytical inference:* resting on that sentence, the recovered share is published per product on a public website, so a consignee can read it without asking the forwarder.

### Conformity before market entry (Article 33)

Cause: «Before placing a product covered by Article 28 or 29 on the market, the natural or legal persons responsible shall ensure that the applicable conformity assessment procedure has been carried out». *Analytical inference:* resting on that sentence, conformity work sits with the person responsible before market entry; the text names no step for a forwarder.

### Company risk assessment (Article 24)

Cause: «Large companies as referred to in paragraph 1 shall, at least every three years and to the extent the required information is available to them, carry out a risk assessment of their raw materials supply chain of strategic raw materials» *Analytical inference:* resting on that sentence, the duty sits with the company identified by a Member State, not with its logistics providers; the text names no information request to forwarders.

### Benchmarks (Article 5)

Cause: the Union sets aims for 2030 of extraction «at least 10 % of the Union’s annual consumption of strategic raw materials, to the extent possible in light of the Union’s reserves», processing «at least 40 % of the Union’s annual consumption of strategic raw materials» and recycling «at least 25 % of the Union’s annual consumption of strategic raw materials and is capable of recycling significantly increasing amounts of each strategic raw material from waste». Import aim: «diversify the Union’s imports of strategic raw materials with a view to ensuring that, by 2030, the Union’s annual consumption of each strategic raw material at any relevant stage of processing can rely on imports from several third countries» and that «no third country accounts for more than 65 % of the Union’s annual consumption of such a strategic raw material». The text states no change to any route, rate or surcharge.

### Footprint declaration (Article 31)

Cause: «the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 38 to supplement this Regulation to establish rules for the calculation and verification of the environmental footprint of different critical raw materials». Limit: «The footprint declaration shall be limited to those environmental impact categories.»

### Penalties (Article 47)

«By 24 November 2026, Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» The text states no penalty amount and names no enforcement body.

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any vertical or freight charge; the effect on a given vertical needs shipper-specific data.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the Article 28 and Article 33 sentences above, the first product-level checks come after the Commission acts, not on a fixed calendar date.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Article 28 and 29 duties reach a consignment held or cleared by a forwarder, and which Member State's penalty rules apply, are questions for counsel.

No phase-in is stated in Articles 5 and 24 beyond the dates above.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Duties fall on Member States, not forwarders. Deadline: «By 24 November 2026, Member States shall lay down rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation». Annual reporting: «By 24 May 2026 and annually thereafter, Member States shall submit a report to the Commission» Strategic stocks: «Member States shall, in their reports submitted pursuant to Article 45, submit to the Commission information on the state of their strategic stocks of strategic raw materials.» No registration scheme for forwarders is stated. *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a forwarder's own reporting exposure is not set by this text.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

COMPETITIVE EDGE: the text asks forwarders for no system build. A documentation lead adds fields for the unique product identifier and the data carrier reference to the shipment record, so the details can be quoted to a customs authority on request; this is a readiness step and not a duty in the text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any record-keeping duty reaches a forwarder is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

«Member States shall not, for reasons relating to information for recycling or recycled content of permanent magnets or for reasons relating to information on the environmental footprint of critical raw material covered by this Regulation, prohibit, restrict or impede the making available on the market» Also: «This Article shall not apply to products covered by type approval pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/858 or (EU) No 168/2013.» For vehicles: «This Article shall not apply to: (a) special purpose vehicles as defined in Article 3, point (31), of Regulation (EU) 2018/858», and the text lists vehicles produced in small series in the same exclusion.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

Entries dated before this document are past; the text states what was due, not whether it was done.

- 11 April 2024: adopted. «Done at Brussels, 11 April 2024.»
- 24 May 2025: Member States identify the large companies that use strategic raw materials to make the listed equipment; only those companies learn they are in scope. «By 24 May 2025 and within 12 months of each update of the list of strategic raw materials pursuant to Article 3(3), Member States shall identify the large companies operating on their territory that use strategic raw materials to manufacture batteries for energy storage and e-mobility»
- 24 May 2026: past; the basis for recycled-content disclosure was due. «By 24 May 2026, the Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 38»
- 24 November 2026: shippers can start planning labels, and national penalty regimes become knowable. «By 24 November 2026, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act establishing the format for the labelling»; «By 24 November 2026, Member States shall lay down rules on penalties»
- 1 January 2027: recycling capacity benchmarks due. «By 1 January 2027, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 38»
- 24 May 2027: the strategic list can change, which changes which materials are in scope. «The Commission shall review and, if necessary, update the list of strategic raw materials by 24 May 2027, and every three years thereafter.»
- 24 May 2028: evaluation due, and vehicle type-approval tables gain a magnet entry (Articles 40 and 41). «By 24 May 2028, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Regulation»; «Articles 40 and 41 shall apply from 24 may 2028.»; «Permanent magnet circularity requirements»
- 24 May 2029: label and data carrier duties reach vehicles and imaging devices. «From 24 May 2029, this Article shall apply to magnetic resonance imaging devices»
- 2030: the year by which the Union aims to reach the capacity and import-spread levels in section 8. «ensure that, by 2030, Union capacities for each strategic raw material have significantly increased»

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012», United Kingdom statutory instrument 2012 No. 1976, the rulebook for how climate change agreements are run. Date made: «Made 25th July 2012». Currency: the source page says the text «is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 03 September 2026». Territory: the consolidated text marks its provisions as UK provisions («Citation and commencement U.K. 1.») and holds no separate extent sentence. The document is written for a forwarder with no background in the scheme. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which facilities a forwarder or its customers operate within the scheme is a question for counsel; the text lists none.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Effective date: «These Regulations may be cited as the Climate Change Agreements (Administration) Regulations 2012 and come into force on 1st October 2012». Who runs it: «The Environment Agency (“the administrator”) is the body appointed as the administrator». Who is bound: «“operator” means a party to an underlying agreement other than the administrator».

*Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, the instrument is an administration rulebook between the Environment Agency and operators of facilities in climate change agreements; it prices missed targets and late or wrong information, and it sets no freight rule. A forwarder meets it only as operator of its own UK site or through customers that hold an agreement.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step is required of a forwarder with no site in a climate change agreement, and nothing in the text sets a freight charge.

- A UK site operations lead checks this month whether any facility the business runs is party to an agreement and, if one is, diarises 1st May 2027 for the first information return (section 10).
- A sales lead asks UK customers with agreements, at the next account review, whether a buy-out fee or a published penalty could change their warehousing or haulage volumes.

*Analytical inference:* resting on the penalty and publication sentences in section 8, the exposure the text prices is a missed or inaccurate return, and it falls on the operator.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The text names the administrator, the Secretary of State, sector associations and operators. The Secretary of State's duty: «The Secretary of State must operate an electronic system for the administration of agreements (“ the Register ”).» Sector association: «“sector association” means a party to an umbrella agreement other than the administrator». Because the list of covered facilities is public («the administrator must publish a list containing the name and address of each facility which is to be taken as being covered by an agreement»), a forwarder can see whether a customer's site is covered. No freight forwarder, carrier or logistics provider is named.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder is the operator of any covered facility, for example a site it runs for its own account, is for counsel; the text does not say.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Legal Confirmation Required:* what the 2026 instrument changes in regulation 12(3)(h) is for counsel once its text is read.

## 7. Threshold Questions

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### Buy-out fee (regulation 12)

Cause: «An underlying agreement must contain the terms set out in paragraph (2).» Scope: «This regulation applies to an umbrella agreement if it contains terms corresponding with the terms set out in regulation 12(2).» For a missed target the fee per tonne rises with the period: «A is £12 where the finding is of a failure to meet a target for target period 1 or target period 2»; «£14 ] where the finding is of a failure to meet a target for target period 3 or target period 4»; «£18 ] where the finding is of a failure to meet a target for target period 5»; and «£25 where the finding is of a failure to meet a target for target period 6». For later periods: «where the finding is of a failure to meet a target for target period 7, 8 or 9, A is the number of pounds sterling which is equal to the result of the application of the formula in paragraph (3) in respect of that target period». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a missed target is paid for per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent, at a rate that moved from £12 to £25 over periods 1 to 6, and from period 7 follows a formula rather than a fixed sum.

### Financial penalties (regulation 15)

Cause: «The administrator may impose a financial penalty on an operator if the operator, in relation to one or more of its facilities». Lower amounts: «where the administrator considers it appropriate, such lower amount as the administrator considers appropriate». General cap, where it applies: «This paragraph applies in respect of a penalty that may be imposed under paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d) on» operators; «(a) [ F71 £500 ] ; or (b) 0.1 × (X – Y)» Greenfield facility in its first 12 months: «This paragraph applies in respect of a penalty which may be imposed under paragraph (1)(a), (c) or (d) on the operator of a [ F75 facility which is ] a greenfield facility, if the penalty notice is served at any time during the 12 month period starting on the date of an underlying agreement»; a different formula, based on the administrator's estimate of levy, then applies. For inaccurate reported emissions the cap is set separately: «of the financial penalty that may be imposed under paragraph (1)(b) is the greater of» «(a) [ F81 £500 ]» or, for target periods 1 to 4, «£12 per tCO 2 equivalent of the difference between the actual emissions and the reported emissions for target period 1, target period 2, target period 3 or target period 4», with other amounts for later periods. Recovery: «A financial penalty under this regulation is recoverable by the administrator as a civil debt if unpaid after the date for payment set out in the notice of financial penalty.» Publication: «The information listed in paragraph (1) must be published for a period of at least one year.» *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a penalty is a published, collectable debt of the operator, with the cap depending on the kind of failure and the kind of site; the text does not tie any penalty to freight rates.

### Termination and appeal (regulations 17 to 21)

«The administrator may terminate an underlying agreement if the operator contravenes the agreement unless the contravention has given rise to the imposition of a financial penalty.» Not a contravention: «a failure to meet, or to make progress towards meeting, targets does not constitute a contravention of an agreement». Appeal: «Subject to paragraph (4), where the administrator terminates an agreement under regulation 17(3), 17(4), or 18», and «the operator may appeal to the First-tier Tribunal» against a penalty. *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, losing an agreement follows unpaid penalties or uncorrected breaches, not a missed target by itself.

Effect by cargo vertical: the text states no effect on any cargo vertical or transport mode; any effect needs customer-specific data.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any fee, penalty or termination term reaches a forwarder through a customer contract or a site it runs is for counsel.

Target periods 1 to 9 and their dates are in section 14.
Obligations surveyed: 0; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 21.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of 2026-11-01: the instrument concerns facilities and energy agreements, not products.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Information duties fall on the operator. Annual: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May 2027 and on or before 1st May in each subsequent year». Later years: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May 2028, and on or before 1st May 2030». After each period: «provide to the administrator on or before 1st May following the end of a target period such information as has been requested by the administrator». The administrator reports too: «Subject to paragraph (5), as soon as reasonably practicable after the end of each target period, the administrator must publish a report setting out energy efficiency improvements and emission reductions achieved under agreements for the target period», including «for each [ F24 facility ] , details of the emissions recorded in the Register and details of whether the target has been met». *Analytical inference:* resting on those sentences, a covered operator has a fixed calendar of returns, and the period report is to give each facility's recorded emissions and whether its target was met, subject to the exceptions in the same regulation, so a covered customer's result can become public.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the operator's returns include «such information relating to the application of the UK ETS to the facility as has been requested by the administrator», under terms where «the operator must, in respect of each of its facilities». A UK site operations lead, if a site is covered, adds the 1st May returns to the site compliance calendar and names the owner of the energy data. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether those terms bind a forwarder's own site is for counsel.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Appeal bar: «There is no right of appeal for a sector association or an operator where the administrator terminates an agreement after receiving a notification under regulation 17(2).» Transition for publication: «This regulation does not apply in relation to a financial penalty imposed before 31 st December 2023.» New sites: «“greenfield facility” means a facility which started to carry out the process by virtue of which it is a facility within the meaning of paragraph 50 of Schedule 6».

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a new warehouse site of a forwarder counts as a greenfield facility is for counsel.
